One of the more popular pages on my site is about
polygonal map generation
[1]
. Making those maps was a lot of work. I didn’t start there. I started with something
much
simpler, which I’ll describe here. The simpler technique can make maps like this in under 50 lines of code:
I’m not going to explain how to
draw
these maps; that’s going to depend on your language, graphics library, platform, etc. I’m only going to explain how to
fill an array
with height and biome map data.
Noise
#
A common way to generate 2D maps is to use a bandwidth-limited noise function, such as Simplex or Perlin noise, as a building block. This is what the noise function looks like:
We assign each location on the map a number from 0.0 to 1.0. In this image, 0.0 is black and 1.0 is white. Here’s how to set the color at each grid location in C-like syntax:
for (int y = 0; y < height; y++) {
for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) {
double nx = x/width - 0.5, ny = y/height - 0.5;
value[y][x] = noise(nx, ny);
}
}
The loop will work the same in Javascript, Python, Haxe, C++, C#, Java, and most other popular languages, so I’ll show it in C-like syntax and you can convert it to the language you’re using. In the rest of the tutorial, I’ll show how the loop body (the
value[y][x]=…
line) changes as we add more features. At
the end
, I’ll show a complete example.
Depending on the library you use, you may have to shift or multiply the values you get back to fit into the 0.0 to 1.0 range. Some libraries return 0.0 to 1.0; some return -1.0 to +1.0; some return other ranges like -0.7 to +0.7. Some don’t say what they return, so you may have to look at the return values to figure out the range.
Elevation
#
Noise by itself is just a bunch of numbers. We need to assign
meaning
to it. The first thing we might think of is to make the noise correspond to elevation (also called a “height map”). Let’s take the noise from earlier and draw it as elevation:
The code is almost the same, except for what’s inside the inner loop; it now looks like this:
elevation
[y][x] = noise(nx, ny);
Yes, that’s it. The map data is the same, but now I call it
elevation
instead of
value
.
Lots of hills, but not much else. What’s wrong?
Frequency
#
Noise can be generated at any
frequency
. I’ve only picked one frequency so far. Let’s look at the effect of frequency.
Try moving the slider
to see what happens at different frequencies:
frequency=
2
It’s just zooming in and out. That doesn’t seem very useful at first glance, but it is.
elevation[y][x] = noise(
frequency
*
nx,
frequency
*
ny);
It’s sometimes useful to think of
wavelength
, which is the inverse of frequency. Frequency is measured in oscillations per distance. Doubling the frequency makes everything half the size. Wavelength is measured in distance per oscillation, measured in pixels or tiles or meters etc. Doubling the wavelength makes everything twice the size. Wavelength is related to frequency:
wavelength = map_size / frequency
.
elevation[y][x] = noise(x
/
wavelength
, y
/
wavelength
);
I have
another tutorial
that explains the
concepts
: frequency, wavelength, amplitude, octaves, pink and blue and white noise, etc.
Octaves
#
To make the height map more interesting we’re going
add noise at different frequencies
:
+
+
=
elevation[y][x] =
1 *
noise(
1 *
nx,
1 *
ny);
+
0.5 *
noise(
2 *
nx,
2 *
ny);
+
0.25 *
noise(
4 *
nx,
4 *
ny);
Let’s mix big low frequency hills and small high frequency hills into the same map.
Move the slider
to add smaller hills to the mix:
0.0
0.5
1.0
Now that looks a lot more like the fractal terrain we want! We can now get hills and rugged mountains, but we still don’t get flat valleys. We need something else for that.
There’s a potential problem though. Since
noise
can go from 0 to 1, the sum
1 * noise() + 0.5 * noise() + 0.25 * noise()
can go from 0 to 1.75. The numbers
[1, 0.5, 0.25]
are called the
amplitudes
. The simplest thing to do is to divide by the sum of amplitudes:
e  =    1 * noise(1 * nx, 1 * ny);
+  0.5 * noise(2 * nx, 2 * ny);
+ 0.25 * noise(4 * nx, 4 * ny);
elevation[y][x] =
e / (1 + 0.5 + 0.25)
;
In practice, you may want to experiment to find the best divisor. Although the sum of amplitudes guarantees the elevation stays in the range 0–1, the elevation values may not be distributed the way you want.
Amplitudes are commonly set to be an array
[1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, …]
, where each amplitude is ½ the previous one. This ratio is called
gain
or
persistence
. However we’re not limited to using a fixed ratio. I use amplitudes
[1, 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5]
for many examples on this page to bring out more fine detail than the conventional amplitudes would do. Amplitudes can also be calculated dynamically, either from previous noise values (e.g. octave 1’s noise can affect octave 2’s a
44122864.article_summary: 本文介绍了使用噪声函数生成二维地图（如高度图和生物群系图）的基本方法，特别强调了利用Simplex或Perlin噪声函数生成地形。文章首先解释了如何通过循环填充一个数组，并用噪声值生成基础地图。接着讨论了频率对地形细节的影响，提出通过调整频率和波长来控制地形的缩放。为增加地形的复杂性，文章引入了多个频率的噪声叠加，即“倍频”或“八度”，并通过调整振幅使地形更接近自然界的分形结构。最后，文章提到可以动态调整振幅以优化地形生成，提供了实现更复杂地形的思路。

data.title: LibriVox
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: LibriVox提供由全球志愿者朗读的公共领域有声书，任何人都可免费收听或下载。其目录包含各类作品，如《Blackfoot Lodge Tales》、《The Magic Lantern and its Management》、科莱特的《La femme cachée》等。此外，LibriVox还发布社区播客，如第157期讨论了清理月活动。截至2025年，LibriVox已 catalog 20,485部作品，涉及48种语言，由14,310名志愿者参与录制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LibriVox及其相关项目的评价与争议

不同观点：
• **支持并推荐LibriVox的资源**：
  - [theschmed] 推荐了Lit2Go，认为其提供高质量的录音，尤其是儿童内容，但也提到Lit2Go上也有面向成人的高质量录音，如《Dracula》和《David Copperfield》。
  - [WillAdams] 推荐了LibriVox上H. Beam Piper的《Little Fuzzy》专业质量录音，但也指出LibriVox的录音质量参差不齐，有时家人不愿意忍受低质量的录音。
  - [waltbosz] 推荐了David Clarke演绎的《Sherlock Holmes》系列，认为其 narration质量很高。
  - [SubGenius] 提到Jane Austen的小说，特别是Karen Savage的演绎非常出色。
  - [photochemsyn] 推荐了Adrian Praetzellis演绎的Kipling的《Kim》，认为这是一个真正的宝藏。

• **LibriVox项目的个人情感与文化价值**：
  - [spookie] 表达了对LibriVox项目的感激，并希望通过贡献母语录音来保存正在消亡的语言（少于1000名使用者）。
  
• **对LibriVox项目未来发展的思考**：
  - [Moosdijk] 提出了AI对LibriVox的影响问题，认为虽然AI可能带来更多高质量的音频书籍，但也可能违背项目的精神。
  
• **对LibriVox功能的建议**：
  - [bArray] 提出LibriVox需要增加多重过滤功能，例如按语言、类型和关键词搜索，以提高用户体验。

• **LibriVox捐赠与支持**：
  - [abawany] 提到LibriVox现在可以通过Internet Archive接受捐赠，提供了捐赠链接。

• **个人使用体验**：
  - [dlcarrier] 分享了一次通过LibriVox找到公共领域书籍的经历，尽管书本身冗长乏味，但录音质量不错，解决了其读书俱乐部阅读任务的时间问题。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：AI技术对LibriVox的影响是潜在的争议点。一方面AI可能提高音频质量和数量，另一方面可能违背项目的志愿者精神和文化价值。
• **推荐的具体资源**：多个评论者具体推荐了他们认为优秀的录音和演绎者，这为其他用户提供了有价值的参考。
• **对文化保存的贡献**：一些评论者提到LibriVox在保存文化遗产和濒危语言方面的潜在作用。

data.title: Show HN: Localize React apps without rewriting code
data.author: maxpr
data.article_summary: Lingo.dev 是一个开源的 AI 驱动工具包，用于网页和移动应用的本地化与翻译。它包括三大工具：Lingo.dev CLI（快速翻译应用和 Markdown 内容）、Lingo.dev CI/CD（自动保持翻译更新）和 Lingo.dev Compiler（在构建时让 React 应用支持多语言，无需修改组件）。用户可以自带大型语言模型（LLM）或使用 Lingo.dev 提供的引擎。该项目欢迎社区贡献，并提供了详细的文档和演示。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用LLM（大型语言模型）和编译工具进行代码库的国际化（i18n）和本地化（l10n）的优缺点及实际应用中的挑战。

不同观点：
• **benbayard**：认为当前应用未处理好复数形式等复杂翻译问题，尤其是俄语、日语等语言。对LLM在真实生产环境中的表现持怀疑态度，建议使用ICU兼容的JSON。同时指出日语等RTL（从右到左）语言会带来UI和本地化挑战。
• **cluckindan**：认为应与现有的翻译管理格式或服务集成，而非依赖LLM。LLM在处理专业术语翻译时表现不佳，尤其对于技术或专业内容网站，当前方案可能不如传统方法。
• **exhaze**：分享了自己类似的工具项目，强调日本本地化的文化差异，以及日语在语言和设计上的独特性。支持使用LLM，并通过实例展示了LLM（如Gemini 2.5）在日语翻译中的优势。
• **halflife**：对LLM方案持怀疑态度，更偏向Angular的编译时i18n解决方案，而非React的运行时方案。希望编译器能与大型组织现有的本地化工作流集成。
• **lukol**：关注法律和品牌相关的特定措辞如何在翻译中保持不变，询问是否允许开发人员手动翻译特定字符串。
• **stared**：认为只需使用Cursor等工具进行少量提示即可开始翻译，并通过实例展示了如何在科学内容中验证翻译结果，强调在特定领域（如科学、工程）中翻译验证的重要性。
• **jjani**：作为早期用户，提出了一些改进建议，包括按语言设置模型、支持多源语言、修复某些技术问题等。
• **thrance**：强烈反对使用自动翻译工具进行本地化，认为机器翻译质量差，会给用户带来不好的体验，建议雇佣专业翻译人员。

补充讨论：
• **techn00** 和 **splix** 关注该工具是否适用于React Native（Expo）和桌面应用（Electron、Tauri），以及在没有React Router的项目中的适用性。
• **maelito** 和 **jackconsidine** 表达了对该工具在具体项目（如carte.app、Next.js）中的应用兴趣。

争议焦点：

44172428.article_summary: Lingo.dev 是一个开源的 AI 驱动工具包，用于网页和移动应用的本地化与翻译。它包括三大工具：Lingo.dev CLI（快速翻译应用和 Markdown 内容）、Lingo.dev CI/CD（自动保持翻译更新）和 Lingo.dev Compiler（在构建时让 React 应用支持多语言，无需修改组件）。用户可以自带大型语言模型（LLM）或使用 Lingo.dev 提供的引擎。该项目欢迎社区贡献，并提供了详细的文档和演示。

data.article_summary: 文章介绍了构建一个包含150万个英语词汇的语义网络的过程，该网络用于单词关联游戏。通过结合人工编辑的词库、书籍分类系统和受限的语言模型查询，研究团队解决了如何从40多个关联中筛选出17个可玩的选项的问题。结果显示，76%的随机词汇对可以在≤7步内连接，平均路径长度为6.43步。该网络展示了类似社交网络的“小世界”现象，允许玩家通过有意义的关联逐步导航，例如从“crown”到“inspect”的链条。传统的词库资源缺乏关联丰富性，而该项目通过扩大涵盖范围，包括俚语、技术术语和复合短语，构建了一个更全面的语义网络。这一成果在词汇关联研究中具有重要意义，并为单词游戏提供了理想的谜题参数。

« HOME
Making the Game
Mapping Language
Other Semantic Games
The Small World of English
Building a word game forced us to solve a measurement problem: how do you rank 40+ ways to associate any given word down to exactly 17 playable choices? We discovered that combining human-curated thesauri, book cataloging systems, and carefully constrained LLM queries creates a navigable network where 76% of random word pairs connect in ≤7 hops—but only when you deprecate superconnectors and balance multiple ranking signals. The resulting network of 1.5 million English terms reveals that nearly any two common words connect in 6-7 hops through chains of meaningful associations. The mean path length of 6.43 hops held true across a million random word pairs—shorter than we’d guessed, and remarkably stable.
1.5M

100M
Relationships
<7
Degrees of Separation
for 76% of words
This is consistent with the small-world structure and near-universal connectivity seen in lexical network research on smaller datasets.
1,2
The network's structure makes intuitive semantic navigation possible—players can
feel their way
through meaningful transitions: a crown's gemstones lead to emerald's foliage and finally to a forest canopy, or a flame becomes an ember, then a glowing memory, a mental recall, and finally the action to cancel.

The Mathematics of Semantic Distance
English exhibits network effects remarkably similar to social networks—nearly any random pair of words can reach each other in just a few hops through chains of meaningful associations. This “small world” phenomenon was first measured in word co-occurrence networks,
3
and persists even after we deprioritize superconnector words that might otherwise dominate many paths.
To probe this, we randomly sampled 1 million word pairs (4 days processing on 32 cores), to get a strong statistical sampling of the connected core of English.

Network Construction and Coverage
When we started this project, we tried the obvious approach: combining existing resources like WordNet with early-generation AI tools including LDA topic modeling and static word vectors. WordNet gave us clean synonym sets but lacked the associative richness players expect (“coffee” → “morning” not just “beverage”). LDA found topical clusters but mixed unrelated terms that happened to co-occur. Word vectors collapsed all senses into single points, making “bank” (river) indistinguishable from “bank” (financial). These produced fragmented, overly generic relationships that lacked the nuance our game needed.
We capture 40 associations per term (enough for algorithmic flexibility) and display 17 in our interfaces (what users can reasonably process). This depth provides flexibility for both puzzle generation and reference use.
1,525,522 headwords
We built a semantic network of 1.5 million English terms by casting a wider net than traditional resources. Where academic dictionaries drew sharp boundaries—excluding slang, technical jargon, compound phrases, and proper nouns—we included what people actually say and write. From “ice cream” to “thermodispersion,” from “ghosting” to “Khao-I-Dang.”
This scale would have cost tens of millions to achieve manually. Consider the monumental pre-LLM efforts:
WordNet (1985-2010)
- Princeton’s 25-year project produced 155,000 words in synonym groups. Became the NLP standard despite missing everyday compounds.
OED
(1857-1928, ongoing)
- The definitive historical dictionary with 500,000+ entries. Took 70 years and thousands of contributors.
Webster’s Third
(1961)
- America’s unabridged dictionary with 476,000 entries. Required 757 editor-years and $3.5 million ($50M+ today).
Roget’s Thesaurus (1852)
- The original meaning-based reference with 15,000 words in 1,000 conceptual categories.
Word counts become arbitrary at this scale. Include every technical term, place name, and slang variant, and the count explodes. Whether we have 1.5 million or 2 million depends entirely on where you draw the line.
Atlas of Connected Meaning
Our inclusion criteria cast a wide net: all terms that volunteer lexicographers at Wiktionary have
included
(slightly more liberal than typical unabridged dictionaries), plus high-importance Wikipedia topics that are 1-3 words long (measured by PageRank), plus frequently produced compound terms generated by LLMs

data.author: fidotron
data.article_summary: 苹果将Swift广泛用于生产环境中的云服务，取得了显著成果。例如，密码监控服务从Java重写为Swift后，性能提升了40%，可处理每天数十亿次请求，且扩展性、安全性和可用性均有改善。该服务是苹果密码管理应用的一部分，帮助用户管理密码和验证码，并通过密码监控功能提醒用户密码是否泄露。重写为Swift是为了解决Java在内存管理和垃圾回收方面的性能瓶颈，特别是在高负载下的长时间暂停问题。Swift的语法简洁、支持协议和泛型，提升了代码的模块化和可维护性，使其更适合大规模云服务需求。使用Swift的Vapor框架和自定义包，苹果成功实现了高效的动态扩展策略。

44172166.article_content:
Swift is heavily used in production for building cloud services at Apple, with incredible results. Last year, the Password Monitoring service was rewritten in Swift, handling multiple billions of requests per day from devices all over the world. In comparison with the previous Java service, the updated backend delivers a 40% increase in performance, along with improved scalability, security, and availability.
The Passwords app, introduced in the fall of 2024, helps users manage their passwords, passkeys, and verification codes. It allows them to store, autofill, and generate strong passwords that can be shared across all their devices, as well as share passwords with trusted contacts. One security feature included in the app is Password Monitoring, which warns users if one of their saved passwords shows up in a data leak. This feature has a server component that is maintained by Apple.
On a regular interval, Password Monitoring checks a user’s passwords against a continuously updated and curated list of passwords that are known to have been exposed in a leak. Importantly, this task is handled in a thoughtful, privacy-preserving way that never reveals users’ passwords to Apple. A detailed discussion of how this is done using the cryptographic private set intersection protocol is in the
Password Monitoring
section of the
Apple Platform Security
guide.
The migration from Java to Swift was motivated by a need to scale the Password Monitoring service in a performant way. The layered encryption module used by Password Monitoring requires a significant amount of computation for each request, yet the overall service needs to respond quickly even when under high load.
Choosing Swift for increased performance
For years, our team relied on Java to power large-scale, mission-critical services because of its proven stability and performance. However, Java’s memory management approach no longer aligns with our growing demands and efficiency goals. Instead of simply expanding hardware resources, we were seeking a more-efficient language to support our growth while reducing server overhead.
Prior to seeking a replacement language, we sought ways of tuning the JVM to achieve the performance required. Java’s G1 Garbage Collector (GC) mitigated some limitations of earlier collectors by introducing features like predictable pause times, region-based collection, and concurrent processing. However, even with these advancements, managing garbage collection at scale remains a challenge due to issues like prolonged GC pauses under high loads, increased performance overhead, and the complexity of fine-tuning for diverse workloads.
One of the challenges faced by our Java service was its inability to quickly provision and decommission instances due to the overhead of the JVM. The Password Monitoring service runs globally, so service load can greatly fluctuate throughout the day, even with client-side techniques to smooth over the distribution of traffic. The peak and trough of a day differ by approximately 50% regionally. To efficiently manage this, we aim to scale down when demand is low and scale up as demand peaks in different regions. A faster bootstrap time is a crucial requirement to support this dynamic scaling strategy.
Given the scale of our application and the volume of traffic we manage daily, the decision to transition from Java to another language was not made lightly. We evaluated our options, and found only a few languages that could help us achieve our goals. While you might expect that Apple would automatically choose Swift, we were pleasantly surprised by how well it fit the unique needs of a cloud-based service like ours. Swift has expressive syntax that was easy to learn, and could deliver the performance improvements necessary to meet the demands of our compute workloads. We decided to take a significant leap and started a rewrite of the Password Monitoring backend using Swift.
Our experience developing with Swift
We began rewriting our service using
Vapor
, a Swift web framework that provided Routing, Controller, and Content modules that we were able to build upon. Our service had additional requirements that led us to create a few custom packages with essential functionality: elliptic curve operations that are crucial for implementing
password monitoring
, auditing, configuration, error handling, and custom middleware.
One of the most significant aspects of Swift that impressed us was its emphasis on
protocols
. In Java, we relied heavily on inheritance, which can lead to complex class hierarchies and tight coupling. Swift’s approach of protocols and generics promotes modularity and reusability by allowing classes, structs, and enums to share common protocols, enabling a more flexible and scalable codebase. This shift in mindset encouraged us to think in terms of behaviors rather than concrete classes, resulting in cleaner and more maintainable code.

data.title: (On | No) Syntactic Support for Error Handling
data.author: henrikhorluck
data.article_summary:
Go语言的错误处理冗长问题一直是开发者抱怨的焦点，主要集中在需要频繁检查`if err != nil`。这种模式在涉及大量API调用的程序中尤为明显，导致代码中充斥大量与核心逻辑无关的错误处理代码。尽管社区对引入新机制的呼声很高，Go团队多年来尝试解决此问题，但未找到理想方案。

2018年，Go团队提出基于“检查和处理”（check and handle）机制的方案，但因过于复杂而被放弃。2019年，提出简化的“try”方案，虽然尝试通过工具`tryhard`评估影响，但因其隐藏控制流且返回机制不透明，再次被拒。

反思过程中，Go团队认识到应更早引入新关键词，并给予社区更多反馈空间。近期，有新提案回归原始设计并改进不足。尽管过程曲折，Go团队将继续听取反馈，探索更优错误处理方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Go语言的错误处理机制及其可能的改进

不同观点：
• 支持现有错误处理机制：一些开发者，如[threemux]和[maxwellg]，表示欣赏Go团队对错误处理的透明态度，并认为经过一段时间的适应后，现有的错误处理方式是可以接受的。他们认为显式的错误处理提供了更多的控制和灵活性，并且不希望为了改进而破坏向后兼容性。
• 提议增加语法糖：[_jab]和[packetlost]等人建议增加语法糖，以区分常见的`if err != nil`和不常见的`if err == nil`，从而减少错误发生。他们认为这将提高代码的可读性和安全性。
• 对比其他语言：[jamamp]和[JamesSwift]对比了Go和Rust等其他语言的错误处理方式，认为Rust的`Result<Value, Failure>`类型和`?`操作符提供了更好的错误处理机制，可以考虑引入类似功能。
• 对过程和决策的不满：[pie_flavor]批评Go团队在错误处理改进上的决策过程，认为他们在多个完美提案之间犹豫不决，导致问题长期未解决。
• 创新IDE插件可视化：[ajkjk]提出了一种创新的方式，通过IDE插件以可视化方式处理错误，从而提高代码的可读性和逻辑流的可视化。

补充讨论：
• 错误处理的常见模式：[jamamp]详细描述了Go中处理错误的四种常见模式，强调了Go中显式处理错误的好处。
• 对错误处理改进的需求：[arp242]提到尽管大多数用户没有对错误处理提出抱怨，但仍有部分用户认为可以做出一些改进。
• 引入高级语言特性：[hackingonempty]和[ziml77]讨论了引入高级语言特性如“do notation”或“monadic-let”的可能性，认为这些特性可以提供更简洁的错误处理方式。

争议焦点：
• 是否引入新的语法或机制：部分开发者认为现有的错误处理机制已经足够，而另一部分开发者则认为需要引入新的语法或机制来改进错误处理。
• 改进过程的透明性和效率：一些开发者对Go团队在错误处理改进上的决策过程表示不满，认为他们在多个提案之间犹豫不决，导致问题长期未解决。

总结：
Go语言的错误处理机制在开发者社区中引起了广泛讨论，部分开发者支持现有的显式错误处理方式，而另一部分开发者则提议引入新的语法糖或高级语言特性来改进错误处理。同时，也有开发者对Go团队在错误处理改进上的决策过程提出批评，认为需要更高效的决策和透明度。

44171677.article_content:
The Go Blog
[ On | No ] syntactic support for error handling
Robert Griesemer
3 June 2025
One of the oldest and most persistent complaints about Go concerns the verbosity of error handling.
We are all intimately (some may say painfully) familiar with this code pattern:
x, err := call()
if err != nil {
// handle err
}
The test
if err != nil
can be so pervasive that it drowns out the rest of the code.
This typically happens in programs that do a lot of API calls, and where handling errors
is rudimentary and they are simply returned.
Some programs end up with code that looks like this:
func printSum(a, b string) error {
x, err := strconv.Atoi(a)
if err != nil {
return err
}
y, err := strconv.Atoi(b)
if err != nil {
return err
}
fmt.Println("result:", x + y)
return nil
}
Of the ten lines of code in this function body, only four (the calls and the last two lines) appear to do real work.
The remaining six lines come across as noise.
The verbosity is real, and so it’s no wonder that complaints about error handling have topped
our annual user surveys for years.
(For a while, the lack of generics surpassed complaints about error handling, but now that
Go supports generics, error handling is back on top.)
The Go team takes community feedback seriously, and so for many years now we have tried to
come up with a solution for this problem, together with input from the Go community.
The first explicit attempt by the Go team dates back to 2018, when Russ Cox
formally described the problem
as part of what we called the Go 2 effort at that time.
He outlined a possible solution based on a
draft design
by Marcel van Lohuizen.
The design was based on a
check
and
handle
mechanism and was fairly comprehensive.
The draft includes a detailed analysis of alternative solutions, including comparisons with
approaches taken by other languages.
If you’re wondering if your particular error handling idea was previously considered,
read this document!
// printSum implementation using the proposed check/handle mechanism.
func printSum(a, b string) error {
handle err { return err }
x := check strconv.Atoi(a)
y := check strconv.Atoi(b)
fmt.Println("result:", x + y)
return nil
}
The
check
and
handle
approach was deemed too complicated and almost a year later, in 2019,
we followed up with the much simplified and by now
infamous
try
proposal
.
It was based on the ideas of
check
and
handle
, but the
check
pseudo-keyword became
the
try
built-in function and the
handle
part was omitted.
To explore the impact of the
try
built-in, we wrote a simple tool
(
tryhard
)
that rewrites existing error handling code using
try
.
The proposal was argued over intensively, approaching 900 comments on the
GitHub issue
.
// printSum implementation using the proposed try mechanism.
func printSum(a, b string) error {
// use a defer statement to augment errors before returning
x := try(strconv.Atoi(a))
y := try(strconv.Atoi(b))
fmt.Println("result:", x + y)
return nil
}
However,
try
affected control flow by returning from the enclosing function in case of an error,
and did so from potentially deeply nested expressions, thus hiding this control flow from view.
This made the proposal unpalatable to many, and despite significant investment
into this proposal we decided to abandon this effort too.
In retrospect it might have been better to introduce a new keyword,
something that we could do now since we have fine-grained control over the language version
via
go.mod
files and file-specific directives.
Restricting the use of
try
to assignments and statements might have alleviated some
of the other concerns. A
recent proposal
by Jimmy Frasche, which essentially
goes back to the original
check
and
handle
design and addresses some of that design’s
shortcomings, pursues that direction.
The repercussions of the
try
proposal led to much soul searching including a series of blog
posts by Russ Cox:
“Thinking about the Go Proposal Process”
.
One conclusion was that we likely diminished our chances for a better outcome by presenting an almost
fully baked proposal with little space for community feedback and a “threatening” implementation
timeline. Per
“Go Proposal Process: Large Changes”
:
“in retrospect,
try
was a large enough change that the new design we published […] should have
been a second draft design, not a proposal with an implementation timeline”.
But irrespective of a possible process and communication failure in this case, the user sentiment towards
the proposal was very strongly not in favor.
We didn’t have a better solution at that time and didn’t pursue syntax changes for error handling for several years.
Plenty of people in the community were inspired, though, and we received a steady trickle
of error handling proposals, many very similar to each other, some interesting, some incomprehensible,
and some infeasible.
To keep track of the expanding landscape, another year later, Ian Lance Taylor created an
umbrella issue
which summarizes the current state of proposed chan

data.title: The Shape of the Essay Field
data.author: luisb
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了人们为何会对手头信息一无所知的原因，并将其分为三类：信息不重要、读者迟钝或读者缺乏经验。作者指出，如果写作目的是向聪明人讲述重要内容，那么主要读者群体往往是年轻人，因为他们更容易受到新思想的影响。写作的影响力取决于它对读者思维的改变程度和话题的重要性，但要在两者间取得平衡很难。作者反思自己的写作动机，强调自己写作并非为了取悦特定年龄的读者，而是为了自我探索和发现。最终，作者思考哪些重要事情年轻人通常领悟较晚，并考虑如何通过写作引发他们的思考。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：评论围绕如何评估读者对某一文章内容的未知程度及其原因，探讨了不同因素对知识获取和理解的影响。

不同观点：
• analog31认为，读者不知道某事的原因可能包括事情不重要、读者迟钝、缺乏经验，甚至信息本身可能是错误的。这种怀疑态度强调了科学训练带来的批判性思维。
• barrkel提出了不同的三个原因：困难、机会和动机。他认为将人们归为“迟钝”是过于简化的做法，并指出动机可以克服困难并发现机会。
• piinbinary欣赏文章将读者已经隐约想到的想法明确表达出来，认为这有助于整理思绪并提供新的讨论起点。
• doctoring指出，“年轻”和“ inexperienced”不能完全等同，年长者在面对新事物时也可能缺乏经验。
• paulorlando通过一个具体例子说明，有些无知源于未能识别和分析自己经历中的异常现象。
• colmmacc强调，让聪明人“知道得更少”其实是帮助他们打破固有假设，看到新的可能性。
• GMoromisato用“diffs”比喻文章的作用，指出知识基础不同会影响文章的新颖性和影响力，并认为知识是多维度的。
• jedberg引用XKCD漫画，指出即使是聪明年长的人也有很多未接触过的重要知识，因此他们也可以被文章 surprise。
• dgs_sgd认为，文章忽略了一个明显的原因：作者认为重要的事情可能对读者并不重要。
• kelseyfrog用煮土豆的比喻表达了对简单工作的价值观，虽然与主题不直接相关，但强调了关注和克制的价值。
• Seattle3503将文章观点与Alva Noë的 strange tools理论联系起来，讨论艺术如何通过 disrupt 常规来揭示感知和概念过程。

• 争议的焦点在于如何定义和解释读者对某一话题的无知。不同评论者提出了多种原因，包括经验缺乏、信息本身问题、机会和动机的缺乏等。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是知识的维度性，GMoromisato和jedberg等评论者强调知识是多维的，而非简单的线性积累。

44168201.article_content:
June 2025
An essay has to tell people something they don't already know. But
there are three different reasons people might not know something,
and they yield three very different kinds of essays.
One reason people won't know something is if it's not important to
know. That doesn't mean it will make a bad essay. For example, you
might write a good essay about a particular model of car. Readers
would learn something from it. It would add to their picture of the
world. For a handful of readers it might even spur some kind of
epiphany. But unless this is a very unusual car it's not critical
for everyone to know about it.
[
1
]
If something isn't important to know, there's no answer to the
question of why people don't know it. Not knowing random facts is
the default. But if you're going to write about things that
are
important to know, you have to ask why your readers don't already
know them. Is it because they're smart but inexperienced, or because
they're obtuse?
So the three reasons readers might not already know what you tell
them are (a) that it's not important, (b) that they're obtuse,
or (c) that they're inexperienced.
The reason I did this breakdown was to get at the following fact,
which might have seemed controversial if I'd led with it, but should
be obvious now. If you're writing for smart people about important
things, you're writing for the young.
Or more precisely, that's where you'll have the most effect. Whatever
you say should also be at least somewhat novel to you, however old
you are. It's not an essay otherwise, because an essay is something
you write to figure something out. But whatever you figure out will
presumably be more of a surprise to younger readers than it is to
you.
There's a continuum of surprise. At one extreme, something you read
can change your whole way of thinking.
The Selfish Gene
did this
to me. It was like suddenly seeing the other interpretation of an
ambiguous image: you can treat genes rather than organisms as the
protagonists, and evolution becomes easier to understand when you
do. At the other extreme, writing merely puts into words something
readers were already thinking — or thought they were.
The impact of an essay is how much it changes readers' thinking
multiplied by the importance of the topic. But it's hard to do well
at both. It's hard to have big new ideas about important topics.
So in practice there's a tradeoff: you can change readers' thinking
a lot about moderately important things, or change it a little about
very important ones. But with younger readers the tradeoff shifts.
There's more room to change their thinking, so there's a bigger
payoff for writing about important things.
The tradeoff isn't a conscious one, at least not for me. It's more
like a kind of gravitational field that writers work in. But every
essayist works in it, whether they realize it or not.
This seems obvious once you state it, but it took me a long time
to understand. I knew I wanted to write for smart people about
important topics. I noticed empirically that I seemed to be writing
for the young. But it took me years to understand that the latter
was an automatic consequence of the former. In fact I only really
figured it out as I was writing this essay.
Now that I know it, should I change anything? I don't think so. In
fact seeing the shape of the field that writers work in has reminded
me that I'm not optimizing for returns in it. I'm not trying to
surprise readers of any particular age; I'm trying to surprise
myself.
The way I usually decide what to write about is by following
curiosity. I notice something new and dig into it. It would probably
be a mistake to change that. But seeing the shape of the essay field
has set me thinking. What would surprise young readers? Which
important things do people tend to learn late? Interesting question.
I should think about that.
Note
[
1
]
It's hard to write a really good essay about an unimportant
topic, though, because a really good essayist will inevitably draw
the topic into deeper waters. E. B. White could write an essay about
how to boil potatoes that ended up being full of timeless wisdom.
In which case, of course, it wouldn't really be about how to boil
potatoes; that would just have been the starting point.
Thanks
to Jessica Livingston and Michael
Nielsen for reading drafts of this.

data.title: Show HN: PinSend – Share text between devices using a PIN(P2P, no login)
data.author: avovsya
data.article_summary: PinSend是一款用于在设备间即时、安全分享文本和图片的工具。用户可以通过创建新会话或输入PIN加入现有会话，开始分享内容。分享过程通过端到端加密确保安全，且数据不存储在服务器上。用户只需在浏览器中操作，无需注册账户。分享时，会生成PIN、链接或QR码，其他设备可以快速加入并实时同步内容。用户还可以随时离开会话或终止整个会话。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：基于WebRTC和P2P技术的文本和文件共享工具的实现、安全性、用户体验及技术细节。

不同观点：
• [nafey] 认为WebRTC的P2P连接必须通过中心化的服务器交换地址，质疑该工具如何在没有服务器中继的情况下实现P2P连接。
• [AnonC] 关注工具的端到端加密和P2P性质，质疑源代码是否开放及自托管的可能性，并询问业务模式及图片传输功能。对当前功能表示怀疑，并提到类似服务如Firefox Send。
• [syx] 强调用户体验的改进，如URL的易用性和PIN的安全性，建议增加QR码功能，并强调端到端加密的重要性。
• [ebfe1] 自荐其开发的文件共享工具，强调浏览器端加密及安全性，并对WebRTC技术表示赞赏。
• [gruez] 质疑文本共享需要网站及PIN的必要性，建议直接使用QR码传输文本。
• [cloudking] 提出Signal应用作为类似解决方案，强调其端到端加密及跨设备使用功能。
• [mgkimsal] 赞赏该工具的实现，并分享自己使用其他工具的经验，同时关注安全性问题，建议增加会话批准功能。
• [fladd] 对工具的实际操作感到困惑，描述了跨设备连接时遇到的问题，质疑会话管理的有效性。
• [globalnode] 对WebRTC技术表示兴趣，但希望有更易懂的学习资源。
• [markvdb] 提供了一些用户界面和功能设计上的建议，如简化URL和避免对用户需求的假设。
• [doomrobo] 关注PIN码的安全性，提到Magic Wormhole使用的PAKE协议，以避免暴力破解攻击。
• [Imustaskforhelp] 提供了大量建议，包括使用类似piping server和wormhole协议的技术，并讨论了隐私保护和托管问题，最后表达了对该工具的赞赏。
• [lxgr] 质疑六位字母数字代码如何实现WebRTC连接的初始设置，认为可能需要服务器参与。
• [giantg2] 担心六位代码的安全性，认为需要增加会话过期和连接批准功能以提高安全性。
• [fabrice_d] 关注初始ICE连接的协商过程，质疑在没有中继服务器的情况下如何实现。

补充讨论：
• 工具的安全性和加密方式是讨论的核心，尤其是端到端加密和PIN码的安全性。
• 用户体验和功能设计也是重要关注点，包括URL的易用性、QR码功能和跨设备连接的便捷性。
• 技术实现细节如WebRTC的初始连接设置和ICE协商过程引起了技术背景用户的兴趣和讨论。
• 业务模式和自托管可能性也是部分用户关心的问题，反映了用户对服务可持续性和隐私保护的关注。

data.title: Show HN: Ultra-lightweight chunker library with emoji support
data.author: Beardier
data.article_summary: "Chonkify" 是一个超轻量级的 JavaScript 库，用于将各种数据结构（如数组、字符串、Set、Map、AsyncIterable 等）分块处理。它支持处理 Unicode 表情符号和复杂的符号，无依赖，支持异步迭代，并且兼容 ESM 和 TypeScript。主要功能包括 `chonk(iterable, size)` 用于同步分块，以及 `chonkAsync(asyncIterable, size)` 用于异步分块。该库大小仅约 5.5 kB，适合处理大型数据集。适用于浏览器和 Node.js 环境。
data.comments_summary:

44172017.article_summary: "Chonkify" 是一个超轻量级的 JavaScript 库，用于将各种数据结构（如数组、字符串、Set、Map、AsyncIterable 等）分块处理。它支持处理 Unicode 表情符号和复杂的符号，无依赖，支持异步迭代，并且兼容 ESM 和 TypeScript。主要功能包括 `chonk(iterable, size)` 用于同步分块，以及 `chonkAsync(asyncIterable, size)` 用于异步分块。该库大小仅约 5.5 kB，适合处理大型数据集。适用于浏览器和 Node.js 环境。

data.title: Vision Language Models Are Biased
data.author: taesiri
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了视觉语言模型（VLMs）在处理图像计数任务时的偏见问题。研究发现，尽管这些模型在常见对象（如阿迪达斯logo有3条纹，狗有4条腿）的图像上能达到100%的准确率，但在处理反事实图像（如有4条纹的阿迪达斯式logo或有5条腿的狗）时，准确率仅为约17%。这表明VLMs依赖于记忆知识而非实际视觉分析。模型在面对熟悉对象时，会默认使用记忆中的知识，而不是进行实际视觉分析，导致在面对细微修改的图像时出现严重错误。文章提出了一种三步测试框架（VLMBias），揭示了VLMs在视觉任务中的根本缺陷，并通过多个领域的实验验证了这一问题。研究结果强调了VLMs在视觉处理中的确认偏误，并呼吁对模型进行改进以提高其视觉分析能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：视觉语言模型（VLM）在处理图像和文本时的错误和局限性

不同观点：
• **[rafram]** 认为VLM在无法读取文字或段落时，会输出它预期看到的内容，而不是简单地失败。这种错误比传统的OCR错误更糟糕，因为输出的内容往往也是人们期望看到的，因此在人工审核中很难发现。

• **[proc0]** 指出VLM的错误中有75.70%是“偏见对齐”的，即模型根据先验知识而非实际图像内容给出答案。他们认为这不只是视觉模型的问题，LLM/transformers也存在类似问题，模型的进步主要体现在分辨率、保真度和输出真实感上，而非正确性和逻辑推理。他们举例说明在生成图像时无法满足特定要求。

• **[jbay808]** 不同意VLM只依赖记忆而不进行视觉分析的观点，认为模型确实能看到图像，只是过度依赖先验知识。他们认为这与人类的视觉处理相似，人类也会在不同情境下依赖先验知识。

• **[jsnider3]** 对VLM无法通过二次检查发现错误感到惊讶，认为这是比视觉错觉更严重的问题。

• **[runako]** 尝试在ChatGPT 4o中复现错误但没有成功，给出的结果显示模型能够识别图像中的异常。

• **[nialv7]** 认为VLM在识别错误方面表现不佳可能与其生成过程有关，因为如果模型无法识别问题，它就无法修复问题。

• **[taeric]** 将这些错误与模型在解决谜题时的表现进行类比，指出模型在处理特定类型问题时的局限性。

• **[VHRanger]** 提到模型在文本输入上的“鹦鹉学舌”行为，并举例说明模型在处理经典谜语时的失败，认为这显示了模型在逻辑推理上的不足。

• **[esafak]** 认为VLM与人类在视觉处理上的差异在于人类能区分真实视觉和合成图像，而VLM则不能。

• **[gamerDude]** 建议通过改变输入方法或进行预处理步骤来改善模型表现，提到可以借鉴人类视觉处理的机制。

• **[LeoPanthera]** 认为VLM在回答某些问题时可能基于一般性知识而非具体图像内容，举例说明模型可能先识别出“Puma”，然后根据一般知识给出答案。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于VLM是否真正进行视觉分析，还是仅仅依赖先验知识。
• 对模型在不同情境下的错误类型和原因有不同看法，有人认为这些错误显示了模型的根本局限，有人则认为这与人类处理信息的方式类似。
• 对如何改进模型表现提出了不同的建议和思考，包括输入方法的改变和借鉴人类视觉处理机制。

Dataset on HuggingFace
Test It Yourself
Finding:
State-of-the-art Vision Language Models achieve
100%
accuracy counting on images of popular subjects (e.g. knowing that the Adidas logo has 3 stripes and a dog has 4 legs) but are only
~17%
accurate in counting in counterfactual images (e.g. counting stripes in a 4-striped Adidas-like logo or counting legs in a 5-legged dog).
VLMs don't actually "see" - they rely on memorized knowledge instead of visual analysis due to bias.
Figure 1: VLM Failures Overview
VLMs fail on 6 counting tasks and one low-level vision task across seven domains
VLMs fail on 6 counting tasks (a–e & g) and one low-level vision task (f). State-of-the-art models achieve perfect performance on original images but catastrophically fail when objects are subtly modified, defaulting to memorized knowledge rather than actual visual analysis.
The Problem: VLMs Can't Count When It Matters
Imagine asking GPT-4o to count the legs of an animal, and it gets it right every time. Impressive, right?
Now imagine adding just
one extra leg
to that animal and asking again. Suddenly, it fails completely.
The Dog Experiment
Original dog (4 legs):
All models get it right
Same dog with 5 legs:
All models still say "4"
They're not counting - they're just recalling "dogs have 4 legs" from their training data.
Figure 3: Subtle Modification Failures
VLMs fail to detect subtle changes in counterfactuals and default to biased answers
VLMs fail to detect subtle changes in counterfactuals (CF) and default to biased answers. Despite clear visual modifications (extra legs, extra stripes), all models consistently output the expected "normal" values rather than counting what they actually see.
The Core Issue:
VLMs suffer from severe confirmation bias. When they see familiar objects, they default to memorized knowledge instead of performing actual visual analysis. This isn't a minor glitch - it's a fundamental flaw in how these models process visual information.
How We Test VLM Bias: The VLMBias Framework
Our testing methodology follows a simple but powerful three-step process that exposes the fundamental difference between memorization and actual visual analysis in VLMs.
Figure 2: VLMBias Testing Framework
Three-step methodology: (a) Confirm VLM knowledge, (b) Test on counterfactuals, (c) Analyze bias-relevant backgrounds
Given a subject (e.g., Adidas logo), we first confirm that all VLMs have sufficient knowledge about the subject via ID and counting sanity-check questions (a). Then, we test VLMs on the counterfactual image (b) and report accuracy on counting (Q1 & Q2) and Y/N identification tasks (Q3). For all tasks, we test the hypothesis that visual bias cues in the background (c) may be so strong that they cause VLMs to ignore the modified object and default to biased answers.
Step 1: Sanity Check
Confirm VLMs have the knowledge
ID Question:
"What shoe logo is this?" → "Adidas" ✓
Counting Question:
"How many stripes?" → "3" ✓
Result: 100% accuracy on original images across all models
Step 2: The Bias Test
Test on counterfactual images
Q1:
"How many visible stripes?" → "3" ✗ (should be "4")
Q2:
"Count the visible stripes" → "3" ✗ (should be "4")
Q3:
"Is this the Adidas logo?" → "Yes" ✗ (should be "No")
Result: 17.05% average accuracy - catastrophic failure!
The Critical Insight:
The gap between Step 1 (100% accuracy) and Step 2 (17% accuracy) proves that VLMs are not actually "seeing" - they're retrieving memorized associations. When the visual evidence contradicts their training data, they consistently choose memorized knowledge over what's actually in the image.

Explore examples from all 7 domains where state-of-the-art VLMs fail spectacularly.

data.title: Cloudlflare builds OAuth with Claude and publishes all the prompts
data.author: gregorywegory
data.article_summary: 该项目是一个用于Cloudflare Workers的OAuth 2.1提供者库，用TypeScript编写，支持PKCE。它为API端点添加授权功能，自动处理所有token管理。开发者可以像编写常规fetch处理程序一样编写API处理程序，并接收已认证的用户信息。该库不限定用户管理和认证方式，也不限定UI框架。它不存储任何秘密信息，仅存储其哈希值。使用示例展示了如何配置API路由、处理程序、授权和token端点等。该库仍处于早期开发阶段，API可能会变化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用LLM（如Claude）生成代码的可行性、安全性及其实际效果

不同观点：
• 支持观点：
  - ElijahLynn：起初持怀疑态度，但通过实际使用发现Claude生成的代码质量不错，并且经过了工程师的严格审查。认为这种AI辅助开发方式有效，尤其在安全性和合规性上得到了保障。
  - paxys：认为AI辅助编码是未来趋势，尤其是在有经验的工程师审查和测试代码的前提下。提出AI不会取代工程师，而是提高生产力。
  - jes5199：个人经验表明使用Claude显著提高了生产力，尽管认知负荷增加，但工具的改进速度很快。

• 反对观点：
  - aeneas_ory：对AI生成代码的安全性表示担忧，认为隐藏的问题可能难以发现。指出使用经过长时间迭代和安全测试的工具更为可靠。
  - _tqr3：个人经验表明使用LLM生成代码时遇到了循环问题和上下文丢失，认为目前LLM的效果还不理想。

• 中立/疑问观点：
  - mtlynch：对帖子中提到的“I (@kentonv)”表示困惑，经过编辑后理解为引用README的内容，但对帖子的清晰度提出建议。
  - Luker88：对使用AI生成代码的版权问题提出疑问，不清楚在这种情况下如何应用版权法。
  - vaidhy：指出阅读他人代码比编写代码更费力，因此认为使用LLM生成短代码片段更为实际。

OAuth 2.1 Provider Framework for Cloudflare Workers
This is a TypeScript library that implements the provider side of the OAuth 2.1 protocol with PKCE support. The library is intended to be used on Cloudflare Workers.
Beta
As of March, 2025, this library is very new, prerelease software. The API is still subject to change.
Benefits of this library
The library acts as a wrapper around your Worker code, which adds authorization for your API endpoints.
All token management is handled automatically.
Your API handler is written like a regular fetch handler, but receives the already-authenticated user details as a parameter. No need to perform any checks of your own.
The library is agnostic to how you manage and authenticate users.
The library is agnostic to how you build your UI. Your authorization flow can be implemented using whatever UI framework you use for everything else.
The library's storage does not store any secrets, only hashes of them.

主要讨论点：Unix与Mac文件处理方式的差异及版本控制系统的历史

不同观点：
• [jandrese的观点] 认为Unix未采用Mac的resource fork机制很遗憾。他指出，使用一对4字节的字段来表示文件类型和关联程序，比通过读取文件开头的几个字节来猜测文件类型要好。他认为`file(1)`命令一直是一种权宜之计（hack）。

• [kps的观点] 没有直接回应jandrese的观点，而是提到了Unix版本控制系统SCCS的Git仓库，表达了对有人能够找到SCCS最早提交记录的期待。这似乎是在讨论Unix的历史和技术遗产，而非具体的文件处理问题。

补充讨论：
• jandrese的论据集中在文件类型的明确标识上，认为通过文件扩展名或特定的字段来标识文件类型更加准确和高效，而不是依赖于读取文件内容来推断类型。

• kps的评论似乎偏离了jandrese的主要论点，将讨论引向了Unix版本控制系统的历史追溯问题，这显示出评论者对Unix技术演进的兴趣。

• 争议的焦点在于文件类型的标识方式：jandrese支持采用类似Mac的resource fork机制，而Unix传统上依赖于通过内容推断文件类型的方法，这被jandrese视为一种不理想的解决方案。

总结来看，评论中存在两个主要讨论方向：一个是关于Unix与Mac在文件类型处理上的技术差异，另一个是关于Unix版本控制系统历史的技术讨论。两者虽在同一主题下，但讨论的具体内容有所不同。

• **StellarScience**介绍其公司专注于科学和工程分析应用开发，涉及空间态势感知、激光系统建模、AI/ML等领域。要求候选人具备物理、工程、数学或计算机科学学士学位，技术栈包括C++23、Qt、CMake等。

• **willdoenlen**（Norm Ai）介绍其公司正在构建用于合规性的人工智能，提供多个工程职位，薪酬范围$150k-$250k，工作地点为纽约市混合模式。公司已筹集$87m资金，客户和投资者包括大型金融机构。

• **sophanox_**（Stored）招聘全栈/后端工程师，工作时间为欧洲时区，要求候选人具备C#、TypeScript、Postgres等技术经验，公司为数字支付创业公司，已完成多轮融资。

• **hollyproulx**（Phonely）介绍其公司通过AI处理数十亿通电话，招聘多个职位包括前端工程师、销售和客户成功经理。公司通过YC加速，成长迅速，工作地点为旧金山。

• 各公司提供的薪酬、工作地点（远程或混合模式）和工作时间灵活性有较大差异。例如，Normcore.io和Monadical.com强调完全远程和灵活工作时间，而Lyra Energy和Phonely则要求onsite或特定地区候选人。

• 多个公司提到股权补偿和创业环境，如ClearStride AI和Adora AI，显示出这些公司希望吸引有创业精神的技术人才。

• 工作地点要求可能成为争议点，尤其是对远程工作的偏好。例如，Lyra Energy和Phonely要求onsite或特定地区候选人，而其他公司如Normcore.io和Monadical.com则提供完全远程工作选项。

data.title: What Happens If We Inline Everything?
data.author: abhi9u
data.article_summary:
本文探讨了在编译器中进行极致内联（inline everything）优化的可能性和后果。内联被视为编译器优化中最重要的一环，但其缺点包括代码重复、代码体积膨胀和寄存器分配压力增加。作者试图忽视这些限制，专注于运行时性能，提出如果内联所有可内联的代码，是否会影响运行时性能。

尽管LLVM无法内联所有调用（如复杂的递归函数），但在多数情况下，可以通过调整内联盈利性分析来实现广泛内联。然而，现代编译器的内联决策和盈利性分析紧密耦合，修改并非易事。作者曾就此问题撰写论文，并简要介绍了LLVM内联决策的过程，指出从Inliner.cpp开始，通过调用图的强连通分量（SCC）进行分析。

最终，作者希望通过实验证明极致内联是否能提升运行时性能，但目前尚无明确答案。

Base image by Jens Mahnke
May 7, 2025
Do you want to share your thoughts? Please shoot me an email.
Don't want to miss any updates? You can follow this
RSS
feed
or sign up for my newsletter:
Background
Gather around kids! Today we'll explore the following intriguing question: what
happens if we inline everything?
If you're not familiar with inlining, you should know that it is considered by
many (including important figures in the compiler community like
Chandler
Carruth
) to be the single most important
optimization in optimizing compilers. For a little more info on how it works,
here's
a shameless plug of a presentation
we gave with a bunch of folks at the LLVM Developers' Meeting on interprocedural
optimization.
I talked about inling
, and
watching the first ~6 minutes should give a good idea.
1
In this video I mention that inlining
has
drawbacks
. In other words, yes, inlining
is
supposed to be the super duper tool in the compiler's toolkit, but you're
supposed to use it with care! Or should you?
What are the drawbacks anyway? In the video I mention basically three: (a) code
duplication, (b) code-size explosion, and (c) increased register-allocator
presure. (a) can increase compile times
2
because the same code is compiled multiple times. (b)
3
can create large executables, which means they both take more
space on the disk, and they take longer to load. Moreover, it can theoretically
lead to instruction cache misses as you jump through all this code. The problem
of (c) is that it can obviously lead to unnecessary register spills.
But today we're going against frugality. The attitude we'll take is simple: we
only care about runtime performance. This means “I have a lot of disk space, and
a lot of time to spare on compile times; let's make our code as fast as
possible!” In other words, if we ignore other constraints and we inline
everything, will the runtime performance be any worse (as (b) and (c) would
imply)? To the best of my knowledge, nobody has answered this (using
experimental evidence) up to now. So, let's find out.
Can we inline everything?
Well, no. There are calls that LLVM simply cannot inline;
4
I mention some cases
in the
video
. In the following experiments, most
of the code used will be available to the compiler (basically except for
standard-library code), and there won't be many virtual functions or function
pointers (definitely not in the code we'll write). So, the biggest obstacle to
inlining will be recursion (which will also be rare). In short, the vast
majority of functions will be inlinable.
I should note here that LLVM
can
inline some simple recursive calls;
particularly calls to tail-recursive functions, but that's because the
tail-recursive call elimination pass removed the recursion first (see
this
). So, for example, it can inline a
simple factorial function:
int
fac
(
int
x
)
{
if
(
x
==
1
)
{
return
1
;
}
return
fac
(
x
-
1
)
*
x
;
}
but it cannot inline a recursive fibonacci function:
int
fib
(
int
x
)
{
if
(
x
==
1
)
{
return
1
;
}
if
(
x
==
2
)
{
return
1
;
}
return
fib
(
x
-
1
)
+
fib
(
x
-
2
);
}
Making LLVM inline everything (else)
This should have been easy, but it's not. It should have been easy to change the
inlining profitability, i.e., the part of LLVM that decides when inlining is
beneficial. If that was the case, folks could change the profitability analysis
without having to understand the internals of inlining. For example, it should
have been easy for a non-compiler-expert, machine-learning researcher to change
LLVM's inlining profitability analysis. In our case, we would just change the
profitability analysis to always say yes!
Unfortunately, however, things are not so simple in modern compilers. It turns
out I wrote
a whole
thesis
on this problem. Today, the transformation and profitability analysis code is
tightly coupled, such that one cannot change the one without understanding the
other. Nevertheless, inlining in LLVM is one of the good cases, as we have a
better separation than in other passes.
5
So, let me briefly explain the
course of an inlining decision today. We'll use the latest LLVM release, which,
as of writing this article, is 20.1.0.
The inlining pass starts at
Inliner.cpp
.
This is a Call-Graph Strongly-Connected-Component (CGSCC) pass. To get a good
idea of what this means, I suggest watching
this
excerpt
by Chandler Carruth, or watching
the
latter half of my video
. But you may
be relieved to know that it's not that relevant to this article; you can just
think that the Inliner visits each function separately. If you want the TL;DR,
here it is: we take the call graph,
6
we split it into strongly connected components (SCCs), and then
we visit each SCC separately.
7
As I mentioned above, most of the complexity in inlining comes from the
profitability analysis. To decide if it's profitable to inline a function call,
LLVM uses what it calls an
InlineAdvisor
. So, eventually we ask for its advice
here
.
...

data.title: Builder.ai Collapses: $1.5B 'AI' Startup Exposed as 'Indians'?
data.author: healsdata
data.article_summary: Builder.ai，一家曾获微软支持、估值15亿美元的AI创业公司，现因主要贷方扣押3700万美元而陷入运营瘫痪，已申请破产保护。这家无代码平台公司此前宣称利用AI帮助企业轻松构建应用，但实际上依靠700名印度开发人员手动编写代码，伪装成AI服务。公司CEO更换、财务造假曝光以及投资者信心的崩溃，最终导致其在英国、美国、阿联酋、新加坡和印度等地申请破产。此事件揭示了AI行业过度炒作、财务监管不力等问题，引发对AI公司透明度和营销伦理的广泛关注。

44169759.article_content:
Technology
Builder.ai, the $1.5 billion 'AI' startup once touted with Microsoft backing, is now seeking bankruptcy protection. A major lender's $37 million seizure paralysed operations.
X /   Harsh Dwivedi | Building Medial @harsh_dwivedi7
The tech world is reeling from revelations that Builder.ai, once hailed as a $1.5 billion (£1.11 billion), 'AI' powerhouse, now faces scrutiny as its highly promoted artificial intelligence facade crumbles, revealing a human-powered operation behind the cutting-edge AI automation.
Builder.ai, the British no-code AI startup that once garnered acclaim for its strategic partnership with
Microsoft
and secured a $250 million (£184.64 million) investment led by the Qatar Investment Authority,
declared
Tuesday that it is initiating bankruptcy protection.
As reported by
Bloomberg
, the company's dramatic decline occurred after a key lender, Viola Credit, withdrew $37 million (£27.33 million) from its accounts, leaving a mere $5 million (£3.69 million) in restricted funds and effectively paralysing operations in five nations.
Earlier this year, CEO Manpreet Ratia took over from founder Sachin Dev Duggal in a boardroom shake-up designed to restore investor confidence. Ratia has since stated that most of the company's workforce has been laid off. As Bloomberg reports, Builder.ai will now commence bankruptcy filings in its operational territories, including the UK, US, UAE, Singapore, and India.
Builder.ai's $450 Million Funding: Big Names, Big Promises
Launched in 2016, Builder.ai presented itself as a groundbreaking platform, allowing businesses to create customised applications with minimal coding, leveraging
artificial intelligence
. As reported by Bloomberg, the company accumulated over $450 million (£332.36 million) in total funding, drawing in prominent investors such as
Microsoft
, the World Bank's IFC, Jeffrey Katzenberg's WndrCo, Lakestar, and SoftBank's DeepCore incubator.
Less than two months ago, Builder.ai admitted to revising down core sales numbers and engaging auditors to inspect its financials for the past two years. This came amidst concerns from former employees who suggested sales performance had been inflated during prior investor briefings.
'Bots' Revealed As Builders From India
Bloomberg notes that these allegations initiated a cascade of investor apprehension, internal changes, and an eventual erosion of confidence. Adding to the troubles, Linas Beliūnas, Director of the financial company Zero Hash, recently exposed that Builder.ai lacked true AI, instead utilising a group of Indian developers who were merely pretending to be bots writing code.
😃 The Natasha neural network turned out to be 700 Indian programmers
The startup BuilderAI offered to write any application, like in a constructor, by selecting the necessary functions.
In reality, customer requests were sent to the Indian office, where 700 Indians wrote code…
pic.twitter.com/lYWipf63cp
— Bernhard Engelbrecht (@BernhardEngel_)
May 29, 2025
'It turns out the company had no AI and instead was just a group of Indian developers pretending to write code as AI,' he wrote in a
LinkedIn post
. Beliūnas also highlights that Duggal reportedly presented false revenue figures to investors. Remarkably, the company managed to sustain this deception for eight years.
Investor Dreams Shattered By Reality
The critical moment arrived when Viola Credit, which had provided the company with a $50 million loan in 2023, took control of $37 million (£27.33 million) from its accounts. This action rendered Builder.ai incapable of fulfilling payroll commitments or maintaining essential operations.
Manpreet Ratia informed Bloomberg that the remaining funds, held in Indian accounts, are inaccessible due to regulatory restrictions.
The Broader Impact Of Builder.ai's Collapse
The insolvency proceedings at Builder.ai mirror a rising trend of instability within AI startups. Phil Brunkard, an executive counsellor at Info-Tech Research Group, shared with Computer World that many AI companies expanded rapidly, fueled by hype, frequently without robust financial oversight or genuinely unique products.
'The Qatar Investment Authority (QIA) is one of the biggest losers in this saga. They led a $250 million (£184.68 million) funding round two years ago,' Beliūnas adds.
Competition regulators are reportedly examining Builder.ai's marketing practices, with potential implications for how AI companies present their capabilities to investors and customers.
The scandal serves as a stark reminder that whilst artificial intelligence continues advancing rapidly, human expertise remains irreplaceable in many complex technical domains—a lesson that Builder.ai learned through public humiliation rather than honest business practices.
As the dust settles, the tech industry faces uncomfortable questions about transparency, accountability, and the ethical boundaries of AI marketing in an increasingly sceptical marketplace.

主要讨论点：科学出版过程中的时间问题、负面结果的发表困难以及科学界的激励机制和障碍

不同观点：
• [gus_massa] 提到科学出版的时间周期存在学科差异。在物理学领域，从投稿到发表大约需要3个月，而在数学领域，审稿过程可能长达18个月甚至更久。他指出了不同学科的审稿速度差异。

• [y-curious] 认为科学出版中存在“没有负面结果的期刊”这样的偏见，强调如果研究者没有取得突破性进展，就很难发表文章，而这直接影响到他们的职业生存。他还批评了科学界的政治化问题，指出在科学成功的道路上，不仅需要科研能力，还需要政治技巧。

• [jltsiren] 批评了原文作者的观点，认为其观点更像是出自一个行政人员，而不是一线科学家。他指出科学进步依赖于个人信念，而非机构和激励机制。此外，他认为原文中的一些说法以偏概全，比如关于作者支付文章处理费用的讨论，以及科学出版仅关注结果而不是论证过程的观点。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是科学出版过程中的时间问题及其对科研工作的影响。不同学科的审稿周期差异显著，这一问题在讨论中被突出。
• 另一个争议点是负面结果的发表困难，这涉及到科学界的发表激励机制，以及这种机制如何影响研究者的职业发展。
• [jltsiren] 对原文中的一些泛泛而论提出质疑，强调科学界的多样性和复杂性，指出并非所有领域都遵循相同的出版规则和激励机制。
• 科学界的政治化问题也被提及，[y-curious] 认为这是科学成功的一个重要因素，而[jltsiren] 则更强调个人信念和自主性的重要性。

data.title: Reaching my first 100 users without money or audience (at 10K users now)
data.author: felixheikka
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过在社区中互动获取首批用户的可行性及用户转化问题

不同观点：
• MeetingsBrowser认为，这种通过在"Build in Public"和"Startup Community"等社区获取用户的方式，似乎仅对那些目标用户是创始人的产品有效。他质疑这种社区的互动更像是一种自我实现的预言，类似于人们为了拥有一定数量的关注者而互相追随，而非真正基于产品价值。

• chukaebi1对分享的获取首批用户的方法表示赞赏，并关注了应用的付费模式问题，询问应用是付费模式还是免费增值模式，以及在首批100名用户中有多少直接转化为付费用户。

补充讨论：
• MeetingsBrowser提到了具体的用户获取过程，即通过在Reddit上发布想法验证帖，并在两周内通过每日行动获得了前100名用户。他还提出了一个重要问题，即是否区分了为提供反馈而尝试产品的用户和真正持续使用产品的用户。

• 争议的焦点在于"Build in Public"和"Startup Community"等社区的真实价值。MeetingsBrowser认为这些社区可能只是一种社交媒体上的互相追随，而非真正为了产品使用和反馈。

• chukaebi1则更关注实际的商业模式和用户转化率，特别是免费用户向付费用户的转化情况，这表明了他对产品商业可行性的关心。

data.title: Ask HN: How do I learn robotics in 2025?
data.author: srijansriv
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何入门机器人学以及相关的学习资源和方法

不同观点：
• [borjah] 推荐通过免费的ROS2课程入门，并强调多领域融合（软件、硬件、机械）的重要性，建议从嵌入式编码和小型项目开始，逐步学习。
• [amacneil] 强调机器人学与传统软件开发的不同，建议从小型机器人套件或模拟器开始，并提到利用AI工具（如ChatGPT）加速学习，同时推荐了自己开发的工具。
• [ActorNightly] 推荐通过游戏《Stormworks》学习机器人学基础，认为其深度和自动化系统对实际机器人项目有帮助。
• [_tqr3] 建议直接动手实践，从简单的RC车和Arduino项目开始，逐步添加传感器和摄像头等组件。
• [r2_pilot] 强调根据目的设计机器人，建议结合电气和机械工程知识，以减少设计和集成中的错误和时间。
• [TrackerFF] 认为乐高机器人套件适合入门，即使是为孩子设计的，也可以提供有效的学习体验。
• [iancmceachern] 指出当前讨论多聚焦于软件，而硬件同样重要，推荐从Pololu、Adafruit和SparkFun等平台开始学习机械设计和硬件。
• [fusionadvocate] 鼓励梦想大，利用现有的廉价组件（如相机、传感器、电机）构建几乎任何东西，但也提醒避免陷入过度依赖“抽象”和现成SDK的陷阱。
• [scottbez1] 建议直接进入项目，设定合理的期望，理解机器人学的多层复杂性，同时强调动手实践和快速迭代的重要性。
• [beklein] 推荐特定的硬件和软件资源，并提到即将举行的全球黑客松作为入门机会。
• [hugs] 提供了一套从购买3D打印机和电子入门套件到构建玩具机器人的详细步骤，并建议通过销售自制机器人筹集资金。
• [breakds] 建议从学习模拟工具和控制理论开始，然后逐步在实际机器人上部署模型。
• [jmpman] 建议志愿者参与First Robotics团队，通过指导高中生学习机器人学。
• [chasd00] 推荐Adafruit的Feather板和Circuitpython，以避免传统嵌入式编程的复杂性，同时提到Ardupilot作为高级选项。
• [AdobiWanKenobi] 反对进行学位学习，建议直接动手构建项目，强调基础控制工程知识的重要性，并认为过多的数学知识不必要。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：部分评论（如[fusionadvocate]和[scottbez1]）提到机器人学的高门槛和现实世界的不可预测性，与其他评论中提到的轻松入门和利用工具加速学习形成对比。
• 资源推荐：多个评论提供了丰富的学习资源和工具链接，如ROS2课程、模拟器、乐高套件、电子元件供应商和游戏《Stormworks》。
• 动手实践 vs 理论学习：多数评论强调直接动手实践的重要性，但也有评论提醒设定合理期望和理解理论基础的必要性。
• 软件 vs 硬件：讨论中既有对软件开发工具和AI工具的推荐，也有对硬件设计和机械工程的重视，显示出多领域融合的趋势。

data.title: Ask HN: Who wants to be hired? (June 2025)
data.author: whoishiring
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：求职者背景和技术能力

不同观点：
• **jenniferabowd**：具有7年以上全栈开发经验，专注于JavaScript、React和Node，也熟悉Java和Python。重视导师制和代码审查，以帮助团队提升。
• **saveriomazza2**：专注于数据工程和MLOps，拥有5年经验，擅长从数据中提取价值，强调解决方案的可维护性和可扩展性，曾从事银行业和SaaS产品的数据驱动项目。
• **afzal_ali**：来自巴基斯坦，愿意迁移，熟悉Ruby on Rails、React、TypeScript、PHP Laravel等多种技术，寻求匹配其技能的远程职位。
• **csvlewis**：全栈工程师，专注于TypeScript、React、Node.js和PostgreSQL，有快速发展的初创公司远程工作经验，寻求中高级远程职位。
• **SanthoshReddy13**：软件工程师，擅长后端系统和云基础设施，曾构建高流量的微服务和数据管道，寻求以Java或Python为主的 backend 或全栈开发角色。
• **scalewithlee**：拥有8年云基础设施经验，曾是Autodesk的主工程师，擅长设计和实施可扩展的生产系统，关注开发者体验。
• **dserban**：专注于高可扩展的分布式系统，精通Scala、Rust和Python，寻求高薪和股权的高级职位。
• **ProllyInfamous**：作为电工，虽然技术背景不同，但愿意迁移并重新进入大型设施管理领域，不使用电子邮件，依赖传统邮寄方式。
• **alamu**：来自尼日利亚，全栈Java开发人员，专注于构建可扩展和安全的后端服务，参与多个开源项目，寻求远程或迁移机会。
• **evilsaloon**：刚毕业的开发人员，虽然经验较少，但具有广泛的知识和项目经验，如构建大型钻石溶解数据库，寻求入门级职位。
• **walaa_volidis**：来自巴勒斯坦，远程工作，愿意迁移，专注于前端和.NET后端技术，寻求匹配其技能的职位。
• **MHM5000**：高级工程师，专注于Python和Django，有丰富的支付平台设计和扩展经验，寻求高级后端或全栈技术领导职位。
• **whatamidoingyo**：具有10年开发经验，主要作为前端开发人员，有丰富的项目经验如JavaScript Today出版物，寻求远程机会。
• **laconicmatt**：具有多种技术经验，包括移动应用开发和Web开发，寻求有趣的开发工作，无论全栈、前端或后端。

补充讨论：
• **技术栈多样性**：求职者技术栈广泛，涵盖前端、后端、数据工程和云基础设施等多个领域。
• **远程工作偏好**：大多数求职者偏好远程工作，部分愿意迁移。
• **经验层次**：求职者经验层次不一，从刚毕业的入门级开发人员到有丰富经验的高级工程师。
• **职业目标**：求职者的职业目标各异，有的寻求特定技术领域的深入发展，有的寻求广泛的开发经验。
• **迁移意愿**：部分求职者愿意迁移，以寻求更好的职业机会。

争议焦点：
• **薪资和股权要求**：如**dserban**的高薪和股权要求可能在求职过程中引发讨论和谈判。
• **迁移意愿**：部分求职者如**ProllyInfamous**的迁移意愿和特殊背景可能引发对其职位匹配度的讨论。

Onlook for Desktop (aka Onlook Alpha)
We're in early preview for Onlook Web. If you're looking for the downloadable desktop electron app, it's moved to
Onlook Desktop
.
Why are we moving to the web? Read about our decision:
Migrating from Electron to Web
Getting Started
Available soon with a
hosted app
or
run locally
.
Usage
Onlook will run on any Next.js + TailwindCSS project, import your project
through into Onlook or start from scratch within the editor.
Use the AI chat to create or edit a project you're working on. At any time, you can
always right-click an element to open up the exact location of the element in
code.
Draw-in new divs and re-arrange them within their parent containers by dragging-and-dropping.
Preview the code side-by-side with your site design.
Use Onlook's editor toolbar to adjust Tailwind styles, directly manipulate objects, and experiment with layouts.
Documentation
For full documentation, visit
docs.onlook.com
To see how to Contribute, visit
Contributing to Onlook
in our docs.
How it works
When you create an app, we load the code into a web container
The container runs and serves the code
Our editor receives the preview link and displays it in an iFrame
Our editor reads and indexes the code from the container
We instrument the code in order to map elements to their place in code
When the element is edited, we edit the element in our iFrame, then in code
Our AI chat also has code access and tools to understand and edit the code
This architecture can theoretically scale to any language or framework that
displays DOM elements declaratively (e.g. jsx/tsx/html). We are focused on making it work well with Next.js and TailwindCSS for now.
For a full walkthrough, check out our
Architecture Docs
.

data.title: What works (and doesn't) selling formal methods
data.author: azhenley
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：正式方法（Formal Methods）在软件工程中的应用及其成本与效益分析

不同观点：
• agentultra认为正式方法的成本被高估了，尤其是像模型检查（model checking）这样的方法，其成本远低于构建错误的东西。虽然定理证明（theorem proving）需要专业知识，但正式方法的应用可以根据出错成本决定。如果错误代价高昂，那么前期投入更多时间是值得的。
• jiehong则提出模拟测试（simulation testing）在成本与效益上可能比正式方法更合适，并认为正式方法应成为编译器类型系统的一部分，以降低采用成本。他还指出，由于不完备性定理的存在，正式方法在某些方面总是会有局限。
• Taikonerd指出，正式方法需要一个正式的模型，而大多数软件并没有这样的模型。例如部署软件通常没有正式定义的模型，这使得应用正式方法变得困难。
• stereolambda对正式方法在企业环境中的实际应用持怀疑态度，认为抽象和类型系统经常出问题，正式方法可能导致过度复杂的系统。他还提到，某些高风险领域可能需要正式方法，但大多数情况下，人们更愿意使用现有的工具和方法。
• jerf提出，大多数程序的状态空间是指数级增长的，但实际运行的路径是多项式级的。因此，非正式程序员更关注多项式级的状态空间，而正式方法关注的是整个指数级的状态空间，这导致了两者之间的认知差异。
• almostgotcaught认为，正式方法不被广泛采用的原因不仅在于成本，还在于需要对抽象模型的一致认同，且证明语言与编程语言之间的精度差异使得许多东西无法直接翻译。
• freekh则表示，正式方法的成本与效益分析可以类比于其他工程领域，如web应用的开发。
• moi2388以幽默的方式指出，正式方法的时间和成本增加可能导致客户流失。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到正式方法的采用成本和实际应用中的沟通问题，尤其是在团队成员不具备正式思维的情况下，如何确保规范的一致性和可验证性。
• 另一个值得注意的点是，正式方法在某些高风险领域（如航空航天软件）中被认为是必要的，但在大多数常规软件开发中，测试和迭代开发等现有方法通常被认为足够。
• 关于正式方法的局限性，讨论中提到了不完备性定理以及证明语言与编程语言之间的差距，这使得正式方法的应用范围受到一定限制。

争议焦点：
• 正式方法的成本与其带来的效益是否匹配，尤其是在非高风险的常规软件开发中。
• 正式方法在实际应用中需要对抽象模型的一致认同，以及证明语言与编程语言之间的精度差异，这使得其广泛应用面临挑战。

data.title: ReasoningGym: Reasoning Environments for RL with Verifiable Rewards
data.author: t55
data.article_summary: 《REASONING GYM: Reasoning Environments for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards》一文介绍了一个名为Reasoning Gym (RG)的库，专为强化学习中的推理任务设计，具有可验证的奖励机制。RG提供超过100个数据生成器和验证器，涵盖代数、算术、计算、认知、几何、图论、逻辑及多种游戏领域。其主要创新在于通过程序生成几乎无限的训练数据，且复杂度可调，不同于以往固定的推理数据集。实验结果表明，RG在评估和强化学习推理模型方面具有良好效果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NVIDIA的推理模型、RL目标是否涉及真正的“推理”、RL训练中的奖励机制及其有效性

不同观点：
• ninakostoska认为NVIDIA的最新推理模型使用Reasoning Gym作为其数据混合的一部分是令人兴奋的进展，并提供了相关的论文链接。
• phh对将RL目标称为“推理”或“思考”表示质疑，认为这些目标可以在没有真正“思考”模型的情况下实现，同时表达了对Gemini 2.5 Pro在RL任务中表现优越的个人感觉，并希望有一个长期维护的“RL Zoo”项目。
• jimmySixDOF分享了关于在RL训练中使用“Spurious Rewards”的实验结果，展示了即使使用随机或错误的奖励信号，模型在数学基准测试中仍能取得显著进展，并提供了相关研究链接。
• sadboots对过度拟合gsm8k（一个数学问题数据集）表示担忧，呼吁停止这种做法。

补充讨论：
• starzmustdie提供了Reasoning Gym的GitHub链接，为项目提供了实际的代码资源。
• phh提到了希望有一个“RL Zoo”项目，能够长期维护并接受外部贡献，以增加新的RL目标。
• jimmySixDOF的评论引出了关于RL训练中内在反馈（如模型自身的信心）作为奖励信号的讨论，展示了利用内在信号进行无监督学习的可能性。

争议焦点：
• 对于RL目标是否真正涉及“推理”或“思考”存在争议，phh认为当前的模型可能并不具备真正的思考能力。
• 关于在RL训练中使用随机或错误奖励信号是否适当以及其潜在风险的讨论，jimmySixDOF展示了其有效性，但其实际应用价值和可能导致的过拟合问题仍需进一步探讨。
• sadboots对过度拟合特定数据集（gsm8k）的担忧，反映了在模型训练中选择合适数据集和防止过拟合的普遍挑战。

Abstract:
We introduce Reasoning Gym (RG), a library of reasoning environments for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. It provides over 100 data generators and verifiers spanning multiple domains including algebra, arithmetic, computation, cognition, geometry, graph theory, logic, and various common games. Its key innovation is the ability to generate virtually infinite training data with adjustable complexity, unlike most previous reasoning datasets, which are typically fixed. This procedural generation approach allows for continuous evaluation across varying difficulty levels. Our experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of RG in both evaluating and reinforcement learning of reasoning models.

44157077.article_summary: 《REASONING GYM: Reasoning Environments for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards》一文介绍了一个名为Reasoning Gym (RG)的库，专为强化学习中的推理任务设计，具有可验证的奖励机制。RG提供超过100个数据生成器和验证器，涵盖代数、算术、计算、认知、几何、图论、逻辑及多种游戏领域。其主要创新在于通过程序生成几乎无限的训练数据，且复杂度可调，不同于以往固定的推理数据集。实验结果表明，RG在评估和强化学习推理模型方面具有良好效果。
44157077.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NVIDIA的推理模型、RL目标是否涉及真正的“推理”、RL训练中的奖励机制及其有效性

不同观点：
• ninakostoska认为NVIDIA的最新推理模型使用Reasoning Gym作为其数据混合的一部分是令人兴奋的进展，并提供了相关的论文链接。
• phh对将RL目标称为“推理”或“思考”表示质疑，认为这些目标可以在没有真正“思考”模型的情况下实现，同时表达了对Gemini 2.5 Pro在RL任务中表现优越的个人感觉，并希望有一个长期维护的“RL Zoo”项目。
• jimmySixDOF分享了关于在RL训练中使用“Spurious Rewards”的实验结果，展示了即使使用随机或错误的奖励信号，模型在数学基准测试中仍能取得显著进展，并提供了相关研究链接。
• sadboots对过度拟合gsm8k（一个数学问题数据集）表示担忧，呼吁停止这种做法。

补充讨论：
• starzmustdie提供了Reasoning Gym的GitHub链接，为项目提供了实际的代码资源。
• phh提到了希望有一个“RL Zoo”项目，能够长期维护并接受外部贡献，以增加新的RL目标。
• jimmySixDOF的评论引出了关于RL训练中内在反馈（如模型自身的信心）作为奖励信号的讨论，展示了利用内在信号进行无监督学习的可能性。

争议焦点：
• 对于RL目标是否真正涉及“推理”或“思考”存在争议，phh认为当前的模型可能并不具备真正的思考能力。
• 关于在RL训练中使用随机或错误奖励信号是否适当以及其潜在风险的讨论，jimmySixDOF展示了其有效性，但其实际应用价值和可能导致的过拟合问题仍需进一步探讨。
• sadboots对过度拟合特定数据集（gsm8k）的担忧，反映了在模型训练中选择合适数据集和防止过拟合的普遍挑战。

data.title: Reducing Cargo target directory size with -Zno-embed-metadata
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Rust（和Cargo）中`target`目录占用大量磁盘空间的问题，这是Rust用户面临的第三大问题。由于Rust的“一切从源代码构建”的编译模式，以及默认启用的调试信息和增量编译，`target`目录很难变得精简。文章分析了目录中主要占用空间的部分，包括调试信息、增量编译缓存以及编译后的Rust库的元数据。特别是，Cargo的流水线编译会导致每个库的元数据在`.rlib`和`.rmeta`文件中重复存储，进一步增加空间占用。作者提出了一种方法，通过修改编译器参数，使元数据仅存储在`.rmeta`文件中，从而减少目录大小。这一方法旨在解决元数据重复问题，从而有效减少`target`目录的总体大小。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cargo团队是否应将`.rlib`文件中的元数据视为公共API的一部分，进而决定其变更是否构成向后兼容性破坏。

不同观点：
• KolmogorovComp认为，将`.rlib`文件中的元数据视为公共API的一部分是荒谬的。他指出，即使有人依赖这些元数据，只要未被文档化，就不应视为破坏性变更。他强调，未被正式记录的功能不应具有与公共API相同的保障。

• 另一方观点（ implied by KolmogorovComp’s statement）是Cargo团队正在考虑将这些元数据视为公共API的一部分，因为担心有人可能已经依赖于这些元数据的存在。这种观点倾向于更为保守的变更管理，以避免对现有用户造成意外影响。

补充讨论：
• 讨论的焦点在于对公共API的定义，以及开发团队在处理未被文档化的实现细节时的责任。KolmogorovComp的观点强调了文档化的重要性，认为没有文档化的特性不应被默认为受保障的API。

• 另一个值得注意的点是Cargo团队的谨慎态度，表明他们在做出任何可能影响向后兼容性的决定时非常小心，尽管这可能导致在处理未文档化依赖时的复杂性。

44158720.article_content:
Disk usage of the
target
directory is a commonly cited annoyance with Rust (and Cargo)
– in the last year’s
Annual Survey
,
it was the third most pressing issue of Rust users, right after slow compilation
1
and subpar
debugging experience. Given the “build everything from source” compilation model of Rust, and both debuginfo and incremental compilation being enabled by default in the
dev
Cargo profile, it is unlikely that the
target
directory will ever become
lean
and small. However, there are still ways of how we could reduce the
target
directory size by a non-trivial amount. I will describe a brand-new method of achieving that in this blog post.
Note that there are also initiatives to reduce the size of the
target
directory along the temporal axis, i.e. prevent it from ballooning over time (see
Cargo Garbage Collection
). This post is more about how to reduce the size of the target directory overall.
What takes up the space, anyway?
It is not the focus of this post to dive deep into exploring what exactly takes space in the
target
directory, but I still think that it is useful to provide at least some background on this. I took
my favourite work project,
hyperqueue
, and compiled
it in several modes to compare the resulting
target
directory sizes
2
, using
rustc 1.89.0-nightly (2eef47813 2025-05-22)
:
Optimizations
Incremental
Debuginfo
target
size [MiB]
No (
dev
)
No
No
462
No (
dev
)

No (
dev
)

870
No (
dev
)

release
)

From the results, it’s clear that both debuginfo and incremental compilation caches take a lot of
space on disk. It might be that we could do something to reduce either of these, but there is one
additional thing that (kind of unnecessarily) causes
target
directory bloat, which is not
easily observable in this table, and that is the metadata of the compiled Rust crates.
Cargo pipelining & metadata duplication
First, we need to briefly talk about how Rust compilation works (in very, very simplified terms).
When a Rust library crate (
rlib
) is compiled in a “standard” way (i.e. no
LTO
or other funny
business) with Cargo, the compiler generates (amongst other things) two main outputs:
Metadata, which contains information necessary to link to that crate from other Rust code.
Object code, which is the compiled assembly code of the Rust crate.
The interesting thing about this is that the final object code isn’t actually needed in order to start
compiling Rust code that depends on a said library, metadata is enough (the object code will only be
needed at the final linking step). Cargo makes use of this fact, and when it compiles your crate graph,
it uses a technique called
pipelining
.
Imagine that you have a binary that depends on crate
B
, which itself depends on crate
A
. When
compiling
A
, Cargo will tell the compiler (using
--emit=metadata,...
) to emit a
.rmeta
file
containing the metadata of
A
as soon as possible. Once that file is ready, we can start compiling
B
by passing it the
.rmeta
file of
A
, even though the object code of
A
is not ready yet,
and thus partially overlap the compilation of both crates, which improves compile times. I will borrow
(and slightly extend) a cute ASCII diagram from
Alex Crichton’s internals post
about pipelining
to succintly show how it works:
--- .rmeta of A generated
v
[-libA----|--------]
[-libB----|--------]
[-binary-----------]
0s        5s       10s       15s                25s
Pipelining has been enabled in Cargo for many years, so it’s nothing new, and if you use Cargo, you
are using pipelining every day, perhaps without even knowing about it. However, there is one
suboptimal thing in regard to disk space usage with the pipelining approach.
The problem is that once the process finishes, you will be left with two copies of the metadata of
each library on disk. The first copy is in the final
.rlib
file (along with the object code), and
the second copy is in the
.rmeta
file. As is usual with Cargo, this problem will balloon if you build
your project with multiple configuration options (different Cargo profiles, different compiler/linker
flags, etc.).
A related issue is that if you are compiling a library as a
dylib
,
so that you generate a Rust dynamic library (e.g.
.so
on Linux), that will also contain the
metadata, even though it should not be required to actually consume (call functions from) the
library at runtime. This can be annoying for people who ship Rust
dylib
s, even though that’s
usually not very common due to Rust currently not having a stable
ABI
.
Avoiding duplicated metadata
So, what can we do about it? Well, last year, I noticed that many years ago, the illustrious
@bjorn3
has
proposed
an idea to introduce a compiler flag
that would cause the metadata to
only
be included in the
.rmeta
files, and no longer be present
in the
.rlib/.so
library files. I liked this idea, and since there already was a
prototype
implementation
prepared, it didn’t seem that hard to push it over the finish line.

data.title: The Atomic Airplane
data.author: mpweiher
data.article_summary: 《核动力飞机的故事》讲述了1980年代飞机核推进计划的老兵们录制了近13小时的演示和访谈，介绍研制核动力飞机的努力，重点是热传导反应堆实验（HTREs），这些反应堆现存于爱达荷州EBR-I博物馆停车场。MIT的Jake Hecla博士在John Webb等人帮助下将这些资料数字化。该项目始于1946年至1951年，探索了多种核反应堆和动力装置设计，最终决定使用喷气发动机。1951年，GEANP开始开发直接循环概念，利用反应堆直接加热空气。项目进行了HTRE-1、HTRE-2和HTRE-3等实验，测试不同燃料和设计。然而，到1961年，由于导弹和核潜艇等竞争性武器系统的发展，核动力飞机项目被取消。文章还描述了计划中的Convair NX-2核动力飞机模型和相关技术细节。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：核动力飞行器的历史、实际应用及相关争议

不同观点：
• **支持与兴趣**：[acidburnNSA] 对核动力飞行器表示兴趣，并分享了1950年代的相关数字化报告和博客链接，显示出对这一历史技术的关注和认可。[t1234s] 提到了UFO研究员Stanton Freedman参与核动力飞机项目，暗示这种技术曾被认真研究过。[webdoodle] 补充说在爱达荷国家实验室可以看到核动力飞机的引擎展示，进一步证实了该技术的历史存在。

• **反对与质疑**：[krunck] 认为核动力飞机是不应被建造的，同时提到了超音速低空导弹，表达了对这类军事科技的反对态度。[loph] 提到乔治亚核飞行器实验室，并指出该地区仍有辐射，暗示核动力项目可能带来的长期环境和健康风险。

• **历史与文化兴趣**：[petalmind] 分享了1957年苏联关于核动力飞机的书籍扫描，展示了这一技术在冷战时期的国际研究背景。[christkv] 认为核动力飞机设计属于最具放射性尘降物设计理念之一，强调了其历史和技术背景。

• **技术发展与未来**：[glimshe] 提出问题，询问是否仍在研究核动力飞机等未来科技，同时提到了曾经被视为未来主义的窗口用户界面。这显示了对当前科技发展方向的思考和疑问。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了多个历史和现代的相关链接与资源，如视频、博客和维基百科页面，提供了进一步了解核动力飞机的资料。[waffletower] 的评论则是对流行文化的引用，与讨论主题相关性较弱。

争议焦点：核动力飞机的技术可行性、安全性及其对环境和健康的潜在影响是评论中争议的焦点。

44130915.article_content:
The Story of the Atomic Airplane
In 1980s, veterans of the Aircraft Nuclear Propulsion program got together and
recorded nearly 13 hours of presentations and interviews describing the amazing
effort to make a nuclear-powered airplane.  The content is mostly focused on the
Heat Transfer Reactor Experiments (HTREs) which can still be seen sitting out in
the parking lot of the EBR-I museum in Idaho.
Dr. Jake Hecla, Stanton Postdoctoral Fellow at MIT, digitized this material with
the help of John Webb. The people who saved this film and got it to Dr. Hecla
are Lee Hite and David Carpenter. The late John Webb (W7NWH), Otto Woike, George
Pomeroy, and Gunnar Thornton contributed to the development and preservation of
this film.
This page contains a full transcript of the recordings with links to the specific
timestamps in the films.
Parts 1-4
Parts 5-7
For a more âvividâ view of the project, make sure to check out
this 1960 film
we got digitized showing the actual hardware these guys are talking about:
1 Intro
01:40
From 1946 through 51, the Fairchild Airplane Company conducted feasibility studies for nuclear propulsion for aircraft, or NEPA. Various cycles, power plants, and nuclear reactors were explored. Among the decisions was that the jet engine, still in its infancy, was to be used. In 1951, a decision was made that GEANP was to develop the direct cycle concept where the air from the compressor
02:09
was heated directly by the reactor fuel elements. Major elements of the ANP program are shown on the chart. During the 1951-53 early nuclear flight was an objective to determine operational feasibility of a nuclear-powered aircraft. The test aircraft was to be a B-36.
02:33
The power plant consisted of four modified J-47s designated the X-39. The energy was supplied by one R-1 reactor. The R-1 was water-moderated and had an aluminum structure. The fuel element consisted of a 310 stainless steel plus UO2 matrix, which was clad with stainless steel. The program was redirected in early 1953. Three heat transfer reactor experiments, HTREs, followed.
03:04
From 1952 through 61, the divided shield design was validated and various shield materials were tested in the tower shield facility at Oak Ridge. Also, 40 test flights of a B-36 with a small 2-megawatt thermal reactor aboard were conducted by Convair at Fort Worth. On January 31st of 1956, in the HTRE 1,
03:31
The first jet engine operated on nuclear power at the National Reactor Test Station in Idaho. The fuel material was nichrome plus UO2. Tests began in 1957 of the HTRE 2. It was similar in design to the HTRE 1, but with an 11-inch hole in the center of the core, where advanced fuel element and moderator designs were tested until 1961.
03:58
The HTRE 3 was built in a full-scale aircraft reactor configuration. It was tested using an air-cooled solid moderator, zirconium hydride, and nichrome with a few elements. Two X-39 engines were operated at full power. Nuclear starts were demonstrated. From 1956 through 59, the XMA-1A development program was to meet the Air Force Camel mission.
04:27
including supersonic sprint. New twin X-211 engines shared a reactor between them. A new solid moderator of yttrium hydride with capability of 2,300 degrees Fahrenheit was developed. However, the advanced fuel element, though structurally improved, did not yet have the capability of 1,800 degrees Fahrenheit turbine inlet temperature.
04:55
By 1959, development tests demonstrated that a BEO ceramic reactor would meet the 1,800 degree Fahrenheit turbine inlet temperature. The XNJ-140 power plant had one X-211 engine with a ceramic reactor. It provided 100 megawatts at cruise conditions. By March 1961, other competitive weapons systems such as missiles and nuclear submarines
05:24
had obviated the need for a nuclear-powered aircraft. Therefore, the A&P program was canceled. This is a model of a nuclear-powered jet engine, the XNJ-140. It is one-tenth scale. The actual engine was 37 feet in length. This is the compressor, the reactor with the shield assembly, the combustor,
05:53
the turbine, and the nozzle. By the end of 1960, 11 builds of the turbine machinery did operate in Cincinnati on chemical fuel. The XNJ-140 was scheduled to operate on nuclear power in 1962 at the National Reactor Test Station in Idaho.
06:33
This is a model of the Convair NX-2 aircraft. It was to fly in 1965. The canard configuration is well suited for a nuclear-powered aircraft. There are three XNJ-140 engines at the rear of the fuselage where they're accessible for remote handling and maintenance. 100 feet forward is the crew compartment, which is shielded.
07:03
Air inlets to the engines are located at the base of the wings. J-75s are mounted in pods and are used for takeoff only in the event of a loss of an engine. The hangar to house this aircraft and provide the remote maintenance was constructed in Idaho by April of 1961 when the Aircraft Nuclear Propulsion Program
07:33
was cancelled.

44130915.article_summary: 《核动力飞机的故事》讲述了1980年代飞机核推进计划的老兵们录制了近13小时的演示和访谈，介绍研制核动力飞机的努力，重点是热传导反应堆实验（HTREs），这些反应堆现存于爱达荷州EBR-I博物馆停车场。MIT的Jake Hecla博士在John Webb等人帮助下将这些资料数字化。该项目始于1946年至1951年，探索了多种核反应堆和动力装置设计，最终决定使用喷气发动机。1951年，GEANP开始开发直接循环概念，利用反应堆直接加热空气。项目进行了HTRE-1、HTRE-2和HTRE-3等实验，测试不同燃料和设计。然而，到1961年，由于导弹和核潜艇等竞争性武器系统的发展，核动力飞机项目被取消。文章还描述了计划中的Convair NX-2核动力飞机模型和相关技术细节。

44170624.article_content:
NASA continues to make groundbreaking discoveries. Among its recent findings was
the cause and timetable for life on Earth coming to an end
. According to the chilling study by Toho University, life on Earth will end due to the loss of oxygen. But don't worry, that won't happen for at least another billion years.
In addition, NASA has made other concerning findings. One of them included the
Colorado River Basin, and how it is emptying at an alarming rate
. Now, the Three Gorges Dam isn't facing these types of issues. However, according to NASA, the massive Dam in China might be altering global time-keeping and the Earth's rotation.
​​​​​​​We'll take a closer look at the findings and other factors that are tampering with the Earth's rotation.
Related
NASA Satellites' Recent Discovery In The Colorado River Basin Has Scientists Worried About The Future
NASA satellites have detected a significant issue in the Colorado River Basin.
Posts
Three Gorges Dam May Increase The Length Of A Day By 0.06 Microseconds, According To NASA
A human-made structure that's altering the Earth's rotation? Yes, that's what NASA has concluded in one of its latest findings. China's Three Gorges Dam is the largest hydroelectric dam, which influences both global dynamics and mass energy production. Its movements are so powerful that it can impact the entire Earth's rotation in microseconds.
To put this into context, if the Three Gorges Dam were filled with 10 trillion gallons of water, this would, in turn, increase the length of a day by 0.06 microseconds. Sure, that isn't much, but given its impact on the Earth's rotation, it is pretty mind-blowing to think about.
NASA has continued with studies related to the Earth's changing rotation. Climate change has also played a significant role in recent developments.
Close
NASA Added That The Earth's Rotation Is Also Changing Due To Climate Change
Thanks to more than 120 years of data,
NASA
was able to link climate change to the Earth's changing rotation.
Factors Include:
Melting ice
Dwindling groundwater
Rising sea levels
Research from Nature's "
Contributions of core, mantle and climatological processes to Earth’s polar motion"
confirmed that, since 2000, days are 1.33 milliseconds longer per 100 years. Glaciers melting in Antarctica and Greenland are believed to be caused by human-created greenhouse emissions.
Related
NASA Confirms The Cause And Timetable For Life Ending On Earth With Chilling Toho University Study
According to research conducted by NASA, life on Earth will not end due to an asteroid.

Users online had a lot to say about
NASA's recent findings
. There was a mix of reactions, ranging from mild to strong. We saw users showcase their sense of humor on the matter, while others believe the issue will only intensify heading into the future.
Users React To NASA's Time Disruption Discovery:
"For reference, this amounts to a bit more than 3 days over the entire age of the universe."
"For reference. 0.06 microseconds is the amount of time that passes before you get honked at from behind after the traffic light turned green."
"Moving that much water upwards is analogous to a figure skater moving their arms outward while spinning. They slow down. Since earth is a closed (mass) system, when trillions of pounds of water are elevated, conservation of momentum cancels the mass redistribution on a rotating body by affecting its rotational speed."
"It's a very easy calculation based on angular momentum. to clarify, this is not much an interesting fact (to me as an engineer anyway). all dams do this. building a skyscraper does this. any time you move mass to higher elevation this happens. this only difference is whether it's 0.00000006 seconds or some other equally irrelevant amount."
"All that water....lots of it...is now held up high, rather than flowing to the sea. Higher altitude means further from the axis of rotation. Like moving further out on a playground roundabout, or a figure skater sticking their arms out when they're doing a twirly thing."
