• yooo000：对好莱坞电影普遍不满，认为缺乏深度和意义。
• ddanielsantos：认为安德森的最近三部电影缺乏灵魂，甚至开玩笑说他可能被AI取代。
• pursuableproofs：喜欢早期的作品如《Rushmore》、《特南鲍姆一家》、《Life Aquatic》，但认为新作的单调 delivery 和缺乏配乐削弱了戏剧性和吸引力。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于安德森的风格是否变得过于重复和缺乏情感深度。
• 一些评论者认为安德森早期的作品更具人性化和真实情感，而后来的作品则显得过于机械和形式化。
• 有评论者建议安德森尝试新的风格和格式，以丰富其电影作品的多样性。
• 也有评论者对安德森的新作持积极态度，认为其作品在视觉和情感上都达到了高水平。

Wes Anderson
’s new film, “The Phoenician Scheme,” is a funny-ha-ha comedy, but there’s nothing funny about its story, which involves a wealthy industrialist’s attempts to realize a grandiose infrastructure project. Anderson’s signature is instantly recognizable in the movie’s decorative production design, its frontal and symmetrical framings, and its antic, densely plotted story—and equally in the fact that it is a violent and death-haunted action film, filled with fights and chases. Yet, compared with “
The Grand Budapest Hotel
” (2014) and the work that has followed, the new film is relatively simple: rather than nesting stories within other stories, it follows its protagonist closely. The result is a heightened clarity—revealing the distinctive world view that Anderson’s methods embody—and an unusually direct emotionalism.
“The Phoenician Scheme” is the story of an amusingly bad man who becomes a little less amusing and a little less bad. Benicio del Toro, alternately glowering and glib, stars as Anatole (Zsa-zsa) Korda, an Onassis-like figure of uninhibited ruthlessness. The action, which runs from 1950 to late 1951, begins as Zsa-zsa, a proud citizen of no country, flits about in a private Air Korda plane that he knows to be a target of saboteurs. Sure enough, mid-flight, a hole is blown in the fuselage, and Zsa-zsa, taking the controls, crash-lands the plane. Unconscious, he has a near-death experience—filmed in black-and-white with a sense of both comedy and wonderment—in which he arrives in a cotton-puff Heaven under the severe scrutiny of a berobed gatekeeper (played by Willem Dafoe).
Badly wounded, Zsa-zsa recuperates in his sixteenth-century Italian palazzo, and summons his twenty-year-old daughter, Liesl (Mia Threapleton), a novitiate nun. She’s the eldest of his ten children (the other nine are boys), and he wants her to renounce her vocation and become the heir to his enterprises, at a critical moment. A grand project in the fictitious country of Phoenicia, thirty years in the making—involving a canal, a tunnel, a railroad line, and a dam—may finally be coming to fruition, and Zsa-zsa, who is set to get five per cent of the profits, will stop at nothing to realize it. The film sardonically conjures a golden age of interventionist arrogance. Though there’s no explicit mention of the Cold War, there’s plenty of espionage and intrigue. Zsa-zsa’s many enemies include American secret agents, an international business consortium, and a well-armed band of revolutionaries, led by a man named Sergio (Richard Ayoade). Zsa-zsa’s scheme comes at a high human cost: it may bring modernization to Phoenicia, but it will depend on slave labor. This doesn’t trouble his conscience any more than does his reputation for financial misdeeds. But the scheme puts several targets on his back: governments and corporate entities see him as a loose cannon, and the revolutionaries see him as a predator.
It’s no wonder that Zsa-zsa is accustomed to assassination attempts. At meals, he puts a drop of reagent into his drinks, and he is unruffled when one turns out to be poisoned. He is at home with violence, literally: he keeps a box full of hand grenades nearby at all times and offers them to guests as if they were cigars or chocolates. He endures danger, such as a submersion in quicksand, with gruff equanimity. He also keeps his cool in heated dealings with a far-flung cast of associates whose backing he needs: with Prince Farouk (Riz Ahmed), he faces two Americans (Tom Hanks and Bryan Cranston) in a high-stakes basketball shoot-out; he takes a bullet for Marseille Bob (Mathieu Amalric) in the Frenchman’s Art Deco night club; he negotiates with the Newark Syndicate’s hipster representative, Marty (Jeffrey Wright), with the aid of deadly force. Closer to home, he hopes to marry a rich second cousin, Hilda Sussman-Korda (Scarlett Johansson), and seeks the support of an estranged half brother, called Uncle Nubar (Benedict Cumberbatch).
This last relationship becomes particularly fraught. Zsa-zsa has outlived all three of his wives, including Liesl’s mother, and Liesl has heard rumors that he killed her, or had her killed. When she confronts him, he pins the blame on Nubar, and Liesl demands that her uncle be punished. (Threapleton, in her first major feature-film role, has a striking presence, both quietly fierce and effortlessly wry.) Thus the movie’s financial and martial machinations take place within a more elemental family drama: in order to win his daughter’s allegiance and affection, Zsa-zsa must pursue a mock-Shakespearean plot of fratricidal revenge. “The Phoenician Scheme” is Anderson’s most sentimental movie—the story of a merciless man so desperate for his devout daughter’s love that he’s willing to kill for it.

data.title: JVM Runtime Parametric Type Support
data.author: agluszak
data.article_summary:
这篇文章提出了对JVM规范的扩展，以支持在运行时传递泛型类型的参数信息，特别是当值类被用作类型参数时（如`List<LocalDate>`）。主要目标是在保持与现有字节码完全向后兼容的情况下，支持方法调用和参数化类实例化的类型参数传递，并提供访问运行时类型信息的API。

关键改动包括：

1. **方法调用端的参数传递**：
   - 引入`ACC_SIDE_VALUE`标记方法，允许传递类型参数。
   - 使用`wide`指令前缀方法调用指令以传递参数值。
   - 提供`currentSideValue()`方法在调用方法内获取传递的参数值。

2. **参数化类实例化**：
   - 引入`ACC_PARAMETRIC`标记类，支持参数化实例化。
   - 使用新的`anew_parametric`指令创建参数化类实例。
   - 提供`currentMetadata()`方法获取类的元数据。

这些扩展允许在运行时保留泛型类型信息，而不改变现有的类型擦除机制。

Hello,
this is a small proposal to try start (re-start) discussions about what would be the minimal changes of the JVM spec enabling java.util collections to be specialized at runtime when value classes are used as type arguments (by example a List<LocalDate>).
regards,
Rémi
---
# Java Virtual Machine Specification Extension: Runtime Parametric Type Support
## 1. Introduction
This specification defines extensions to the Java Virtual Machine to support runtime propagation of type arguments for parametric (generic) classes and methods. While maintaining full backward compatibility with existing bytecode, these extensions enable type arguments to be available at runtime through two primary mechanisms: method call side value and parametric class instantiation.
### 1.1 Goals
- Propagate type arguments at runtime while preserving type erasure compilation
- Maintain complete backward compatibility with existing bytecode
- Support both parametric method calls and parametric class instantiation
- Provide clean APIs for accessing runtime type information
### 1.2 Overview
The specification introduces:
- A method modifier for method supporting side value
- Reuse the opcode wide to specify method call side value
- An API method "currentSideValue" to get the side value associated to a method call inside the callee
- A new class modifier for parametric class
- A new opcode anew_parametric for parametric Class instantiation (to send the layout + metadata)
- An API method "currentMetadata" to get the metadata inside a parametric class
---
## 2. Class File Format Extensions
### 2.1 Access Flags
Two new access flags are introduced:
#### 2.1.1 ACC_SIDE_VALUE (new_flag)
- **Applicable to**: Methods
- **Purpose**: Indicates that a method accepts a side value (type arguments) from callers
- **Behavior**: Enables `wide` method calls and access to `currentSideValue()` within the method
#### 2.1.2 ACC_PARAMETRIC (new_flag)
- **Applicable to**: Classes
- **Purpose**: Indicates that a class supports parametric instantiation
- **Behavior**: Enables `anew_parametric` instruction and access to `currentMetadata()`
### 2.2 Flag Validation
- Methods with `ACC_SIDE_VALUE` must be declared to handle side value parameters
- Classes with `ACC_PARAMETRIC` must support the `LayoutHandle` interface for instantiation
- These flags are ignored by JVM implementations that do not support this extension
---
## 3. Method Call Side Value
### 3.1 Concept
Method call side value enable the passing of an object (type arguments) from a call site to the callee method at runtime. This mechanism simulates generic type parameter passing without modifying method signatures.
### 3.2 Method Declaration
Methods that accept a side value must be marked with the `ACC_SIDE_VALUE` access flag:
```java
// Conceptual representation
public static ACC_SIDE_VALUE void message(String message) {
Object sideValue = currentSideValue();
...
}
```
### 3.3 Bytecode Instructions
#### 3.3.1 Wide Prefix for Method Calls
The `wide` instruction is extended to prefix method call instructions when side values are passed:
**Syntax:**
```
wide <method_call_instruction>
```
**Supported Instructions:**
- `invokestatic`
- `invokevirtual`
- `invokespecial`
- `invokeinterface`
- `invokedynamic`
#### 3.3.2 Stack Layout
When using `wide` with method calls, an additional argument must be present on the stack:
**Stack (top to bottom):**
```
[method arguments...]
[side value (Object)]
```
**Example Bytecode:**
```bytecode
ldc "TypeArgument"     // Push side value
ldc "hello"            // Push method argument
wide
invokestatic Foo.message(Ljava/lang/String;)V
```

#### 3.4.1 currentSideValue() Method
**Signature:** `public static Object currentSideValue()`
**Behavior:**
- Returns the side value passed to the current method
- Returns `null` if the method was called without `wide`
- Must only be called within methods marked `ACC_SIDE_VALUE`
**Exceptions:**
- `LinkageError`: Thrown if called from a method not marked `ACC_SIDE_VALUE`
#### 3.4.2 Call Resolution
1. When `wide` prefixes a method call, the JVM pops the side value from the stack
2. The side value is made available to the target method via `currentSideValue()`
3. The method call proceeds normally with remaining stack arguments
4. If the target method is not marked `ACC_SIDE_VALUE`, a `VerifyError` is thrown

## 4. Parametric Class Instantiation
### 4.1 Concept
Parametric class instantiation allows objects to be created with associated type metadata that remains accessible throughout the object's lifetime.
### 4.2 Class Declaration
Classes supporting parametric instantiation must be marked with the `ACC_PARAMETRIC` access flag and work with the `LayoutHandle` interface.

data.author: samizdis
data.article_summary: 本文提出了一种替代大爆炸理论的新模型，认为宇宙可能起源于一个巨大黑洞内部的反弹，而非传统认为的奇点爆发。作者Enrique Gaztanaga及其团队在《Physical Review D》发表的论文中，基于已知物理学和观测结果，提出宇宙的起源可以通过物质在高密度下坍缩形成黑洞，随后在内部反弹并扩张来解释。这一模型试图解决标准宇宙学模型中关于奇点、暗能量和宇宙膨胀等未解之谜。通过引入量子力学效应，他们发现坍缩不必导致奇点，而是可能引发宇宙的新生阶段。这一理论挑战了传统观点，提供了一个不依赖未知场和新成分的宇宙起源解释。

The Big Bang is often described as the explosive birth of the universe – a singular moment when space, time and matter sprang into existence. But what if this was not the beginning at all? What if our universe emerged from something else – something more familiar and radical at the same time?
In a new paper,
published in Physical Review D
, my colleagues and I propose a striking alternative. Our calculations suggest the Big Bang was not the start of everything, but rather the outcome of a gravitational crunch or collapse that formed a very massive black hole – followed by a bounce inside it.
This idea, which we call the black hole universe, offers a radically different view of cosmic origins, yet it is grounded entirely in known physics and observations.
Today’s
standard cosmological model
, based on the Big Bang and cosmic inflation (the idea that the early universe rapidly blew up in size), has been remarkably successful in explaining the structure and evolution of the universe. But it comes at a price: it leaves some of the most fundamental questions unanswered.
Get your news from actual experts, straight to your inbox.
Sign up to our daily newsletter
to receive all The Conversation UK’s latest coverage of news and research, from politics and business to the arts and sciences.
For one, the Big Bang model begins with a singularity – a point of infinite density
where the laws of physics break down
. This is not just a technical glitch; it’s a deep theoretical problem that suggests we don’t really understand the beginning at all.
To explain the universe’s large-scale structure, physicists introduced a brief phase of rapid expansion into the early universe called
cosmic inflation
, powered by an unknown field with strange properties. Later, to explain the accelerating expansion observed today, they added another “mysterious” component:
dark energy
.
In short, the standard model of cosmology works well – but only
by introducing new ingredients
we have never observed directly. Meanwhile, the most basic questions remain open: where did everything come from? Why did it begin this way? And why is the universe so flat, smooth, and large?
New model
Our new model tackles these questions from a different angle – by looking inward instead of outward. Instead of starting with an expanding universe and trying to trace back how it began, we consider what happens when an overly dense collection of matter collapses under gravity.
This is a familiar process: stars collapse into black holes, which are among the most well-understood objects in physics. But what happens inside a black hole, beyond the event horizon from which nothing can escape, remains a mystery.
In 1965, the British physicist Roger Penrose proved that under very general conditions,
gravitational collapse must lead to a singularity
. This result,
extended by the late British physicist Stephen Hawking and others
, underpins the idea that singularities – like the one at the Big Bang – are unavoidable.
The idea helped win Penrose a share of the 2020 Nobel prize in physics and inspired Hawking’s global bestseller
A Brief History of Time: From the Big Bang to Black Holes
. But there’s a caveat. These “singularity theorems” rely on “classical physics” which describes ordinary macroscopic objects. If we include the effects of quantum mechanics, which rules the tiny microcosmos of atoms and particles, as we must at extreme densities, the story may change.
In
our new paper
, we show that gravitational collapse does not have to end in a singularity. We find an exact analytical solution – a mathematical result with no approximations. Our maths show that as we approach the potential singularity, the size of the universe changes as a (hyperbolic) function of cosmic time.
This simple mathematical solution describes how a collapsing cloud of matter can reach a high-density state and then bounce, rebounding outward into a new expanding phase.

data.title: Typing 118 WPM broke my brain in the right ways
data.author: b0a04gl
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者通过一年时间将打字速度从60 WPM提高到118 WPM的经历，以及这一过程如何帮助他提升了工作效率和心理状态。作者起初打字缓慢，感到挫败，后来通过每天早晨打字五分钟作为大脑重置的仪式，逐渐提高了速度和准确性。他放弃了传统的手指摆放规则，找到了自己的打字节奏。打字速度的提升不仅让他在写代码和文档时更加高效，还帮助他在思维混乱或遇到困难时恢复专注。最终，这一习惯让他成为更出色的开发者，减少了工作中的挫败感。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：打字速度及其在开发和其他职业中的重要性，是否需要遵循"正确的"打字方式

不同观点：
• **支持"正确"打字方式**：dawnofdusk认为打字的"正确方式"（如使用标准指法）是有价值的，并且可以通过练习达到150+wpm的高速度和准确性。这种观点强调了通过学习标准技术可以提高打字效率。

• **反对"正确"打字方式的必要性**：JohnMakin和capitanazo77等人认为，打字的"正确方式"只是建议，而非必须。JohnMakin通过自己不按标准指法但依然达到高速度的例子，说明只要方法适合自己，不必拘泥于标准方式。capitanazo77则推荐使用vim等工具，认为工具和习惯可以直接提升效率。

• **打字速度对开发者的影响**：smithkl42指出，优秀的开发者不仅打字快，还熟练使用各种快捷键，能够快速在IDE中导航。这表明打字速度和效率在开发工作中具有实际意义。

• **自我发展的打字风格**：JohnMakin和rudimentary_phy分享了他们通过玩MMO游戏（如Everquest）发展出的自我打字风格。这种非正式学习的方式让他们达到了较高的打字速度，但带有个人独特的"坏习惯"。

• **打字速度对非编程职业的影响**：MollyRealized作为法律行政人员，提到打字速度在初期是优势，但过快的打字速度可能导致在商务环境中产生过于详细的文档，反而不利。

• **打字速度的局限性**：kendalf89和ryandrake提到，尽管经过打字课程和长期练习，他们的打字速度依然较低，且这并未显著影响他们的编程能力。这暗示打字速度可能并不是所有职业或任务中的关键技能。

补充讨论：
• **打字方式与健康问题**：ashwinsundar分享了使用人体工学键盘和调整打字方式后，缓解了手腕疼痛的经历，强调了打字方式对健康的影响。

• **工具和练习平台的推荐**：thu询问如何在学习触摸打字时引入符号和数字，haneul则推荐了Monkeytype作为优于keybr的打字练习工具，提供了更多选项和模式。

争议焦点：
• **是否需要遵循"正确"的打字方式**：dawnofdusk支持学习标准打字方式，而JohnMakin等人则认为只要方法有效，不必拘泥于标准方式。

• **打字速度对不同职业和任务的重要性**：不同用户对打字速度在各自工作中的实际影响有不同看法，有些人认为非常重要，而另一些人则认为影响有限。

44162327.article_content:
← Back to all posts
Typing 118 WPM Broke My Brain in the Right Ways (A Year-Long Journey)
June 2, 2025
•
6 min read
Productivity
Typing became my therapy. Not even kidding.
Started at 60 WPM, felt like dragging my feet through mud every time I had to write code comments or documentation. Now? 118 WPM. No home row bullshit. No "proper finger placement." Just pure, chaotic rhythm.
Proof here
because I know you don't believe me.
My Daily Brain Reset Ritual
Every morning, before I even think about opening VS Code, before Slack starts destroying my soul, before the daily standup where we pretend we know what we're doing, I just
type
. Five minutes. That's it.
It's like meditation but actually useful. Resets my brain, calms the static from yesterday's debugging session, and gets me in the zone. Way better than staring at my ceiling wondering why I chose this career.
Speed is Useless if You're Wrong
Here's the thing that took me way too long to figure out: rushing makes everything worse. Every time I tried to go fast, I'd mess up, backspace like crazy, and end up slower than when I started. Classic developer move, honestly.
So I slowed down. Focused on hitting every key right. And boom — speed just... happened. 90 WPM, 100 WPM, 118 WPM. All came when I was hitting 100% accuracy consistently.
It's like debugging. You can't just randomly change stuff and hope it works. You gotta be methodical, get it right, then optimize. Same energy.
Some words still absolutely wreck me though. "Obviously" keeps coming out as "obviousily" and I want to throw my keyboard every time. So now I just slow down for those demon words and blast through the rest. Strategic speed management or whatever.
Screw the Rules, Find Your Flow
Plot twist: I don't type "correctly" at all. My fingers just go wherever they want. It's like anarchist typing. My left pinky probably hasn't touched the 'A' key in months, but somehow I'm still in the 99.5 percentile.
Turns out the "proper way" is just a suggestion. Like following PEP 8 or using semicolons in JavaScript. Sure, it's nice, but if your way works better, who cares?
When Your Brain is Fried
You know those days when you've been staring at the same bug for 3 hours and your brain feels like mush? Or when you've been doomscrolling Twitter instead of working and feel dead inside?
That's when I open
Keybr
. It's like going to the gym but for your neurons. Good typing session = instant mood boost. Small win = dopamine hit. Better than coffee, honestly.
Sometimes I use it as a break between coding sessions. Brain getting foggy? Type for 2 minutes. Stuck on a problem? Type. Deployment failed and you want to quit tech forever? You guessed it.
The Inevitable Skill Issue Moments
Not gonna lie, there were weeks where I absolutely tanked. Bad accuracy, slow speeds, feeling like I'd forgotten how to use a keyboard. Classic imposter syndrome but for typing.
"Maybe I'm not actually good at this. Maybe 118 WPM was just a fluke. Maybe I should just stick to hunt-and-peck like a normal person."
But then I'd bounce back. Always. Usually harder and faster than before. It's like when you're stuck on a bug for days and then suddenly the solution is obvious. The struggle makes the breakthrough better.
The Numbers Don't Lie
Been doing this for over a year now. 7,000+ lessons completed on Keybr. My brain genuinely feels different. Not just the typing speed, but focus, discipline, the ability to sit down and just
do the thing
.
It's one of those weird habits that seems pointless but somehow fixes everything else. Like how learning vim makes you better at thinking about text editing, or how writing tests makes you better at designing APIs.
Real talk:
This stupid little habit has probably made me a better developer. Faster at writing code, better at documentation, less frustrated when I have to type out long variable names or commit messages.
Plus, there's something deeply satisfying about watching words appear on screen at the speed of thought. It's like having a direct brain-to-computer interface, but with more finger movement.
So yeah. Typing fixed my brain. And probably made me less annoying in code reviews because I can actually write coherent comments now.
End of story. Now go find your own weird productivity hack that makes no sense but somehow works.

• **打字速度对非编程职业的影响**：MollyRealized作为法律行政人员，提到打字速度在初期是优势，但过快的打字速度可能导致在商务环境中产生过于详细的文档，反而不利。

• **打字速度的局限性**：kendalf89和ryandrake提到，尽管经过打字课程和长期练习，他们的打字速度依然较低，且这并未显著影响他们的编程能力。这暗示打字速度可能并不是所有职业或任务中的关键技能。

补充讨论：
• **打字方式与健康问题**：ashwinsundar分享了使用人体工学键盘和调整打字方式后，缓解了手腕疼痛的经历，强调了打字方式对健康的影响。

• **工具和练习平台的推荐**：thu询问如何在学习触摸打字时引入符号和数字，haneul则推荐了Monkeytype作为优于keybr的打字练习工具，提供了更多选项和模式。

争议焦点：
• **是否需要遵循"正确"的打字方式**：dawnofdusk支持学习标准打字方式，而JohnMakin等人则认为只要方法有效，不必拘泥于标准方式。

• **打字速度对不同职业和任务的重要性**：不同用户对打字速度在各自工作中的实际影响有不同看法，有些人认为非常重要，而另一些人则认为影响有限。

data.title: DiffX – Next-Generation Extensible Diff Format
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了传统Unified Diffs在现代软件开发中的局限性，指出其缺乏标准化，无法有效处理编码、修订版本、元数据以及文件路径的表示等问题，导致工具在解析和使用差异文件时面临困难。文章提出了一种新的可扩展差异格式——DiffX文件格式，旨在解决这些问题。DiffX文件格式兼容现有工具，具备前瞻性且保持人类可读性。它引入了结构化的元数据和标准化字段，例如编码和版本信息，使得工具可以更可靠地解析和修改差异文件。DiffX格式通过扩展Unified Diffs，使其适应现代开发需求，同时不破坏现有工具的兼容性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于DiffX格式的讨论及其必要性，包括对现有diff/patch工具和格式的批评与建议。

不同观点：
• **laserbeam**：不赞成使用高度层次化的YAML格式，认为应给不同深度的元数据块取不同名称以提高可读性和减少错误。同时，质疑为何使用JSON和key=value两种格式，建议统一为一种格式以简化解析和集成工具。
• **HelloNurse**：认为当前提议的范围不必要地扩大了，特别是关于单个diff表示多个提交列表、二进制补丁、文本编码等问题。指出这些功能更像是特定版本控制系统的内部需求。
• **ed**：认为现有的git patch格式已经解决了这些问题，并提供了文档链接供参考。
• **xyzzy_plugh**：认为文档难以阅读，指出讨论的实质是补丁元数据管理而非diff格式。认为现有格式已经可扩展，并对提议的元数据格式表示怀疑。
• **greatgib**：不支持使用多行JSON或YAML，强调diff文件单行命令的优点，便于使用简单的shell工具进行解析和操作。
• **itake**：指出diff工具在处理长行（如压缩JSON或长数组）时的困难，审查变化不方便。
• **redleader55**：质疑该格式试图解决的问题是什么，并询问这些改进是为谁设计的，是否真的有必要。
• **signa11**：推荐使用difftastic，认为它在处理diff信息方面更优越。
• **bawolff**：认为提议中的许多问题并不实际存在或不常见，比如编码问题、单个diff表示多个提交的问题等。
• **xiphias2**：认为新格式缺乏前向兼容性，JSON通过标准化解决了大部分问题，提议应参考此做法。
• **bravesoul2**：建议如果磁盘空间不是问题，可以直接存储整个原始文件和新的文件，或者使用CRDT操作序列以提高可合并性。
• **chipx86**（DiffX作者之一）：解释了DiffX的背景和设计目标，强调该格式是为了解决工具在处理diff文件时遇到的问题，而不是最终用户的问题。列举了多个版本控制系统（如Git、Mercurial、Perforce等）在处理diff文件时的差异和问题，并说明DiffX试图通过统一和扩展格式来解决这些问题。
• **koiueo**：认为JSON不适合作为元数据的通用表示格式，过于复杂。
• **KingOfCoders**：讽刺地认为应将JSON添加到所有东西中。
• **dedicate**：认为对于复杂变更和提交历史，工具（如Git或代码审查平台）的功能比试图创建一个超级格式更为重要。

补充讨论：
• **格式和可读性**：多位用户对使用JSON和YAML格式的必要性和可读性提出质疑，认为简单、单行的命令更易于操作和解析。
• **实际需求**：一些用户质疑DiffX试图解决的问题是否真实存在，或者是否仅为特定系统或高级用户的需求。
• **工具和格式的关系**：有观点认为，围绕diff的工具（如Git）比diff格式本身更为重要，复杂功能可以通过工具实现而非格式本身。

争议焦点：
• 是否需要一个新的diff格式（DiffX）来解决现有工具的问题，还是通过改进现有格式和工具即可满足需求。
• 使用JSON和key=value两种格式的必要性以及JSON作为元数据格式的适用性。
• 单个diff文件是否应表示多个提交，以及二进制文件处理的需求和实现方式。

44176737.article_content:
DiffX - Next-Generation Extensible Diff Format
¶
If you’re a software developer, you’ve probably worked with diff files. Git
diffs, Subversion diffs, CVS diffs.. Some kind of diff. You probably haven’t
given it a second thought, really. You make some changes, run a command, a
diff comes out. Maybe you hand it to someone, or apply it elsewhere, or put it
up for review.
Diff files show the differences between two text files, in the form of
inserted (
+
) and deleted (
-
) lines. Along with this, they contain some
basic information used to identify the file (usually just the name/relative
path within some part of the tree), maybe a timestamp or revision, and maybe
some other information.
Most people and tools work with
Unified Diffs
. They look like this:
--- readme    2016-01-26 16:29:12.000000000 -0800
+++ readme    2016-01-31 11:54:32.000000000 -0800
@@ -1 +1,3 @@
Hello there
+
+Oh hi!
Or this:
Index: readme
===================================================================
RCS file: /cvsroot/readme,v
retrieving version 1.1
retrieving version 1.2
diff -u -p -r1.1 -r1.2
--- readme    26 Jan 2016 16:29:12 -0000        1.1
+++ readme    31 Jan 2016 11:54:32 -0000        1.2
@@ -1 +1,3 @@
Hello there
+
+Oh hi!
Or this:
diff --git a/readme b/readme
index d6613f5..5b50866 100644
--- a/readme
+++ b/readme
@@ -1 +1,3 @@
Hello there
+
+Oh hi!
Or even this:
Index: readme
===================================================================
--- (revision 123)
+++ (working copy)
Property changes on: .
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Modified: myproperty
## -1 +1 ##
-old value
+new value
Or this!
==== //depot/proj/logo.png#1 ==A== /src/proj/logo.png ====
Binary files /tmp/logo.png and /src/proj/logo.png differ
Here’s the problem
¶
Unified Diffs themselves are not a viable standard for modern development.
They only standardize parts of what we consider to be a diff, namely the
---
/
+++
lines for file identification,
@@
...
@@
lines for
diff hunk offsets/sizes, and
-
/
+
for inserted/deleted lines.
They
don’t
standardize encodings, revisions, metadata, or even how
filenames or paths are represented!
This makes it
very
hard for patch tools, code review tools, code analysis
tools, etc. to reliably parse any given diff and gather useful information,
other than the changed lines, particularly if they want to support multiple
types of source control systems. And there’s a lot of good stuff in diff files
that some tools, like code review tools or patchers, want.
You should see what GNU Patch has to deal with.
Unified Diffs have not kept up with where the world is going. For instance:
A single diff can’t represent a list of commits
There’s no standard way to represent binary patches
Diffs don’t know about text encodings (which is more of a problem than you
might think)
Diffs don’t have any standard format for arbitrary metadata, so everyone
implements it their own way.
We’re long past the point where diffs should be able to do all this. Tools
should be able to parse diffs in a standard way, and should be able to modify
them without worrying about breaking anything. It should be possible to load a
diff, any diff, using a Python module or Java package and pull information out
of it.
Unified Diffs aren’t going away, and they don’t need to. We just need to add
some extensibility to them. And that’s completely doable, today.
Here’s the good news
¶
Unified Diffs, by nature, are
very
forgiving, and they’re everywhere, in
one form or another. As you’ve seen from the examples above, tools shove all
kinds of data into them. Patchers basically skip anything they don’t
recognize. All they really lack is structure and standards.
Git’s diffs are the closest things we have to a standard diff format (in that
both Git and Mercurial support it, and Subversion pretends to, but poorly),
and the closest things we have to a modern diff format (as they optionally
support binary diffs and have a general concept of metadata, though it’s
largely Git-specific).
They’re a good start, though still not formally defined. Still, we can build
upon this, taking some of the best parts from Git diffs and from other
standards, and using the forgiving nature of Unified Diffs to define a new,
structured Unified Diff format.
DiffX files
¶
We propose a new format called Extensible Diffs, or DiffX files for short.
These are
fully backwards-compatible with existing tools
, while also being
future-proof
and remaining
human-readable
.
#diffx:
encoding=utf-8, version=1.0
#.change:
#..preamble:
indent=4, length=319, mimetype=text/markdown
Convert legacy header building code to Python 3.
Header building for messages used old Python 2.6-era list comprehensions
with tuples rather than modern dictionary comprehensions in order to build
a message list. This change modernizes that, and swaps out six for a
3-friendly `.items()` call.
#..meta:
format=json, length=270

"author"
:
"Christian Hammond <christian@example.com>"
,
"committer"
:
"Christi

data.title: Standard Completions
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了多个提供与OpenAI兼容的Completions和Chat Completions API的供应商，如Deepseek、OpenRouter和vLLM等，虽然OpenAI已将Completions视为遗留API，且Chat Completions也被弱化以推广OpenAI Responses API。尽管OpenAI承诺无限期支持当前的Chat Completions API，但它缺乏多模态输出、输入对象存储、显式缓存和助理前缀等功能。各供应商以非标准方式添加了这些功能，导致开发者使用不便。例如，助理前缀在不同供应商中的实现方式各异，且没有标准信号来指示是否支持某些功能，开发者需尝试或检测上游供应商。文章呼吁建立一个标准化的OpenAI API超集，以简化开发者体验，并促进LLM生态系统的互操作性。感兴趣的供应商和开发者可参与Standard Completions工作组。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于旧的 completion API 与新的 chat creation API 哪个更优越的讨论

不同观点：
• [lolpanda的观点] 认为 legacy completion API 优于新的 chat creation API。理由是 completion API 将所有输入视为单个字符串，而 chat API 则要求将输入作为消息列表处理。在处理现代的代理工作流时，模型通常需要处理大量输入数据，包括 RAG 数据、函数调用和其他元数据，用户和助手的消息仅是整体提示的一小部分。因此，将对话与其他输入数据统一格式化为一个单一的文本提示（如使用 <conversation>...</conversation> 标签）更为直观。OpenAI 的新 completion API 支持单个大字符串或消息列表，这一点很不错。此外，他们提到在 Claude 工具中尝试过类似方法，将提示构建成包含指令和示例的较大提示。

• [pawanjswal的观点] 对 lolpanda 的观点表示赞同，指出许多开发者在开发过程中都会遇到这一问题。他认为指出 API 的不一致性并倡导建立一个通用基准是有益的，认可了 lolpanda 提出的改进建议。

补充讨论：
• lolpanda 提到了新的 completion API 支持单个大字符串或消息列表，这表明新 API 也在尝试解决一些格式上的灵活性问题。
• 讨论中还提到 Claude 工具中的 XML 格式化方法，表明在不同平台上对提示格式的不同处理方式也是开发者关注的重点。
• 争议的焦点主要在于处理大规模输入数据时，哪种 API 格式更直观和高效。lolpanda 更倾向于使用单一的字符串格式，而新的 chat API 则采用消息列表的方式，这在处理复杂工作流时可能带来不便。

44143671.article_content:
🌉 Standard Completions
Many LLM providers and open-source projects now offer OpenAI-compatible Completions and Chat Completions APIs, including Deepseek, xAI, OpenRouter, Nous Research, vLLM, and more.
However, OpenAI considers Completions
a legacy API
, and while Chat Completions will not be deprecated, it has been
de-emphasized in favor of the OpenAI Responses API
.
While OpenAI has committed to supporting the current Chat Completions API indefinitely, it does not support features like multimodal outputs, stored input objects, explicit caching, assistant prefixes (prefill), and other features. Providers offering OpenAI-compatible APIs have added these features in non-standard ways, complicating usage for developers.
For example, a request with an assistant prefix works three different ways across three different OpenAI-compatible providers:
# openrouter: trailing assistant message
curl -X POST "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENROUTER_API_KEY" \
-d '{
"model": "anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet",
"messages": [
{ "role": "user", "content": "Tell me a joke." },
{ "role": "assistant", "content": "Sure! How about a knock-knock joke:" }
]
}'
# deepseek: "prefix": true
curl -X POST "https://api.deepseek.com/beta/chat/completions" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEEPSEEK_API_KEY" \
-d '{
"model": "deepseek-chat",
"messages": [
{ "role": "user", "content": "Tell me a joke." },
{ "role": "assistant", "content": "Sure! How about a knock-knock joke:", "prefix": true }
]
}'
# vLLM: "continue_final_message": true
curl -X POST "https://inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1/chat/completions" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $NOUS_API_KEY" \
-d '{
"model": "DeepHermes-3-Mistral-24B-Preview",
"messages": [
{ "role": "user", "content": "Tell me a joke." },
{ "role": "assistant", "content": "Sure! How about a knock-knock joke:" }
],
"add_generation_prompt": false,
"continue_final_message": true
}'
Even worse, because there is no standard way for a provider to signal if they support features like logprobs or assistant prefixes, the only way for an API consumer to detect if the feature is supported is to try it and see what happens, or
attempt to detect the upstream provider even if they are being proxied
.
We hope by standardizing a superset of the OpenAI completions APIs, we can make this experience easier for developers, produce a standard SDK that providers can recommend to their users instead of the OpenAI SDK—while maintaining backwards compatibility with the OpenAI SDK—and make the LLM ecosystem more interoperable.
Join us! If you are a provider or developer interested in joining the Standard Completions working group, please get in touch via email, Twitter/X, or open an issue on the rfcs repository:
Email: standardcompletions (at) vgel (dot) me
Twitter/X: @stdcompletions
standardcompletions/rfcs Github repository

data.title: A manager is not your best friend
data.author: thisismytest
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了管理者为何应避免与下属抱怨和共鸣（commiseration），因为这种行为会对组织造成破坏，导致低信任环境，并形成小团体。文章指出，虽然人们习惯通过共鸣寻求安慰，但在管理角色中，共鸣往往是有害的，会引发优越感并阻止其他团队改进。管理者应像“好 therapist”一样，倾听但不过度附和，通过提问澄清事实，而非简单地附和情绪。文章建议，管理者应避免使用消极语言，尽量从乐观角度解释其他团队的行为，并专注于客观事实而非主观批评。最终目标是通过建立同理心来促进高效协作。

不同观点：

• [NAHWheatCracker] 反思了自己作为技术领导的经历，认为适度的共鸣可以帮助团队解决问题或接受无法改变的事实，但这种需求因人而异，取决于文化和人际关系。

- 争议的焦点在于管理者是否应与下属共同抱怨和表达共鸣，部分人认为适度的共鸣有助于解决问题，而另一些人则认为管理者应保持外交和中立。
- 管理者在职场中的角色和职责被广泛讨论，包括他们在团队中建立心理安全、处理批评反馈和维持人际关系方面的责任。

44176425.article_content:
02 Jun 2025
•
management
As people become managers, it’s quite common for their team members to want to commiserate with them. This is especially true for friendly, competent, reasonable-seeming managers – people want to commiserate with
winners
. This makes commiseration extra dangerous, as it comes with a hint of flattery (“I respect your opinion and trust your discretion”).
But commiseration, especially with your direct reports, is organizational poison. It erodes the fabric of an organization and builds factions. It leads to feelings of superiority and creates a low-trust environment –
even if what you’re complaining about is made up!
Worst of all, it doesn’t give other teams an opportunity to improve. If I think that HR sucks, and I commiserate with my directs about it, my team is going to treat them poorly. HR will never know why, will never fix the problem, and will just think that my team are jerks (and they’ll arguably be right). Commiseration is self-fulfilling because it’s a form of victimhood: The world is conspiring against us, the only truly virtuous team.
Commiseration comes naturally to most people, because it happens all the time in real life. As your best friend, if you come to me saying that you were just dumped by your girlfriend, you will get unconditional sympathy beyond words. You’re the best, she didn’t deserve you, you can do so much better, everyone knows you’re the man, I have no idea why you ever spent time with her. There will be no questions, there will be no need for you to explain anything about the situation, even if all you did for the last 2 years was sit on your couch smoking weed and playing Warzone,
Greg
. Unless you did something totally crazy or illegal, my loyalty will be immediate and unconditional, because – let’s be real – none of it matters. You’re going your way, she’s going hers, and it’s over.
As a manager, your empathy needs to be highly conditional. Your job is to get to the truth of a matter in a respectful way, not make your team feel good. You are largely stuck with your coworkers, and you need to get stuff done together or everyone suffers. If you break up with your girlfriend you get unconditional sympathy. But if you break up with your girlfriend, and the 3 of us were trying to climb Mt. Everest together, I’m going to be a lot more measured in how I communicate and balance your relationship so that we can all survive the next few days.
Commiseration is generally a sensitive topic, so I’ve tried to boil down how to handle situations when a direct comes to you with grievances via some heuristics:
You don’t really want to debate your team in every situation, but your job is to essentially be a scientist and get to the bottom of what’s going on. If someone wants to commiserate about some other team, your first job is to ask a bunch of questions about what’s going on. In my experience, 90% of the time the situation is a grey area, and probably 30% of the time the person who wants to commiserate is actually in the wrong, on balance.
Your role as a manager is also to be a perspective-creator. Sure, that salesperson was overly optimistic on how impactful this custom feature was for a prospect. And sure, the deal wasn’t as large and didn’t close as quickly as they said it would. But sales incentives are a law of the universe, and sales directors need to manage around them just as much as product teams do, because
not
having sales incentives is even worse. And by the way, we’re not so great at estimating development timelines either. Everyone’s blood pressure should always be lower after they’ve spoken to you.
Bad therapists just let you rant. Good therapists let you vent, but they ask clarifying questions, and they sometimes push back. The phrase “is that actually true?” or “Can you explain that more?” are your friends. Good therapists validate feelings but they don’t necessarily validate
facts
. “I know you feel like you’re being a good daughter” is not the same as “you are the best daughter.” You want to be a good therapist.
Remove the phrase “I don’t know why they…” from your lexicon. No matter how you end this sentence, the subtext will be clear: “I don’t know why they’re so incompetent.” Instead, it’s often better to give the most optimistic view for why another team is behaving the way that they are. It might not be
right
, but it builds empathy which is the bedrock on which productive collaboration is built.
If someone is trying to get you to commiserate with them, try to speak in terms of reiterating a decision framework. Rather than “marketing doesn’t know what they’re doing,” you want to say something like “our role is to build the product and have a strong POV for marketing, and their role is to make sure that our launch generates enough pipeline. If you don’t think that’s going to happen then let’s talk to them.” The goal is to focus on objective truths rather than disparaging opinions.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Anna's Archive（AA）的文本搜索、全文检索技术可行性、法律问题及其实际应用的讨论。

不同观点：
• **技术可行性与实现方法**：
  - **bhaney**：认为将AA数据转换为纯文本并在普通硬件上建立全文检索是可行的，但需要较长时间。主要挑战在于从各种格式中提取纯文本、清理数据以及选择合适的数据库进行全文检索。
  - **imdavidsantiago**：同意技术上可行，但强调了将文档转换为纯文本和高效索引是大规模实现全文检索的主要挑战。
  - **podgorniy**：提到了一种针对压缩fb2文件的搜索解决方案，虽然不完全符合AA的需求，但有潜力。

• **现有解决方案与工具**：
  - **net01**：提到AA举办了竞赛，并有一些提交的搜索工具和可视化工具超出了最低要求。
  - **ggm**：指出AA已有完整的元数据索引，但全文检索（free text search）和页面级返回是不同的需求。
  - **nextos**：认为Z-Library已经在某种程度上实现了全文检索，但其规模小于AA，且在某些地区需要通过Tor访问。
  - **renegat0x0**：提到了一些其他搜索引擎，但认为这些可能不适用于AA。
  - **laserstrahl**：介绍了OpenLip这个安卓应用，它通过发送请求到AA并解析响应，实现书籍的下载和阅读。

• **法律与内容过滤问题**：
  - **simgt**：担心AA中可能包含非法内容（如恋童、恐怖主义等），并考虑下载部分内容时如何避免接触到这些内容。
  - **ggm**：指出AA中的文本由于知识产权问题可能成为法律目标，即使衍生作品也会面临法律风险。

补充讨论：
• **创新应用与未来方向**：
  - **allenleein**：提出了一种不同的角度，即通过映射互联网上频繁提及或引用的书籍，将其内容转化为结构化数据，并为LLMs优化，创建一个可语义搜索的个人图书馆。

data.article_summary: 本文讨论了通过阅读小说来帮助处理复杂决策的过程。作者Steven Johnson在《Farsighted》一书中提出，面对如婚姻、家庭和职业等重大决策时，需要管理各种变量并预测结果，尽管这并不完美。他建议通过阅读小说，如乔治·艾略特的《 Middlemarch》，来练习决策。小说中角色面临的多维度决策和结果为读者提供了模拟经验，帮助他们更好地应对现实生活中的复杂问题。此外，文章还引用了Stripe CEO帕特里克·科里森的例子，他通过阅读经典小说提升对智力和人性的理解。最终，小说不仅帮助我们理解他人，还通过自我反思更好地理解自己，为个人决策提供实用价值。

¶ Decisions, decisions!
Steven Johnson
’s 2018 book
Farsighted
presents a method for processing decisions—not the easy kind (cherry pie or apple?) but the tough,
Russ Roberts
–y,
wild
kind, with all the considerations and contingencies that spool out like thirty-seven balls of yarn rolling downhill. Do I:
marry Sally?
put Dad in the nursing home?
change a policy that affects my coworkers’ retirement?
move to Montreal?
chuck it all and go into the car-wash business with my cousin Earl?
Good luck!
Photo by
Letizia Bordoni
on
Unsplash
Wild problems often involve simple, binary choices—yes or no—but they contain countless concerns and consequences. Sally, Dad, coworkers, Montreal, Earl: to one degree or another, the variables multiple as we consider them and ramify in ways we can’t fully corral.
To decide, says Johnson, we must manage to map the variables and then predict the outcomes. We’ll do so imperfectly, and we’ll get more wrong than right—whether the extent of our errors proves material or not. (The future ain’t easy, friends.)
One help in this fraught and feeble process? Surprisingly, Johnson suggests novels, pointing to George Eliot’s
Middlemarch
as his primary example. The tortured decisions with which Dorothea and Lydgate contend involve multiple dimensions and layers, and Eliot takes us inside their minds as they messily try mapping the variables and predicting their outcomes. Novels are for their readers, in other words, practice. “When we read those novels,” says Johnson, “we are not just entertaining ourselves; we are also rehearsing for our own real-world experiences.”
But the practice extends beyond personal considerations.
What’s the Big Deal about ‘Middlemarch’?
Joel J Miller
·
November 20, 2024
Read full story
¶ Thinking across dimensions.
I recently returned to Johnson’s
Farsighted
because Johnson did. In
an essay here at Substack
he mentioned
reading a tweet
in which Stripe CEO Patrick Collison recounted the experience of reading ten classic novels during the year:
Jane Eyre
by Charlotte Brontë
Middlemarch
by George Eliot
To the Lighthouse
by Virginia Woolf
Bleak House
by Charles Dickens
Portrait of a Lady
by Henry James
Anna Karenina
by Leo Tolstoy
Life and Fate
by Vasily Grossman
Heart of Darkness
by Joseph Conrad
Madame Bovary
by Gustave Flaubert
The Magic Mountain
by Thomas Mann
Why would a Silicon Valley tech exec read these sorts of books? Collison admits skepticism about fiction’s power to improve our personal morality but says they can elevate our appreciation of intellectual excellence.
What about improving our understanding of human nature more broadly? “There is almost certainly some extent to which this argument is valid,” says Collison, “though I always wonder: do they help you better understand
humanity
, or better understand
the kind of people who write books like these
?”
I don’t know if novels help us better understand abstract humanity. But I’m convinced as theaters for self-reflection they do help us better understand ourselves and what we think about the world around us; that might generalize to the whole species, but it needn’t do so to be valuable for the individual reader.
Revisiting his argument in
Farsighted
, Johnson offers two explanations of why, one more obvious, the other less so. First, the obvious one:
Novels (and fictional narratives in general) [are] extensions of the human mind’s marvelous aptitude for building
simulations
of potential events. It’s something we do so effortlessly that we rarely stop to think about how nuanced a skill it really is: creatively projecting forward into our possible futures based on our previous experience of the world. Narratives of all sorts allow you to parachute into other simulated experiences, which ultimately give you more data for your own simulations. But novels, I would argue, give you the richest simulation of the
interior life
of other people’s experiences: you get a ringside view of all that emotional and cognitive action. . . . It seems fairly obvious to me that there is practical utility in running these simulations. We accumulate wisdom that we can apply to our own lives by watching other people live theirs.
But, says Johnson, great novelists can push us further, past the mere interiority of their characters’ mental and emotional experience. They can take us across the many dimensions a character’s thought process might travel, all of the external pressures and factors that could come to bear.

data.author: JumpCrisscross
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了风电场之间存在的“风能盗窃”现象，即当一个风电场在另一个风电场的上风处时，会减慢风速，影响下风处风电场的能量输出。这种现象被称为尾流效应，可导致下风向风电场能量输出减少10%或更多。随着全球海上风电场的快速扩展，特别是规模和密度的增加，尾流效应愈发显著，可能延伸超过100公里。这种效应引发了风电场开发商之间的纠纷，尤其是在风电场密集的北海地区。为了解决这一问题，英国已启动新研究项目，旨在通过建模分析2030年风电场的尾流效应，帮助政府和开发商优化规划，避免纠纷。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：风力发电的影响及相关争议

不同观点：
• **风权与资源争夺**：[glkindlmann] 提出风力发电涉及“风权”问题，类似于水权。风力资源可能在不同风电场之间引发冲突，尤其是在上游和下游风速受影响的情况下。[JohnKemeny] 补充说明，这种资源争夺类似于其他共享资源（如水电、太阳能）的争端，强调需要制定更好的规则来解决这些冲突。

• **风电场对环境和气候的潜在影响**：[g42gregory] 担心大规模风电场可能降低环境风速，进而影响气候、鸟类、昆虫等，并质疑风电场的正负效应是否平衡。[DocTomoe] 担心未来可能发现风电场对生态系统的潜在破坏，类似于过去对煤炭和核能的误判。

• **风电场对风速和能量输出的具体影响**：[roxolotl] 提到一个关于飓风的研究，指出风力发电机可能削弱 approaching 飓风的能量，从而减轻风暴的影响。[acyou] 则好奇全球变暖对风电场输出的影响，因为暖空气密度较低，但整体能量可能更多。[morkalork] 强调风电场的尾流效应可能影响百公里外的其他风电场，因此需要优化风电场布局以最大化总输出。[collinmcnulty] 希望将风电场对风速的影响与其他障碍物（如建筑物）进行比较。

• **尾流损失的实际影响**：[glumreaper] 引用研究数据指出，尾流损失对风电场输出影响较小（约3.28%），并认为相较于风电场的长期寿命，这种损失可以忽略不计。[p0w3n3d] 强调风力发电从空气中提取能量必然导致风速下降，这是能量守恒的基本原理，认为这是显而易见的。

• **创意与科幻设想**：[polishdude20] 提出一个科幻设想，未来人类在风暴频繁的地区建立风电场，利用风暴能量，同时保护居住区免受强风侵袭。[hulitu] 则以讽刺口吻提到未来可能出现太阳能农场“偷走”彼此阳光的情况。

• **支持风电发展**：[bamboozled] 强调尽管风电场存在问题，但必须继续实验和开发更好的解决方案，不能让风电成为像“核能”那样的禁忌话题，否则可能错失拯救文明的机会。

补充讨论：
• **风向变化的影响**：[amai] 提出风向变化可能使得不同风电场轮流“偷走”彼此的风，从而缓解尾流损失的长期影响。

争议焦点：
• 风电场对环境和气候的潜在负面影响及其是否能通过技术优化和规则制定加以缓解，是讨论中的主要争议点。一方担心风电场可能对生态系统造成不可逆的破坏，另一方认为这些问题相对较小或可通过技术手段解决。

'Wind theft': The mysterious effect plaguing wind farms
7 May 2025
Share
Save
Sophie Hardach
Share
Save
Getty Images
As wind farms expand, some can accidentally "steal" each others' wind – causing worries over some countries' energy transition to net zero.
As offshore wind farms are expanding around the world in the race to meet net zero climate targets, a worrying phenomenon is attracting growing attention: in some conditions, wind farms can "steal" each other's wind.
"Wind farms produce energy, and that energy is extracted from the air. And the extraction of energy from the air comes with a reduction of the wind speed," says Peter Baas, a research scientist at Whiffle, a Dutch company specialising in renewable energy and weather forecasting. The wind is slower behind each turbine
within the wind farm
than in front of it, and also behind the wind farm as a whole, compared with in front of it, he explains. "This is called the wake effect."
Simply put, as the spinning turbines of a wind farm take energy from the wind, they create a
wake
and slow the wind beyond the wind farm. This wake can stretch more than 100km (62 miles) for
very large
, dense offshore wind farms, under certain weather conditions. (Though more typically, the wakes extend for tens of kilometres, according to researchers). If the wind farm is built upwind of another wind farm, it can
reduce
the downwind producer's
energy output
by as much as
10%
or
more
, studies suggest.
Colloquially, the phenomenon is known as
wind theft
– though as Eirik Finserås, a Norwegian lawyer specialising in offshore wind energy, notes: "The term wind theft is a bit misleading because you can't steal something that can't be owned – and nobody owns the wind."
Getty Images
The wind wake caused by wind turbines can stretch for more than 100km (62 miles) (Credit: Getty Images)
Still, he points out that the phenomenon can have a number of negative consequences for wind farm developers, and even, potentially, cause problems across borders (more on this later). There are in fact a number of ongoing
disputes
between
wind farm developers
over alleged wind theft, raising
concerns
in countries that rely on ramping up offshore wind energy to meet their net zero climate targets.
While the problem of wind theft has been
long known
in principle, it is growing more pressing due to the scale and speed of the offshore expansion, and the
size and density
of offshore wind farms, experts say.
In less than five years, we need to deploy thousands more turbines – Pablo Ouro
In the North Sea, which is seeing an offshore wind boom, the impact of such wakes on offshore energy production is likely to increase in the next decades as the sea becomes more crowded with wind farms, according to
simulations
by Baas together with researchers from the Delft University of Technology and the Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute. The
denser
and
bigger
the wind farm, the stronger the wake effect, Baas says.
A
new research project
in the UK, launched this spring, aims to provide a clearer picture of the wake effect to help governments and developers improve their planning, and avoid disputes. The project will model wakes and their impact on wind farms' output in
2030
, when there will be thousands more turbines in UK waters than today, says project lead Pablo Ouro, a research fellow in civil engineering at the University of Manchester.
"We have seen wake effects for years, and knew they happen," says Ouro. "The problem is that in order to achieve net zero, we need to deploy a given amount of offshore wind capacity. So for
2030
, we need to have three times more capacity than we have now, which means that in less than five years, we need to deploy thousands more turbines," he explains.
"[Some of] these turbines are going to be operating very close to those that are already operating, so things are getting more and more crowded. So these wake effects are now starting to have more impact," he says.
Getty Images
Countries are ramping up offshore wind energy, resulting in disputes between wind farm developers over "wind theft" (Credit: Getty Images)
The UK government has pledged that by 2030, Britain will generate enough power from renewable sources, such as wind, to cover its electricity needs. A 2025 UK government
policy paper
highlights the need to better understand wake effects in this context, describing them as an emerging issue that creates uncertainty for offshore wind farms.
Currently, there are a number of
disputes
in the UK between offshore wind farm developers over potential wake effects, Ouro says. In his view, these disputes are partly caused by uncertainty over the precise impact of wakes. For example, current UK guidelines on how much offshore wind farms should be
spaced apart to avoid wake effects
, may not reflect the
actual extent
the wakes can reach, he says. Also, because offshore wind farms are built in clusters, it can be difficult to assess how they might all affect each others'

主要讨论点：PS3模拟器的进展及其技术挑战

不同观点：
• [phoe-krk] 认为PS3模拟器从最初被认为无法全速模拟，到如今通过各种优化实现高效模拟，展现了开发者在技术上的创造力和不懈努力。他提到自己一直在关注各类模拟器的进展，并对目前的优化效果表示赞赏。

• [leshokunin] 强调了PS3的Cell处理器的独特性和复杂性，指出该处理器由索尼和IBM投入巨资开发，目的是与之前的游戏机CPU完全不同。正因为如此，能如此高效地模拟Cell处理器显得尤为 remarkable（值得注意）。

补充讨论：
• [seam_carver] 对RPCS3模拟器增加了对Apple Silicon原生支持表示高兴，这表明用户在不同硬件平台上对模拟器的需求和关注，特别是对新硬件的支持表示欢迎。

争议焦点：
• 虽然没有直接的争议，但[phoe-krk]和[leshokunin]的观点之间存在一种潜在的对比。[phoe-krk]关注的是模拟器技术进步本身，而[leshokunin]则更强调Cell处理器的设计初衷和其独特性带来的挑战。两者都认同模拟器技术的成就，但侧重点不同。

总结：
讨论主要围绕PS3模拟器技术的发展以及其在应对独特硬件架构（如Cell处理器）方面所取得的显著进步。参与者们从技术进步、硬件独特性和平台支持等角度分享了各自的见解。

data.article_summary: 《Business Insider》专注于讲述创新故事，涵盖商业、科技、金融、政治等多个领域。它通过深入分析和独家报道，揭示行业趋势、创业故事和市场动态，满足读者对前沿资讯的需求。文章通常简明扼要，配以数据图表和专家观点，帮助读者快速了解全球重要事件及其潜在影响。此外，平台还关注成功企业家和新兴企业的成长路径，激励和启发商业领袖及创业者。通过多样化的内容形式，《Business Insider》已成为获取全球商业创新信息的重要来源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：无人机攻击与防御的技术和安全威胁

不同观点：
• [amai] 认为强力手持激光设备可能是应对无人机威胁的解决方案，并引用了一个YouTube视频作为示例。
• [0x38B] 补充了文章中的照片信息，提供了无人机在仓库中被堆叠和准备攻击的链接。
• [getcrunk] 认为政府迟早会采用自动化反无人机雷达/炮塔系统，并对目前尚未广泛采用表示惊讶，指出这是涉及“国家安全”的问题，且这一威胁已存在10到15年。
• [idiotsecant] 关注个人利用廉价无人机造成大规模破坏的可能性，特别是针对国家电力设施，强调了电网恢复供电的困难性。
• [moi2388] 质疑如果无人机如此有效，为什么防御费用高达数十亿，并建议使用猎杀无人机来对付潜在的入侵无人机。
• [fisherjeff] 简单提及了一个新闻链接，暗示了从监视到攻击的转变。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于无人机技术带来的安全威胁及其防御措施的有效性和成本问题。
- [getcrunk] 和 [idiotsecant] 都提到了国家安全问题，但前者关注政府反应的滞后性，后者则聚焦个人利用无人机造成大规模破坏的潜在威胁。
- [moi2388] 对防御技术的高成本表示质疑，并提出了猎杀无人机的可能解决方案。
- 多个评论提到了技术解决方案，如激光设备、自动化反无人机系统和猎杀无人机，显示了对技术防御手段的关注。

总体来看，讨论围绕无人机攻击的威胁程度、防御技术的有效性和成本，以及政府和个人在技术使用中的角色展开。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：QR码是否应被用于广告，尤其是户外广告。

不同观点：
• 反对使用QR码在广告中：WorldWideWebb认为QR码在广告中，尤其是户外广告中，存在安全隐患。他将使用QR码比作在公共场所随意拿起杯子喝水，暗示其具有潜在风险和不确定性。这种观点强调了用户在使用QR码时可能面临的安全问题，比如链接至恶意网站或钓鱼网站。

• 潜在的支持观点（未明确表达，但可推断）：另一方可能认为QR码是一种便捷的工具，可以快速引导消费者获取更多信息或享受服务。然而，这一观点未在评论中明确表达，但可以从QR码被广泛应用的现实中推断出其有一定的实用价值和便利性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：QR码的安全性和用户对其的信任问题是争议的核心。WorldWideWebb的评论突显了对QR码滥用的担忧，特别是在公共场合，用户可能无法预知扫描后的结果。
• 论据和例子：WorldWideWebb使用了生动的比喻，将使用QR码比作在公共场所随意喝水，强调其潜在的危险性和不可预知性。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：虽然评论中没有直接提到，但QR码的便利性和其在现代营销中的广泛应用也是讨论的一部分。这一技术在提供便捷的同时，也要求用户提高警惕，以防范潜在的安全威胁。

data.title: Show HN: LLMFeeder – Browser extension to extract clean content for LLM context
data.author: jatinkrmalik
data.article_summary: LLMFeeder是一款浏览器扩展，能够将网页内容一键转换为干净的Markdown格式并复制到剪贴板，方便用户将其提供给大型语言模型（LLM）使用。该工具在本地执行所有操作，确保数据不会传输到外部服务器，并提供多种自定义选项和快捷键支持。LLMFeeder强调隐私与安全，不含任何分析或数据收集机制，支持Chrome和Firefox浏览器。用户可以通过浏览器扩展商店、直接下载或从源代码安装该扩展，并能根据需要调整内容范围和格式选项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[用户对某工具（推测为浏览器扩展）的评价和反馈]

不同观点：
• [smcleod] 表示目前在使用 **Markdownload** 工具，并计划尝试新分享的工具。该用户对新工具支持 **Firefox** 而非仅支持 **Google Chrome** 表示赞赏，暗示了对跨浏览器支持的重视。
   
• [v01d4lph4] 对分享表示感谢，并表示会进行尝试，但未提及对浏览器兼容性的具体看法，也没有与其他工具进行对比。

补充讨论：
• [smcleod] 通过提及当前使用的工具 **Markdownload** (附带GitHub链接)，提供了对比的背景，显示出对浏览器扩展工具有一定了解，且关注多浏览器兼容性。
• 没有明显的争议，但[smcleod]的观点隐含了对某些扩展仅支持Google Chrome的不满，表明了对更多浏览器兼容性的期望。

LLMFeeder - Webpage to Markdown for your LLM context!
A browser extension that converts web page content to clean Markdown format and copies it to clipboard with a single click, perfect for feeding content to Large Language Models (LLMs). Available for both Chrome and Firefox.
Demo
Click the image for YT Demo video. 👆
Privacy & Security
LLMFeeder operates as a fully client-side extension with zero backend dependencies. All content processing occurs locally within your browser's execution environment:
No Remote Data Transmission
: The extension performs all operations (content extraction, Markdown conversion, clipboard operations) entirely within your browser's sandbox. No data is ever transmitted to external servers.
Zero Telemetry
: Unlike many extensions, LLMFeeder contains no analytics, tracking, or data collection mechanisms of any kind.
Minimal Permissions
: The extension requests only the permissions strictly necessary for its core functionality (activeTab, clipboardWrite, storage, scripting).
Verifiable Codebase
: Being fully open source, the entire codebase is available for inspection to verify these privacy claims. Users are encouraged to review the source code to confirm the absence of any data exfiltration mechanisms.
This architecture ensures that your content remains exclusively on your device throughout the entire extraction and conversion process.
Features
Smart Content Extraction
: Uses Readability algorithm to focus on main content
One-Click Simplicity
: Single action to process and copy content
LLM-Optimized Output
: Clean, structured Markdown perfect for AI consumption
Visual Feedback
: Clear indication of successful copying
Customizable
: Configure content scope and formatting options
Keyboard Shortcuts
: Convert content without opening the popup
Multi-Browser Support
: Works on both Chrome and Firefox

主要讨论点：线上二手交易平台的吸引力与实际使用价值

不同观点：
• **rootsudo的观点**：  
  - 认为该线上二手平台的创意不错，但质疑其存在的必要性。
  - 提出Value Village和Salvation Army等传统二手商店已经在进行数字化转型，并提供促销活动，用户可能更倾向于直接从这些源头购买。
  - 提到新物品的价格可能与二手物品相近，甚至更便宜，这会使用户更倾向于选择亚马逊等平台，以获得更快捷和可靠的服务。
  - 指出该平台存在一些小问题，如没有详细的“关于我们”页面，主要联系方式是hotmail邮箱，这些问题可能影响用户信任。
  - 认为最好的价值还是亲自去实体店淘货，尽管耗费时间，但可以找到非常便宜的商品。
  - 个人更倾向于使用eBay，因为可以对商品质量有更好的预估，并且可以方便地进行价格比较。

• **Kye的观点**：  
  - 认为 thrift store 的吸引力在于能够随机浏览并寻找意外的宝藏。
  - 质疑该线上平台与eBay或Craigslist的区别，不清楚其独特之处在哪。

补充讨论：
- **rootsudo** 提到商品状态与库存照片不符的问题，尤其是书籍的版本和状态、桌游的缺失部件等问题，可能影响用户体验。
- **Kye** 强调 thrift store 的独特购物体验，可能对线上平台的定位提出挑战，认为线上平台需要明确自己的独特价值主张。
- **争议焦点**：线上二手平台是否能够提供比现有平台（如eBay、Craigslist）更独特的价值，以及能否在价格、商品质量和用户体验方面与传统二手商店和亚马逊等电商平台竞争。

总结：讨论围绕线上二手平台的实用性和独特性展开，涉及其与现有平台的竞争关系、用户体验问题以及其相较于实体店的优劣势。

data.author: TMWNN
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Temu及其商业模式的性质和长远战略

不同观点：
• [aiiizzz] 认为将Temu的商业策略称为“漏洞”是一种带有偏见的看法。他可能认为这种描述过于简单化或负面，暗示了对Temu商业手法的不同理解或辩护。

• [Terr_] 引用了评论员的说法，认为Temu目前的商品供应只是一种“桥头堡”或“入门毒品”，其最终目的是引入一种在中国已经成功的混合社交媒体和购物的商业模式。他将这种模式比喻为《楚门的世界》中的商业手法，但更新为适应现代移动和流媒体技术的发展，暗示这种模式可能在美国还不普遍，但具有潜在影响力。

• [jaoane] 认为Temu能够在用户数量减半的情况下仍然视之为“完全胜利”，表明他对Temu的商业韧性和市场策略持有较为乐观的态度，认为即使面对用户流失，Temu依然能够取得成功。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Temu的商业模式是否应被视为一种短期策略（如“入门毒品”）或长期战略（如混合社交媒体和购物模式）。[Terr_] 的观点暗示了Temu的潜在长远目标，而[aiiizzz] 则质疑这种描述的准确性和公正性。

• [jaoane] 的评论提供了一种不同的成功标准，即在用户数量变化的情况下仍然可以视为胜利，这可能反映了不同的商业成功衡量方式。

• 另外，评论中提到的“混合社交媒体和购物”模式，以及其在中国的成功和在美国的不普遍性，指出了跨文化商业模式移植的可能性和挑战。

data.article_summary: 文章揭示了美国移民系统中一个鲜为人知但影响深远的漏洞：科技公司通过在周日报纸分类广告中刊登虚假招聘信息，以帮助外籍员工申请绿卡。这些广告并非真的在招聘，而是为了满足法律要求，证明没有美国公民能胜任该岗位，从而为外籍员工申请永久居留权。这种做法已经存在几十年，尽管对国内外员工都不利，却一直未被广泛关注。在当前科技行业裁员和AI威胁的背景下，这种招聘骗局更加剧了国内科技工作者的就业困境。文章指出，H-1B签证和绿卡申请程序复杂且易被滥用，但因涉及大公司利益，改革面临困难。

The Tech Recruitment Ruse That Has Avoided Trump’s Crackdown on Immigration
by
Alec MacGillis
June 3, 2025, 5 a.m. EDT
Every Sunday, newspapers are full of ads for tech jobs that aren't really looking for applicants. They reveal an aspect of U.S. immigration law that hurts both domestic and foreign workers — yet has endured for decades.
by
Alec MacGillis

Reporting Highlights
Temp to Permanent:
There’s periodic debate over the 120,000 foreigners annually awarded temporary H-1B visas, but almost no attention to the process by which many receive green cards.
Filled, Then Verified:
Foreign workers are eligible for permanent residency only when no U.S. citizens can do the job — but companies confirm that after foreigners have been employed as temps.
Lost in Print:
The law also requires that companies advertise these jobs in the classified ads of Sunday print newspapers, decreasing the chances that U.S. applicants see the listing.
These highlights were written by the reporters and editors who worked on this story.
It’s a tough time for the rank-and-file tech worker or computer science graduate looking for a job. The Silicon Valley giants have laid off tens of thousands in the past couple years. The longstanding threat of offshoring persists, while the new threat of AI looms.
There is seemingly one reason for hope, which you won’t find in popular hiring websites like Indeed.com or ZipRecruiter. It’s exclusively in the help-wanted classifieds in printed newspapers. Every Sunday, metropolitan newspapers across the country are full of listings for tech jobs, with posted salaries sometimes exceeding $150,000. If you’ve got tech skills, it seems, employers are crying out for you, week after week.
One day this spring, I decided to test this premise. I set out with the classified pages from the most recent Sunday edition of The Washington Post, which were laden with tech job offerings in the suburbs of Northern Virginia and Montgomery County, Maryland.
First, I drove to the address given for one of the employers, Sapphire Software Solutions, whose ad said it was looking for someone to “gather and analyze data and business requirements to facilitate various scrum ceremonies for multiple business systems and processes.” I arrived at an office building in Ashburn, Virginia, near Dulles International Airport. But the receptionist in the appointed suite looked confused when I asked for Sapphire.
“This is virtual office,” she said, in a heavy Eastern European accent. “We have many kinds of virtual offices.” She gestured at a long filing-cabinet drawer that was open behind her, full of folders. “You must mail to them.”
From there, I drove 2 miles to another company advertising for help, Optimum Systems, whose address turned out to be an office park full of dental practices. But the office door said nothing about Optimum, instead carrying a sign for an accountant and a different tech firm. It was dark and empty.
And from there, I drove 6 miles to a company called Softrams, which was advertising for a “Full Stack Developer.” I walked into an office in a building that also housed a driving school. The reception area was empty. I called hello, and a woman appeared. I told her I was a reporter wanting to learn more about the listing. She was surprised and asked if she could read the ad in my hand. “I’ll check with the team and get back to you,” she said.
A few days later, after similarly mysterious visits to other offices, I reached the woman, Praveena Divi, on the phone. “This ad is for a PERM filing,” she said. “A filing for a green card.”
To anybody familiar with the PERM system, those words meant the ad was not really intended to find applicants. I had entered one of the most overlooked yet consequential corners of the United States immigration system: the process by which employers sponsor tech workers with temporary H-1B visas as a first step to getting them the green card that entitles them to permanent residency in the U.S. It is a process that nearly everyone involved admits is nonsensical, highly vulnerable to abuse, as well as a contributor to inequities among domestic and foreign tech workers.
Yet the system has endured for decades, largely out of public view. There is occasional debate over the roughly 120,000 workers from overseas who are awarded H-1B visas every year for temporary high-skilled employment. data.title: Gemini in Chrome
data.author: aru
data.article_summary: Gemini是一项内置于Chrome浏览器的人工智能助手功能，旨在帮助用户更高效地浏览和理解网页内容。用户无需切换标签页，即可获取关键要点、澄清概念、获得问题答案，甚至总结文章或页面内容。Gemini还可以帮助比较产品选项、解答好奇心，并通过对话形式协助组织思路或深入探讨话题。该功能仅在用户点击Gemini图标或使用设定好的快捷键时激活，确保用户自主控制。目前，Gemini在Chrome的功能主要面向美国地区的Google AI Pro和Ultra订阅用户，并计划扩展到更多语言和地区。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google在Chrome中集成LLM（Gemini）功能引发的不同观点和讨论

不同观点：
• [支持功能集成] 一些用户（如[nullbyte]）对Google将LLM功能直接集成到Chrome中表示欢迎，认为这是一个很好的想法，并表示一直在寻找这样的功能。
• [质疑功能必要性] 其他用户（如[sebastiennight]）则对LLM的总结功能作为主要使用场景表示困惑，质疑其实际应用价值，并询问真实使用场景。
• [隐私担忧] 部分用户（如[i_love_retros]）对Google访问用户数据（如邮件、日历、网页浏览记录等）表示强烈担忧，认为这是对隐私的严重侵犯。
• [反对强制推送] 一些用户（如[Molitor5901]）表示不喜欢公司向他们推送LLM功能，希望能自行选择是否使用，甚至希望移除相关按钮。

补充讨论：
• [竞争和市场优势] 一些讨论提到Google通过Chrome、Android等广泛使用的产品获得市场竞争优势，其他公司难以抗衡（如[leoff], [SoKamil]）。
• [功能比较] 有用户（如[lol768]）指出类似功能已经在其他浏览器（如Firefox）中存在，并认为浏览器扩展甚至可能提供更多自定义选项。
• [功能限制] 一些用户（如[jadbox]）指出当前版本的功能限制，如不支持Google Workspace操作和多标签处理。
• [法律与政策] 用户（如[t1amat]）提到在政府考虑是否要求Google剥离Chrome的背景下，Google推出此功能的时机可能不佳。

总结：Google在Chrome中集成LLM功能引发了关于功能实用性、隐私担忧、市场竞争和法律政策的多方面讨论。用户对此功能的看法不一，有的表示欢迎，有的则强烈反对。

The web, reimagined.

Frequently asked questions
What is Gemini in Chrome?
With the
Gemini in Chrome
feature, you can get AI assistance on your desktop to do things easily like get key takeaways, clarify concepts, find answers and more. To provide the most relevant responses, Gemini in Chrome uses the content of the web page you’re viewing.
Gemini in Chrome is part of the Chrome browser on desktop, and is different from visiting Gemini in any browser at
gemini.google.com
or starting a chat with the Gemini web app by typing @gemini in the address bar in Chrome. You can use the Gemini web app in other browsers (or the content area of Chrome), but you won’t be able to share page content or use Live mode like you can with Gemini in Chrome.
How do I use Gemini in Chrome?
You can access
Gemini in Chrome
through the Gemini icon in the Chrome toolbar or via a keyboard shortcut that you set up on a Windows or Mac desktop.
Where is Gemini in Chrome available?
Gemini in Chrome
is first rolling out to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the US who have their Chrome language set to English. We look forward to bringing this feature to more people and additional languages soon.

data.title: Ask HN: How do I learn practical electronic repair?
data.author: juanse
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电子产品维修的学习与实践

不同观点：
• atonse：通过Louis Rossmann的电子指南学习基本概念，并通过实践提高技能。建议根据需要解决的问题来学习特定技能，例如焊接或识别电容器。强调动手实践和利用在线资源（如YouTube）。
• analog31：强调动手拆解和研究旧电子垃圾来建立对设备工作原理的直观理解。推荐YouTube作为学习资源，并分享个人常用工具和技巧，如使用放大镜和光源。
• BigCatStuff：推荐YouTube频道作为学习资源，如MyMateVince和Electronics Repair School。建议从便宜的工具开始，如万用表和焊接工具。
• mikewarot：分享从1950年代电视维修经验中学到的知识，强调对高压的谨慎处理和实际操作中的一些具体问题，如银云母电容和老旧电子设备的维修。
• kazinator：认为电子工程知识对于有效调试电路至关重要，推荐《The Art of Electronics》一书，并指出某些高级电子知识在基础维修中不一定是必要的。
• lnsru：认为深厚的电气工程知识是调试和维修电路所必需的，并指出不同类型的故障需要不同的技能和知识。还提到有些设备不值得修理，因为经济上不划算。

补充讨论：
• homieg33：分享利用ChatGPT成功修复无线N64控制器接收器的经验，展示了AI在维修中的辅助作用。
• reassembled：推荐加入在线社区（如Northwest Repair Discord）以获取技术分享和建议。
• gtani：提到PC组装和维修作为市场化技能的价值，尤其是键盘等外设的维修。
• Bjartr：建议通过购买二手破旧电子设备来练习维修，这样不仅可以提高技能，还能通过转售获利。
• iamflimflam1：推荐YouTube频道（如StezStixFix）展示即使只有基础知识也能进行有效 troubleshooting。
• cafp12：认为学习基本电路是必要的，并分享通过相关爱好（如3D打印和机械键盘）积累经验的例子。
• headora：推荐购买HiFi维修套件并从简单的焊接练习开始，逐步提高技能。
• paulgerhardt：建议通过修复有设计缺陷的流行电子设备来快速提高技能，并提到通过转售这些设备来积累经验和经济收益。

争议焦点：
• 是否需要深厚的电子工程知识才能有效进行电子设备维修。kazinator和lnsru强调深厚的理论知识，而atonse和analog31则更注重实践和动手能力。
• 维修的经济可行性。lnsru和paulgerhardt提到有些设备由于成本和复杂性问题不值得修理，而Bjartr则认为通过转售修复物品可以使练习过程自给自足。

data.title: Root shell on a credit card terminal
data.author: stgl
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者对支付卡终端进行逆向工程的过程，目标是探索其安全特性。作者选取了广泛应用于瑞士的Worldline Yomani XR终端，初步检查未发现明显漏洞，于是进行拆解。设备采用了定制ASIC和多层PCB设计，具备多种防篡改机制，如利用板间连接的压力敏感性、锯齿状痕迹和柔性PCB等。拆解后重新组装，设备显示“检测到篡改”，无法操作。

作者通过“芯片取下”方法提取固件，发现固件未加密，但有特殊的ECC布局。通过自定义文件系统读取器，成功提取并查看了Linux文件系统。系统使用3.6内核和Buildroot 2010.02构建，存在较旧的软件版本，显示出潜在的安全隐患。在探索过程中，作者意外获得了root shell，提升了进一步研究的信心。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：信用卡读卡器的安全性、硬件故障问题及相关技术细节

不同观点：
• Disposal8433认为，虽然可以通过USB卡读卡器伪造交易，但由于银行与商户之间的合同和法规约束，实际执行这种操作是非法的，且风险很高。卡读卡器的安全性依赖于这些外部合同和监管，而非设备本身。
• joshstrange对Stripe M2读卡器的质量表示不满，指出在使用极少的情况下有较高故障率，但仍认为M2是其最佳选择。他还提供了有关其公司如何使用这些设备的背景信息。
• londons_explore推测，触发防篡改封条时可能会打开根shell，系统会进入安全或非安全模式，非安全模式下可能开放根shell供调试使用，但关键私钥会被删除。
• mrbluecoat淡化了根shell暴露的风险，指出没有证据表明敏感数据如卡信息会因此受到威胁，但认为这是安全设计者值得注意的阅读材料。
• ComputerGuru对Linux环境下的安全模式选择机制表示担忧，认为即使引导程序安全，但如果加载到一个被入侵的环境中执行，仍然存在风险。

补充讨论：
• ttkari提出，触发防篡改模式可能是进行拒绝服务攻击的有效方式，尤其是在零售场所。
• halpow建议尝试Android基信用卡终端，认为这些设备可能更具“回报”。
• Liftyee对硬件限制的规避和利用表现出兴趣，认为即使触发防篡改状态后仍有许多值得探索的地方。
• ofjcihen质疑为何一开始就要打开设备触发篡改状态，认为这可能使测试变得无意义，建议这是最后才应尝试的手段。
• rswail解释了EMV标准下信用卡终端的安全机制，强调交易数据在传输和静态时的保护措施，指出业务流程与实际卡交易安全无关。
• thenthenthen和grishka分享了欧洲和芬兰的支付终端使用情况和不同设计体验。
• bill_mcgonigle对技术细节如焊接线类型及Busybox源代码提供表示好奇。
• zzzeek根据图表推测 rooted mp2 子系统负责获取硬件的篡改状态并传递给mp1系统，建议尝试禁用篡改信号以启动mp1。
• _trampeltier分享了一次支付时终端更新的实际经历，增加了讨论的现实案例。

争议焦点：
• 根shell暴露的实际风险及其对整体系统安全性的影响。
• 打开和篡改信用卡终端的必要性和伦理问题。
• Stripe M2读卡器的质量问题是否影响其作为最佳选择的可行性。

44150803.article_content:
Root Shell on Credit Card Terminal
In this project, I started to reverse engineer payment card
terminals because they seemed to be an interesting target for security
research, given the high stakes involved. Although I initially didnât
know much about this industry, I did expect a ton of security features
and a very security-hardened device. And to some degree, this was also
correct.
First Look
The model I went with is a Worldline Yomani XR terminal. Although it
seems to be discontinued at the time of writing, this is the model that
is
everywhere
in Switzerland. From big grocery chains to the
small repair shop on the corner, everyone has one or a whole fleet of
this exact terminal.
After booting it up and aimlessly clicking through the UI, I did a
quick port scan, but couldnât find anything interesting. So naturally,
I started to take it apart.
The housing and the PCBs appear to be well-made. The design consists
of multiple PCBs: a small connector board for the outward-facing
connectors, the main board, and a vertical board the card slot sits on.
The main SoC seems to be a custom ASIC, a dual-core Arm processor
code-named âSamoa IIâ in the firmware, but I am jumping ahead.
According to Worldline documentation, this seems to indeed be a custom
ASIC, rather than just a rebranded off-the-shelf chip. Next to it,
there is a small external flash and RAM.
Tamper Protections
During disassembly, I kept looking for a tamper switch that would
detect when the deviceâs housing was opened, like I had seen previously
on laptops and other devices. However, I couldnât find such a switch.
Rather, they use the board-to-board interconnects as a way of detecting
when the device is opened. Because they use relatively
pressure-sensitive Zebra strips between the boards, they have to be
tightly screwed together. Even unscrewing some of the screws is enough
to break contact and trigger a tamper event. Of course, the tamper
detection must also work when the power is disconnected, so thatâs the
purpose of the coin cell battery.
But this is not all in terms of tamper resistance: The âvulnerableâ
PCBs are covered by zick-zack traces that act as a tamper detection
mechanism. Accidentally breaking a single copper trace during a
physical penetration attempt (hole drill etc.) is enough to trigger the
tamper detection.
Trace meander on the display PCB acting as tamper detection.
The card slot itself is contained in an additional, internal
housing. Wrapped around this housing, there is a flex PCB acting as
tamper protection.
Card reader assembly wrapped in a tamper detection flex PCB.
After putting the device back together, it was clear that my
intrusion had not gone undetected. Sure enough, the device would now
only show a big red screen screaming âTAMPER DETECTEDâ. In this mode,
the device seems to be fully unresponsive to any kind of external
input. So, game over?
Chip-Off Firmware Extraction
Since any âruntimeâ exploration seems to be futile now, I wanted to
take a look a the firmware. For this, I desoldered the on-board flash
chip, soldered some wires to it in âdead bugâ style and proceeded to
dump the contents.
BGA flash chip of the card terminal desoldered and connected to a
flash reader.
To my surprise, the contents seemed to be entirely unencrypted!
However, the contents seemed to have a strange ECC layout. Instead of
following the flash chipâs inherent page layout and putting the ECC
data in the interleaved spare areas, it appeared as if the some ECC
data was present in the page and some clear text was in the spare
areas. With the help of some friends, I figured out the layout: instead
of using the standard 2048 byte payload + 64 byte ECC/spare layout, it
uses 3x 694 byte chunks of data each followed by 10 ECC bytes. The ECC
bytes do not appear to be all used. Instead, the last 16 bytes of the
spare area seem to act as metadata for the YAFFS2 file system. Now
normally, there are less ECC bytes per page and therefore the usable
metadata area for the filesystem is larger than 16 bytes. For this
reason, the YAFFS2 filesystem had to be patched to work with smaller
metadata structures.
I implemented a compatible filesystem reader and with it, I could
successfully dump the filesystem contents!
View
yomani-unpacker on Github
Now it was clear that this device runs Linux. I found a standard
Linux filesystem with a lot of interesting files to browse through. The
system runs a 3.6 kernel, built with Buildroot 2010.02 (!) in February
of 2023. The system seems to use a custom bootloader, âBooter v1.7â.
Although I donât know how recent the firware version was that I ended
up dumping, it must have been released after February 2023. So finding
such an ancient kernel is rather concerning. Userspace-wise, the system
uses classy init scripts, busybox, and uClibc (final release was 13
years ago). libcrypt has version 0.9.26, ouch.
Finding a Root Shell on Accident
Having seen the firmware gave me some new confidence
44150803.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者对支付卡终端进行逆向工程的过程，目标是探索其安全特性。作者选取了广泛应用于瑞士的Worldline Yomani XR终端，初步检查未发现明显漏洞，于是进行拆解。设备采用了定制ASIC和多层PCB设计，具备多种防篡改机制，如利用板间连接的压力敏感性、锯齿状痕迹和柔性PCB等。拆解后重新组装，设备显示“检测到篡改”，无法操作。

作者通过“芯片取下”方法提取固件，发现固件未加密，但有特殊的ECC布局。通过自定义文件系统读取器，成功提取并查看了Linux文件系统。系统使用3.6内核和Buildroot 2010.02构建，存在较旧的软件版本，显示出潜在的安全隐患。在探索过程中，作者意外获得了root shell，提升了进一步研究的信心。

data.title: A critical look at NetBSD’s installer
data.author: jaypatelani
data.article_summary: 本文是关于NetBSD安装过程的详细指南，特别关注其安装程序`sysinst`。作者之前撰写了关于FreeBSD和OpenBSD安装的系列文章，而本文则聚焦于NetBSD 10.1在amd64系统上的安装。文章首先提到NetBSD的安装程序是菜单驱动的，与FreeBSD类似，但操作更简便，如使用字母热键导航。语言和键盘布局选择相对简单，但包含一些意外选项如冰岛语和德语NEO2布局。安装过程清晰简洁，但某些界面如硬盘和分区方案选择可以提供更多解释。作者建议在选择安装目标和分区方案时增加更多说明，以帮助新手更好地理解选项（如MBR和GPT的区别）。总体而言，文章提供了对NetBSD安装过程的深入见解，并指出其可改进之处。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NetBSD的系统安装程序（sysinst）的用户体验及其对新用户的适应性

不同观点：
• rahen认为，虽然sysinst的用户体验有提升空间，但他质疑作者是否以典型用户的视角来使用NetBSD。作为有旧式Unix经验的用户，他更偏好类似OpenBSD和Alpine Linux的命令行安装程序，并建议用类似程序替代sysinst。
• JSR_FDED赞赏了原作者的评论，认为新用户视角对改进系统很有价值。
• sam_lowry_对截图的获取方式提出疑问，猜测安装程序是否在虚拟机中运行。
• jmclnx同意评论中对sysinst在分区步骤可能让新用户困惑的看法，建议新用户多次阅读指南，并提供了关于创建独立/usr和/var分区时的具体操作建议，以避免启动错误或警告。

补充讨论：
• rickcarlino简单提及了对Gemini://交叉发布的赞赏，但未深入讨论技术内容。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于sysinst是否适合现代用户，特别是新手用户，以及是否有必要用其他更符合Unix哲学的安装程序替代它。

44176919.article_content:
[New to Gemini? Have a look at my
Gemini FAQ
.]
This article was bi-posted to Gemini and the Web
; Gemini version is here:
gemini://gemini.circumlunar.space/users/kraileth/neunix/2025/installing_bsd_pt3.gmi
The
first part
of this series was about FreeBSD’s installer and the
second
covered OpenBSD’s installation program.
This is a longer article and it has the most images that I ever included in one. While writing the other two articles didn’t take me too long, this one has has occupied several evenings / nights over the course of about three weeks.
NetBSD is an OS that I installed only a couple of times over the years, so I’m not very familiar with its installer,
sysinst
. This fact was actually what led to this article (or the whole series rather): Talking to a NetBSD developer at EuroBSDcon 2023, I mentioned my impression that NetBSD was harder to install than it needed to be. He was interested in my perspective as a relative newcomer, and so I promised to take a closer look and write about it. While it certainly took me long enough, I finally get to do this. So let’s take a look at NetBSD’s installer, shall we? The version explored here is NetBSD
10.1
on
amd64
.
Installing a simple graphical NetBSD system
Sysinst is menu-driven like FreeBSD’s installer, but the two are quite different. This is not a direct comparison, but I’m going to mention other installers where appropriate. Like in the previous two articles, I’m going to install the OS twice: One time using the standard VGA console and once to assess how well it works over serial. Both installations will be in VMs just for the sake of convenience.
Language settings
The first screen that the installer presents is the language selection. If you’re used to more mainstream operating systems, you may be surprised that there’s only four languages in addition to English. But hey: Many other installers are available in English only, and if you’re somebody who’s more comfortable with German, (Castilian) Spanish, French, or Polish than with English, it’s nice to have the option!
I like that there’s a short introduction text at the top which briefly explains how to navigate the installer. This is very nice for newcomers! Assigning each item an alphabetic hotkey is also a great mechanic that makes navigating the installer a breeze even if there’s a lot of options (FreeBSD’s choice of numeric hotkeys is obviously inferior as soon as there are more than ten items).
Language selection
After selecting the language, the installer presents a list of supported keyboard layouts. Again, NetBSD’s installer does not offer the most comprehensive list ever, but there are some surprises. Given the relatively short list, your preferred keymap may not be available.
You probably wouldn’t expect that somebody invested the effort to make Icelandic available, would you? And there’s also things like “German (NEO2)”, a relatively obscure ergonomic variant (that I’ve actually used in the past before adopting BONE whith is basically NEO3). Not even FreeBSD offers NEO2, BTW. Those unusual cases are strong indicators of the NetBSD project being happy to include contributions. So if you consider making a keymap for your layout, another option in the list could probably be yours!
Keyboard layout selection
Next is the main menu that allows the user to either install a fresh system, upgrade an existing one, reboot and so on. Like in the menu before, the text at the top did not change. But it didn’t have to since once again the menu options are self-explanatory.
Installer options
The next screen presents some information on the steps of the installation process and asks if that is what the user wants to do. It’s concise and to the point – I like it. It means an additional key press, but it’s helpful for newcomers.
Installation process overview
Preparing the hard disk
Now sysinst needs to know the installation target. I believe a more detailed explanation at the top would be beneficial. It’s probably nitpicking to point out that “Extended partitioning” is not exactly an answer to the question “On which disk do you want to install NetBSD?”. That aside, I genuinely believe this screen could be improved. Something like “Select a single disk as the installation target or choose ‘extended partitioning’ for softraid, a logical volume manager or device encryption.” would be better. Probably mentioning that ‘wd*’ means IDE or SATA drives, ‘sd*’ is for SCSI or external USB drives and ‘ld*’ are logical drives like VirtIO drives and NVME could be helpful as well.
Installation target selection
The next screen does not have any explanatory text at all – another missed opportunity. While people who install NetBSD probably know it, would it hurt to mention that MBR is the scheme that older BIOS systems expect while GPT is required for EFI systems? I guess it wouldn’t.
Partitioning scheme selection
The partition options and the description text for GPT are fine.
Partitioning options
The default partition layo

data.title: Binary Wordle
data.author: eh8
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了名为"Binary Wordle"的猜词游戏。玩家需要通过输入由0和1组成的二进制数来猜测目标单词，游戏界面提供输入框和按钮（0、1、Enter、Backspace）用于操作。每次猜测后，系统不会直接显示正确答案，而是让玩家根据反馈继续尝试。文章还提到更多有趣的内容可以在chengeric.com网站上找到。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕二进制版Wordle游戏（Digitle）的玩法、难度和潜在改进的讨论。

不同观点：
• [调侃与命名] tylerchr分享其妻子将二进制版Wordle称为“Digitle”，引发对游戏名称的调侃。neuroelectron对此回应表示看懂了这一幽默。
• [游戏机制与难度] umvi认为二进制过于简单，但十六进制有挑战性，并分享了自己设计的基于十六进制的Wordle变种"dwordle"。abotsis则认为目前的二进制玩法过于简单，建议通过减少猜测次数或引入“猜数字”的玩法增加难度。
• [游戏体验与运气] soneca、dhsysusbsjsi和mulmen分享了自己在首次或较早尝试中就猜中结果的经历，kylec则指出这种快速胜利其实有1/32的概率，降低了成就感。
• [与其他游戏的比较] citizenfishy认为Digitle与Mastermind类似，暗示其缺乏创新性。asimovDev分享了一个类似游戏的链接，指出其相似性。
• [技术问题] thehours提到游戏输入存在问题，键盘输入时只有先输入'0'才能继续，需要刷新页面才能解决。
• [功能建议] nickburlett提出添加“分享”按钮的建议，类似于其他变种Wordle游戏。

补充讨论：
• 游戏的运气成分较高，部分玩家通过几次尝试就能猜中结果，可能导致游戏性不足。
• 不同玩家对游戏难度的感知不同，有些认为二进制过于简单，建议通过增加复杂性或减少猜测次数来提高挑战性。
• 玩家对游戏功能和体验提出了一些改进建议，如添加分享按钮和解决输入问题。

争议焦点：
• 游戏的难度和可玩性是主要争议点，部分玩家认为当前版本过于简单，需要增加复杂性或新的机制来提升游戏体验。
