44176825.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了名为"Binary Wordle"的猜词游戏。玩家需要通过输入由0和1组成的二进制数来猜测目标单词，游戏界面提供输入框和按钮（0、1、Enter、Backspace）用于操作。每次猜测后，系统不会直接显示正确答案，而是让玩家根据反馈继续尝试。文章还提到更多有趣的内容可以在chengeric.com网站上找到。
44176825.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕二进制版Wordle游戏（Digitle）的玩法、难度和潜在改进的讨论。

不同观点：
• [调侃与命名] tylerchr分享其妻子将二进制版Wordle称为“Digitle”，引发对游戏名称的调侃。neuroelectron对此回应表示看懂了这一幽默。
• [游戏机制与难度] umvi认为二进制过于简单，但十六进制有挑战性，并分享了自己设计的基于十六进制的Wordle变种"dwordle"。abotsis则认为目前的二进制玩法过于简单，建议通过减少猜测次数或引入“猜数字”的玩法增加难度。
• [游戏体验与运气] soneca、dhsysusbsjsi和mulmen分享了自己在首次或较早尝试中就猜中结果的经历，kylec则指出这种快速胜利其实有1/32的概率，降低了成就感。
• [与其他游戏的比较] citizenfishy认为Digitle与Mastermind类似，暗示其缺乏创新性。asimovDev分享了一个类似游戏的链接，指出其相似性。
• [技术问题] thehours提到游戏输入存在问题，键盘输入时只有先输入'0'才能继续，需要刷新页面才能解决。
• [功能建议] nickburlett提出添加“分享”按钮的建议，类似于其他变种Wordle游戏。

补充讨论：
• 游戏的运气成分较高，部分玩家通过几次尝试就能猜中结果，可能导致游戏性不足。
• 不同玩家对游戏难度的感知不同，有些认为二进制过于简单，建议通过增加复杂性或减少猜测次数来提高挑战性。
• 玩家对游戏功能和体验提出了一些改进建议，如添加分享按钮和解决输入问题。

争议焦点：
• 游戏的难度和可玩性是主要争议点，部分玩家认为当前版本过于简单，需要增加复杂性或新的机制来提升游戏体验。

data.title: Merlin Bird ID
data.author: twitchard
data.article_summary: Merlin是一款鸟类识别应用，提供三种主要功能。Sound ID可实时听取并识别周围鸟鸣，支持离线使用，适用于美国、加拿大、欧洲等地，并将扩展到更多地区。Photo ID可通过照片识别鸟类，同样支持离线使用。Bird ID Wizard通过回答三个简单问题提供可能的鸟类匹配。应用由eBird支持，用户可以创建自定义鸟类清单，并将识别的鸟类添加到个人生活清单中。Merlin结合社区贡献的照片、鸣叫声及专家建议，帮助全球鸟类爱好者识别鸟类。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对鸟类识别应用（特别是Sound ID和Merlin）的功能、效果和局限性的评价与讨论。

不同观点：
• [正面评价] 许多用户对Sound ID和Merlin应用表示高度赞赏。用户[urban_winter]、[Mossy9]、[ainiriand]、[waetsch]等分享了使用这些应用识别鸟类叫声的积极体验，认为这些工具帮助他们更好地享受观鸟 hobby，并成功识别了多种鸟类，甚至在嘈杂环境中也有一定的效果。

• [技术细节] 用户[eichin]和[gcr]讨论了Sound ID背后的技术，指出其通过声谱图和计算机视觉技术实现鸟类识别，并强调了研究团队的专业性如何提升模型的准确性。用户[sgarman]和[michaelmior]则提到了开源项目Birdnet-go和BirdNET-PI，提供了自行搭建识别系统的选择。

• [局限性与误差] 用户[AnotherGoodName]和[podlp]提到应用在识别相似鸟种或在数据不足的地区（如发展中国家）时可能出现误差。用户[OptionOfT]分享了一个具体案例，指出应用将模仿啄木鸟叫声的模仿鸟错误识别为啄木鸟。

• [设备问题] 用户[pixelesque]指出iOS更新后应用存在耗电问题，而[andsoitis]则希望在声音回放时能够将音频投放到外部扬声器。

• [娱乐与教育价值] 用户[ainiriand]和[waetsch]强调了应用的娱乐和教育价值，尤其是对于家庭成员的参与和学习。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：虽然大多数用户对应用的准确性表示信任，但部分用户对其在特定情况下（如高频叫声、相似物种识别）的可靠性提出质疑。
• 应用使用场景：用户分享了在不同环境下使用应用的经验，包括嘈杂的城市环境和安静的郊区，显示了应用的多样性和适应性。
• 技术进步：讨论中提到了机器学习和AI技术在观鸟应用中的成功应用，展示了技术在爱好领域的积极影响。

总体而言，用户对鸟类识别应用的评价积极，但也指出了一些技术局限性和设备相关问题，希望未来能够进一步改进。

44176829.article_content:
Identify Bird Songs and Calls
Sound ID
listens to the birds around you and shows real-time suggestions for who’s singing. Compare your recording to the songs and calls in Merlin to confirm what you heard. Sound ID works completely offline, so you can identify birds you hear no matter where you are.
Available for birds in the US, Canada, Europe, with some common birds of Central and South America, and India. More species and regions coming soon.
More About Sound ID
Identify Birds in a Photo
Snap a photo of a bird, or pull one in from your camera roll, and
Photo ID
will offer a short list of possible matches. Photo ID works completely offline, so you can identify birds in the photos you take no matter where you are.
More about Photo ID
Bird ID Wizard—Step-by-step
Answer three simple questions about a bird you are trying to identify and Merlin will give you a list of possible matches. Merlin offers quick identification help for all levels of bird watchers and outdoor enthusiasts to help you learn about the birds in any country in the world.
Regions Merlin Covers
Save Birds to Your Life List
Build a digital scrapbook of your birding memories with Save My Bird. Tap “This is my bird!” each time you identify a bird, and Merlin will add it to your growing life list.
Save Your Birds with Merlin
Explore Lists of Birds Near You
Merlin is powered by
eBird
, allowing you to build custom lists of the birds you’re likely to spot wherever you are. Use the filter options to explore birds for different locations or time of year, or switch to show all the Offline Birds you’ve downloaded. Get more from the app with these
Merlin Tips and Tricks
.
See How Merlin Can Help You ID Birds
The Best Birding App, Powered By You
Merlin features the best of community contributed photos, songs, and calls, tips from experts around the world to help you ID the birds you see, and range maps from
Birds of the World
—all powered by billions of bird observations submitted to
eBird
.

data.title: Show HN: Hacker News historic upvote and score data
data.author: clacker-o-matic
data.article_summary: Hacker News Alerts Dashboard 是一个用于监控用户帖子在 Hacker News 首页表现的工具。它显示了以下关键信息：总故事数（数据库中跟踪的故事）、最高点数（获得最多点赞的故事）、平均点数（每个故事的平均点赞数）以及平均在首页停留时间（故事在首页显示的平均时长）。用户可以点击某个故事查看其在 Hacker News 首页的排名历史。该工具还提供数据刷新功能，并仅对跟踪的用户显示信息。当前，故事数据正在加载中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对数据收集和可视化项目的反馈与争议

不同观点：
• **zX41ZdbW** 分享了其数据收集项目，能够生成热图，并提供了具体的SQL查询示例，展示了如何获取和处理Hacker News上的数据。
• **ChrisMarshallNY** 对数据中的“最高点数461”提出质疑，指出其看到的帖子有超过2200点，并提供了具体帖子链接。
• **bilekas** 也对数据准确性提出疑问，提到自己看到的帖子有超过390点，并提供了一个例子。
• **namiwang** 赞赏项目，并提到自己曾经创建过类似项目（Track HN），建议可以合作以开发更强大的功能，提供了项目链接。
• **TheEdonian** 对数据图表的快速增长表示怀疑，提出这些帖子是否因为上了首页而获得大量关注，或者是否存在购买点赞的行为。
• **welder** 提供了一个相关网站链接（hnrankings.info），可能作为参考或对比。
• **jcmp** 对项目进入Hacker News首页表示祝贺，语气较为轻松。
• **baxtr** 对网站的设计表示赞赏，但质疑数据的实际应用价值，询问可以如何利用这些数据。
• **NAHWheatCracker** 同样赞赏网站设计，但对数据的个人使用价值表示不确定，并提出了用户体验上的建议（点击帖子后自动返回顶部不便）。
• **canterburry** 对数据中的时间因素感兴趣，询问最佳发帖时间以获得更多关注。
• **mocmoc** 简单评论，提到项目使用claude完成，语气较为模糊。
• **meghanafour** 简单赞赏，语气轻松。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点主要集中在数据准确性上，ChrisMarshallNY和bilekas对项目中提到的最高点数提出质疑，并提供了其他高点数帖子的例子。
• 另一个讨论点是数据的可操作性，baxtr和NAHWheatCracker对如何利用这些数据提出了实际问题和用户体验建议。
• 有用户（namiwang）提出合作建议，希望结合类似项目的力量，共同开发更强大的功能。
• TheEdonian对数据图表的快速增长提出怀疑，涉及到社交媒体数据真实性的普遍问题，如购买点赞等。

这些观点展示了用户对数据准确性、实用性及潜在合作机会的不同看法。

data.title: Consider Knitting
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 这篇文章旨在向长时间面对电脑编程的人推荐编织（广义上包括钩针、编织等纤维艺术）作为一种有益的爱好。作者以自身经历为例，讲述了作为程序员，他在疫情后感受到身体对触觉体验的渴望，而编织提供了这种满足感。编织不仅是触觉上的享受，还能通过不断练习提高技能，带来类似游戏中提升等级的成就感。作者强调，编织可以作为一种冥想式的活动，帮助程序员在工作之外放松身心，并体验手工艺的乐趣。文章呼吁不论背景，编程人士都可以尝试编织，享受其带来的身心平衡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：手工艺活动的选择及其带来的满足感

不同观点：
• [padraigfl] 认为制作弹出式卡片是一种兼具被动和动手乐趣的活动。他享受设计布局、测量和准备材料的过程，并认为这是一种可以边看视频边进行的重复性工作。
• [voidUpdate] 分享了制作玩偶的乐趣，认为这是一种能够自我表达的创作方式，即使成品有时不太完美，也可以作为不错的礼物。
• [tiniuclx] 强调弦乐器演奏带来的即时反馈和手部动作的细微差别，认为音乐比手工艺更具吸引力。
• [lukaslalinsky] 推荐在冬季制作帽子，认为这是一个简单但实用的项目，能够结合图案设计，并且网上有大量教程可供参考。
• [jvanderbot] 喜欢木工，认为除了动手乐趣外，还涉及到数学计算和实用成品的制作。

补充讨论：
• [bonki] 提到钩针编织需要全神贯注，无法同时进行其他活动，这让他感到压力而不是放松。
• [Gigachad] 制作cosplay配件和定制玩偶，认为这是一种非常令人满意的创作活动，因为能够亲手制作并交付给买家。
• [KurSix] 更喜欢十字绣，认为这种手工艺能够满足对触觉和模拟创作的渴望，尤其是在长时间面对数字工作之后。
• [safety1st] 指出，桌面工作或知识型工作缺乏感官刺激，因此需要通过感官解锁的爱好来平衡生活，例如举重和唱歌。
• [jader201] 提到网络上关于编织鸡的流行趋势，似乎对编织的广泛流行感到好奇。
• [pingou] 推广自己开发的编织学习应用Knitting Genius，认为编织与编程有相似之处，且触觉体验非常令人愉悦。
• [rkangel] 将编织比作执行软件，强调编织技术的重复应用可以产生复杂的成品，类似于CPU的工作原理。
• [sergioisidoro] 从编织中学到即使每个部分都是单点失败，也可以创造出美丽且有用的东西，认为这种无冗余的创作过程是一种有价值的体验。
• [davidwilliammr] 对安静编织的理念表示认同，但认为花费大量时间制作如茶巾或毛衣等物品不值得。

art
knitting
Let’s say that, like me, you are a person who stares at a computer and writes
code for a living. As a straight male who grew up in a time where knitting was
very strongly female coded, it for the most part never occurred to me that
knitting was a thing I could do and might enjoy. Regardless of your demographic
categories and background, it’s possible that you have also not really
considered knitting.
This article exists to get you to do so. Specifically, I’ll try to convince you,
one software person to another, why it might be a good fit for your life and
brain. This is a pitch for knitting, but—for better or worse—an extremely
nerdily argued one.
Before I start, note that when I say “knitting”, you can read that as any of the
various
fiber arts
, including crochet, weaving, macramÃ©, cross-stitch, etc.
I talk about knitting here because that’s the one closest to my heart and I
strive to speak from the heart. You can make stuff out of string however you
want. We are all fiber friends.
The sense of touch
I love the aesthetics of programming. Sitting in a cool quiet room, techno
thumping in my headphones, coffee mug next to me, while a neatly arranged field
of glowing monospace glyphs stream across my screen. But there’s one sense
unmentioned in that sentence: touch. The sense we devote more neurons to than
any other is curiously underutilized while pumping out code.
It’s no surprise that some programmers
fetishize
keyboards
. It’s just about the only part of programming that has any physical sensation
at all
.
I got into knitting a few years after the pandemic. While I have a variety of
hobbies, most are still staring at a screen and maybe
pushing some buttons and
turning knobs
. When I wasn’t doing those, I was staring at a screen
for work, or staring at a screen for
not-work
.
I don’t know if I have a good way to explain how much my body craved tactile
experience by the end of that. It’s like my fingers ached. A deep hunger, but
not for taste. I’d wander around the house, driving my wife insane, unable to
sit down and get comfortable. My body was just screaming at me to
do
something.
My youngest daughter had just picked up knitting, and she taught me. At first it
was frustrating and annoying. But once I had the basics down, it was like a a
deep sigh felt in my hands. Knitting is
so
touch-centered. Skilled knitters
can knit without looking at their hands at all—touch alone is sufficient.
There are so many different kinds of yarn to work with and they all feel
different. Cotton is tough and firm, like twine. Wool is soft and springy,
forgiving as you pull stitches open to work them. Superwash wool is smooth and
glides off the needles. Non-superwash wool has this very slight stickiness to it
that makes the resulting fabric feel solid and whole. Thin fingering weight yarn
wraps tightly around your finger like a reminder knot. Working it is like
performing delicate surgery. Squishy chunky wool spreads your fingers wide and
works so quickly it’s like fabric is spooling out of your hands on its own
accord.
Even needles each have their own personality. Stiff grippy bamboo with its dull
clack. Less worrisome to use because stitches don’t slide off as easily, but
harder work to push against the friction. Polished stainless steel where the
stitches just fly off the needles—good when you are done with those stitches
but not so much otherwise.
Once you’ve worked a few thousand stitches into your muscle memory, you can
watch your fingers form stitches almost of their own accord, hypnotically. Right
needle opens the stitch and slides in. Left finger wraps the yarn around the
needle. Right finger grabs yarn. Right hand pulls the needle back out, a new
stitch formed and transferred to the other needle. Over and over, like a
meditation in the body.
Knitting
feels good
. It is an intimate, constant reminder that we are a tool-using species with thousands of years of evolution giving us incredible dexterity and the emotional wiring to make us want to use it.
An open world game with optimized skill curve
Of course, you could get much of that same tactile joy by driving to your
nearest yarn store and wandering around the aisles jamming your fingers into
every ball and skein of yarn they have. (An activity I certainly
also
do and
highly recommend.) Knitting isn’t just about having a hedonistic tactile
experience. It is a skilled art with an unbelievably deep lore.
I
used to be a game programmer
, and I tend to look at a lot of
activities through the lens of game design. Games are interesting because they
are user experience distilled to its essence. When you are, say, using a banking
app to transfer some money into savings, there is a user experience in play. But
there’s also a
utility
, a real effect you are trying to have in the material
world. You may use your banking app and be satisfied that it helps you save
money even if the UX is trash.
But a game, almost by definition, doesn’t
do
anything “out

data.author: peter_d_sherman
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：操作系统研究及其架构设计的有效性和实用性

不同观点：
• [transpute] 列举了多个操作系统和虚拟化技术的研究谱系，包括Xen、KVM、EC2、Barrelfish等，展示了操作系统和虚拟化技术的演变和应用场景，但没有直接表达个人立场，仅提供了背景信息。

• [davemp] 对当前的操作系统研究表示失望，认为大多数操作系统研究只关注基础的调度和外围设备多路复用，离实际可用系统差距较大。他指出，为了实现实用性，通常需要在新的架构上运行Linux，从而丧失新架构的大部分优势。

• [peter_d_sherman] 对Barrelfish操作系统表示兴趣，引用了其设计概述，强调了其多内核架构的特点，即每个核心运行一个小内核，其余部分作为分布式系统进程。这种设计不共享内存，即使是具有缓存一致性的共享内存机器也是如此，只有在传递消息和数据以及启动其他核心时才使用共享内存。

• [andsoitis] 补充了可以下载和运行Barrelfish操作系统的链接，提供了实际操作的可能性，增加了对该操作系统实际应用的讨论。

补充讨论：
• davemp对操作系统研究的基础性和实用性之间的差距提出质疑，认为很多研究成果难以直接应用，需要依赖传统的操作系统（如Linux）来实现实际功能。
• peter_d_sherman则对Barrelfish的具体设计表示兴趣，强调其在多核环境下的独特架构和分布式系统特性，提供了对davemp观点的一种回应和补充。
• andsoitis提供了Barrelfish操作系统的实际下载和运行链接，鼓励实际操作和体验，增加了讨论的实用性。

争议焦点：操作系统研究的基础性和实用性之间的差距，以及如何在新的架构设计中实现实际可用性。

data.title: An illustrated guide to Amazon VPCs
data.author: egonschiele
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了亚马逊VPC（虚拟私有云）的概念及其重要性。VPC是为了解决AWS早期存在的问题而创建的，当时所有用户共享一个网络，导致IP地址冲突和安全风险。IP地址冲突是指不同用户的服务器拥有相同IP地址，这在迁移到AWS时会造成问题。此外，共享网络还可能导致用户之间的数据泄露风险。为了解决这些问题，AWS为每个用户提供了独立的VPC，使他们可以在自己的私有网络中运行服务器，避免IP冲突和安全问题。VPC允许用户将现有的本地服务器连接到AWS，同时保持其原有的IP地址，从而实现平滑的迁移和整合。理解VPC对于使用AWS的其他网络功能至关重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AWS VPC（虚拟私有云）及其安全性和历史演变，以及对算法学习资源的推荐。

不同观点：
• [MehdiHK] 对算法书籍《Grokking Algorithms》表示赞赏，认为它能够帮助 struggling with common data structures and algorithms 的人更轻松地学习算法，并使学习过程变得有趣。该评论虽然与VPC不直接相关，但引出了对技术书籍的推荐，强调了其教育价值和趣味性。

• [davesmylie] 讨论了AWS的历史，特别是对早期AWS资源可被其他客户直接访问的机制表示惊讶，认为这在现代看来是不可思议的，并指出早期互联网资源直接连接到网络是常态。该评论强调了对AWS安全机制演变的关注以及对早期技术环境的反思。

补充讨论：
• [MehdiHK] 的评论引入了对技术书籍的推荐，特别提到《Grokking Algorithms》这本书对初学者的帮助。虽然没有直接讨论VPC，但其评论背景是在VPC相关的讨论中出现的。

• [davesmylie] 的评论涉及AWS早期资源安全性问题，提出了对过去技术实践的质疑，并暗示了技术安全性的进步。这一评论引发了对AWS技术历史演变的讨论，特别是对资源安全性的关注。

争议焦点：
• 尽管两个评论的观点没有直接冲突，但它们反映了不同关注点之间的潜在争议。一方面，[MehdiHK] 关注技术学习和教育资源，强调学习体验的趣味性和有效性；另一方面，[davesmylie] 则关注技术实践的历史和安全性，对早期AWS资源可访问性表示担忧。这可能引发对技术进步与安全性平衡的更深入讨论。

总结：
主要讨论点围绕AWS VPC的历史演变及其安全性和一本算法书籍的推荐。不同评论者分别关注技术教育资源和对云计算安全性的历史反思，反映了技术发展过程中学习与安全性之间的潜在张力。

In this section, I talk about why VPCs were invented and how they work. This is critical to understand because almost everything you do in AWS will happen inside of VPC. If you don't understand VPCs, it will be difficult to understand any of the other networking concepts.
If you're reading this, maybe you have one of these
and you just found out that to put your app on AWS, you need all of this:
And you have no idea what VPCs, subnets and so on are.
I'll help you learn about all those pieces. A little about me, I’m a long-tailed duck, and I run a business selling phones to hackers, called
Blackhatberry
. Now let's get started.
This is the story of VPCs (Virtual Private Cloud)s, our first big topic. Many moons (and suns) ago, some AWS engineers were sitting in a room. They had a serious issue.
"Guys, lets talk business. Why aren't more companies moving to AWS?" they said.
"Maybe because all instances run in a single shared network, which means users can access each other's instances, and see each other's data," someone said.
"Maybe because it's hard for them to move their existing servers to AWS, because of IP address conflicts," someone else said.
"Wait… what are IP address conflicts?”
“And existing servers? Shouldn’t they be moving to
our
servers?”
IP address conflicts
This is the first reason people weren’t switching to AWS. Here's what I mean by IP address conflicts. I own a bunch of servers for Blackhatberry. One of them has the IP address `172.98.0.1`. Now, my neighbor also has a server for her business. She loves my ip address. “Ah, 172.98.0.1, what a beautiful destination,” she says. So she copies my address!
Now we both have servers with the same IP address!
Sidebar: You can find your local IP address using `ipconfig getifaddr en1` (works for Macs for wireless internet connections).
Now you're thinking "so what?". And actually... you're totally right. Even though our servers have the same IP address, they are in
different
networks, so it's not an issue.
But here comes trouble
. Because we both want to get on AWS. But if we have two servers with the same IP address on AWS, that's a problem!
Bam: IP address conflict. Every server in a network needs to have a unique IP address for the same reason that every house in a city needs to have a unique address. Otherwise, if someone has a package, they wouldn't know which house to deliver it to.
Now I know what you're thinking. Why don't you just get new servers in AWS? Why connect your on-prem ("on premises") servers to AWS? Isn't the whole point that you're
moving to AWS?
And sure, we can afford to do that, but there are companies with dozens of on-prem servers. Migrating everything to AWS is simply not an option for them. They need functionality so they can create
new
servers in AWS, but also connect their
existing
, on-prem servers into the
same network
. And this does not work when everyone is part of the same network, because of IP address conflicts.
This was a huge problem for AWS! I mean, see how serious these engineers look:
This IP conflict issue meant people with on-prem servers had no easy way to gradually move to AWS. Think of all the potential customers they were losing!
I'm giving you this background so you can understand why VPCs were invented. IP address conflicts weren't the only issue. In AWS, everyone's servers used to be on the same network, which meant if you were careless, it was easy for anyone to connect to your server and look at all kinds of sensitive data!
For both these reasons, Amazon needed to give each customer their own private network, instead of having them all on the same shared network. And so VPCs were born.
Why do they call it a VPC if you can't see it!
So there are two problems we're trying to solve:
IP address conflicts
The fact that users can access each other's instances because they're in one big shared network.
Remember: duplicate IPs were totally fine when my network and my neighbor's network were separate. What Amazon needed was a way to give each person their own private network, but
inside
AWS
. That way, they could bring their IP addresses with them, and they wouldn't conflict with anyone else's IP addresses.
Maybe you're wondering, "why can't we just change the IP addresses so all machines have a unique IP address?" Well, in networking, you set up some things based around specific IP addresses (I'll get to exactly what stuff later), so that idea would require a lot of work in practice.
Separate networks would also solve the security problem.
This is the big idea behind a VPC: everyone gets their own private network inside AWS.
By the way, why am I spending so long on VPCs? Isn't this post about putting one

data.title: Ask HN: Startup getting spammed with PayPal disputes, what should we do?
data.author: june3739
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何应对通过PayPal进行的钱洗白和欺诈行为，以及如何保护电子商务网站免受恶意交易的影响。

不同观点：
• cookiengineer认为这是一个利用PayPal API漏洞进行的钱洗白计划，涉及example.com和www.example.com域名混淆的问题。建议通过阻断已知的恶意ASN、检查漏洞和虚拟化软件环境来缓解风险，并提供了自建的防火墙和反垃圾项目作为参考。
• tyingq和paxys建议通过配置PayPal账户只接受验证买家的付款，以此作为基础防护措施。
• Foofoobar12345怀疑欺诈者在测试被盗的PayPal账户，并提到与PayPal支持交涉的困难，最终选择关闭PayPal支付。
• dabinat分享了其通过指纹识别和速率限制成功缓解了类似问题的经验，认为减缓恶意用户操作频率是有效的策略。
• noodlesUK警告说PayPal可能会对风险账户进行封禁，建议准备好替代支付服务提供商（PSP）。
• imdavidsantiago提供了多种技术手段，如浏览器指纹识别、完整头信息记录和引入轻微的支付摩擦，以对抗自动化滥用行为，并建议直接联系PayPal的商户技术支持。
• abxyz建议对高风险交易采取手动审核，并强调与PayPal客户经理直接沟通的重要性，以防止账户被封禁。
• kolp推荐使用Cloudflare的WAF规则来阻止TOR和数据中心IP的威胁，并建议寻找PayPal的替代方案。
• cryptonym提到使用TLS指纹识别、行为评分和IP信誉等技术，建议咨询高级CDN供应商或购买独立的机器人检测解决方案。
• gtech1提出直接阻止可疑域名的注册。
• christophilus通过速率限制和IP封锁成功解决问题，认为只要比竞争对手更不容易成为目标即可。
• herbst对PayPal的客户支持不满，建议直接使用信用卡支付以避免相关问题。
• toomuchtodo提出尝试使用Cloudflare的Turnstile来阻止机器人流量。
• rendall则质疑如果忽略问题会有什么后果，并尝试分析对PayPal关系的影响。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于如何有效缓解PayPal支付欺诈问题，部分人建议采取技术手段如指纹识别和速率限制，而另一些人则建议直接联系PayPal客户经理或准备替代支付方案以防账户被封禁。
• 多种技术解决方案被提出，如浏览器指纹识别、CAPTCHA、IP封锁和Cloudflare的Turnstile，显示出社区对技术防护的高度关注。
• 部分讨论者分享了实际经验和具体操作建议，如与PayPal支持交涉的困难和通过手动审核账户来防止欺诈行为的实践。
• 建议商家对PayPal账户风险进行主动管理，并考虑替代支付方案以防不测。

data.title: Meta and Yandex exfiltrating tracking data on Android via WebRTC
data.author: liuandrewk
data.article_summary: 研究发现，Meta和俄罗斯的Yandex通过其嵌入数百万网站的跟踪代码（Meta Pixel和Yandex Metrica），滥用合法互联网协议，绕过Android系统和浏览器的隐私保护，秘密获取用户唯一标识符。这种行为使得这两家公司能够将浏览器的短暂标识符与移动应用中的持久用户身份关联，甚至在隐私浏览模式下也能实现用户去匿名化。该问题仅在Android上发现，原因在于Android对本地通信和后台执行的控制较宽松。Google表示正在调查此滥用行为，并指出这违反了其Play市场的服务条款和用户隐私预期。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google和Meta等大公司对用户数据的安全处理及其商业动机

不同观点：
• 观点一：Google为了最大化利润，故意允许对用户数据的滥用。
  - 论据：Google有能力通过技术手段（如沙盒）保护用户数据，但为了利润而选择不作为。
  - 例子：法院已经证明这些公司不尊重法律，表明它们在数据保护上不够负责。

• 观点二：Google已经在采取措施保护用户数据，技术上也在不断改进。
  - 论据：Android系统本身具备保护用户数据的能力，可能只是需要更好地实施和优化。
  - 例子：沙盒技术的存在说明Google在技术上已有解决方案，只是商业决策上可能有其他考量。

• 观点三：Meta等公司同样存在数据滥用问题，不仅仅是Google。
  - 论据：这些公司普遍存在为了商业利益而忽视数据安全的问题。
  - 例子：Meta也多次被曝出数据泄露和滥用问题，说明这是一个行业普遍现象。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：Google是否故意为了利润而忽视数据安全，还是技术实施和商业决策上的问题。
• 其他讨论：如何通过法律和政策手段迫使这些公司加强数据保护，以及用户自身如何提高数据安全意识。
• 部分评论提到需要更严格的监管和透明度，以防止大公司滥用用户数据。

通过这些观点可以看出，讨论的核心在于大科技公司在用户数据保护上的责任和动机，以及如何通过技术、法律和用户自我保护来解决这些问题。

Tracking code that Meta and Russia-based Yandex embed into millions of websites is de-anonymizing visitors by abusing legitimate Internet protocols, causing Chrome and other browsers to surreptitiously send unique identifiers to native apps installed on a device,
researchers have discovered
. Google says it's investigating the abuse, which allows Meta and Yandex to convert ephemeral web identifiers into persistent mobile app user identities.
The covert tracking—implemented in the
Meta Pixel
and
Yandex Metrica
trackers—allows Meta and Yandex to bypass core security and privacy protections provided by both the Android operating system and browsers that run on it.
Android sandboxing
, for instance, isolates processes to prevent them from interacting with the OS and any other app installed on the device, cutting off access to sensitive data or privileged system resources. Defenses such
as
state
partitioning
and
storage partitioning
, which are built into all major browsers, store site cookies and other data associated with a website in containers that are unique to every top-level website domain to ensure they're off-limits for every other site.
A blatant violation
“One of the fundamental security principles that exists in the web, as well as the mobile system, is called sandboxing,” Narseo Vallina-Rodriguez, one of the researchers behind the discovery, said in an interview. “You run everything in a sandbox, and there is no interaction within different elements running on it. What this attack vector allows is to break the sandbox that exists between the mobile context and the web context. The channel that exists allowed the Android system to communicate what happens in the browser with the identity running in the mobile app.”
The bypass—which Yandex began in 2017 and Meta started last September—allows the companies to pass cookies or other identifiers from Firefox and Chromium-based browsers to native Android apps for Facebook, Instagram, and various Yandex apps. The companies can then tie that vast browsing history to the account holder logged into the app.
This abuse has been observed only in Android, and evidence suggests that the Meta Pixel and Yandex Metrica target only Android users. The researchers say it may be technically feasible to target iOS because browsers on that platform allow developers to programmatically
establish localhost connections
that apps can monitor on local ports.
In contrast to iOS, however, Android imposes fewer controls on local host communications and background executions of mobile apps, the researchers said, while also implementing stricter controls in app store vetting processes to limit such abuses. This overly permissive design allows Meta Pixel and Yandex Metrica to send web requests with web tracking identifiers to specific local ports that are continuously monitored by the Facebook, Instagram, and Yandex apps. These apps can then link pseudonymous web identities with actual user identities, even in private browsing modes, effectively de-anonymizing users’ browsing habits on sites containing these trackers.
Meta Pixel and Yandex Metrica are analytics scripts designed to help advertisers measure the effectiveness of their campaigns. Meta Pixel and Yandex Metrica are estimated to be installed on
5.8 million
and
3 million
sites, respectively.
Meta and Yandex achieve the bypass by abusing basic functionality built into modern mobile browsers that allows browser-to-native app communications. The functionality lets browsers send web requests to local Android ports to establish various services, including media connections through the
RTC protocol
, file sharing, and developer debugging.
A conceptual diagram representing the exchange of identifiers between the web trackers running on the browser context and native Facebook, Instagram, and Yandex apps for Android.
A conceptual diagram representing the exchange of identifiers between the web trackers running on the browser context and native Facebook, Instagram, and Yandex apps for Android.
While the technical underpinnings differ, both Meta Pixel and Yandex Metrica are performing a “weird protocol misuse” to gain unvetted access that Android provides to
localhost ports
on the 127.0.0.1 IP address. Browsers access these ports without user notification. Facebook, Instagram, and Yandex native apps silently listen on those ports, copy identifiers in real time, and link them to the user logged into the app.
A representative for Google said the behavior violates the terms of service for its Play marketplace and the privacy expectations of Android users.
“The developers in this report are using capabilities present in many browsers across iOS and Android in unintended ways that blatantly violate our security and privacy principles,” the representative said, referring to the people who write the Meta

data.title: Show HN: I build one absurd web project every month
data.author: absurdwebsite
data.article_summary: "ABSURD.website" 每月推出一个荒诞的项目，通过各种奇特的产品和服务展示创意。这些项目包括为电商网站增加招财猫动画、为AI出租灵魂、快速语言学习工具、艺术家逝世效应数据库、以及 puzzle 解决服务等。其他项目还有如厕所水香水、隐形内衣、慢递服务、眼睛交友网站等。每个项目都以幽默和反常规的方式呈现，旨在通过荒诞艺术引发思考和娱乐。网站邀请用户订阅以获取每月更新，并参与这些独特的创意实验。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• 一些参与者（如[hinkley]、[90s_dev]、[bradly]）分享了自己制作的非实用但有趣的项目，强调了创造性和娱乐性。例如，制作无用的网站或复杂的个人项目，尽管无实际用途，但带来乐趣和学习机会。
  
• [nathan_douglas]提到了一个复杂且具有教育意义的项目，虽然也是“无用”的，但目的是通过复杂性进行学习，这表明某些“无用”项目实际上可以具备教育价值。

• [fibbery_]提出了一个关于分享和合作社区的问题，指出某些项目兼具技术、艺术和政治批判性，并询问是否存在适合分享这些项目的社区，暗示了对特定社区文化的需求。

• [filoleg]表达了对这些创造性项目的欣赏，认为这些项目尽管看似荒谬，但展示了人类的创造力，值得赞赏。

补充讨论：
• [AnnaPali]指出了一个实际的观点，认为某些项目虽然看似无用，但实际上反映了当前某些工作流程中人与AI的协作方式，指出了技术与人类任务分配的现实联系。

• [westondeboer]和[XetiNA]讨论了特定项目的趣味性，如“艺术家死亡效应数据库”和“无限滚动”的用户界面设计，反映了对项目艺术性和用户体验的思考。

data.title: FFmpeg Merges WebRTC Support
data.author: Sean-Der
data.article_summary:
本文主要介绍了FFmpeg项目中的一些代码变更，特别是新增了对WHIP muxer的支持以及相关的配置和文档更新。WHIP是一种基于WebRTC的低延迟流媒体传输协议。更新内容包括：

1. **配置文件更改**：
   - 增加了对`whip_muxer`的依赖检测，特别是对`openssl`的版本要求（≥1.0.1k）。
   - 更新了TLS和DTLS协议的依赖和选择逻辑，主要涉及`openssl`。

2. **文档更新**：
   - 在`muxers.texi`文件中添加了关于WHIP muxer的详细说明，包括其工作原理、使用示例和支持的选项。
   - WHIP muxer通过HTTP协议交换SDP和ICE信息，使用STUN和DTLS建立会话，并通过SRTP加密传输音视频数据。
   - 提供了一个使用示例，演示如何将输入文件转换为WebRTC流，并建议使用H.264编码（无B帧）和Opus音频编码。

3. **代码文件变更**：
   - 修改了`Makefile`文件，增加了对WHIP muxer的对象文件依赖。
   - 更新了多个源文件，如`configure`、`tls.c`、`http.c`等，以支持新的muxer和协议。

总体而言，这次更新主要为FFmpeg添加了对低延迟WHIP协议的支持，并完善了相关文档和配置。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：WebRTC广播技术的应用前景及WHIP协议的支持情况

不同观点：
• Sean-Der表达了对WebRTC广播技术的高度期待，认为这是一个令人兴奋的技术进展。他特别提到Broadcast Box项目，并在他的README文档中列出了支持这一技术的原因。
• Sean-Der指出，GStreamer、OBS和FFmpeg现在都支持WHIP（WebRTC HTTP Ingestion Protocol），这为各种平台（包括移动端、网页、嵌入式系统和广播软件等）提供了一个统一的视频广播协议。

补充讨论：
• WHIP协议的支持被视为实现跨平台视频广播的重要一步，这将极大地方便不同设备和软件之间的互操作性。
• Sean-Der的观点中隐含了对技术统一和标准化的重要性的强调，认为WHIP协议的支持将简化开发者在不同平台上实现视频广播的工作。
• 争议的焦点可能在于新技术的普及和应用速度，以及在实际应用中是否能够如预期般顺畅运行。此外，不同平台对WHIP协议的支持程度和技术细节也可能引发进一步的讨论。

总结来看，评论主要围绕WebRTC广播技术的潜力和WHIP协议的支持所带来的便利展开，表达了对该技术前景的乐观态度，同时也指出了标准化在技术发展中的重要性。

data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: Armin Ronacher在博客中分享了他对AI迅速发展的思考。他描述了自己从手动编程转向使用AI工具（如Claude Code）的经历，感受到工作效率和生活平衡的显著改善。尽管编程速度没有明显加快，但AI让他有更多时间做其他事情，如看书或陪伴家人。他认为，AI正在彻底改变人类的生活、工作、学习和交流方式，且这种变化不可逆。他反思了自己从对AI持怀疑态度到接受并乐观其未来的过程，强调AI已超越了单纯工具的范畴，正成为创新和创造的全新基础。他还提到，AI的广泛应用引发了对教育和全球经济影响的深思，并预测各国将争夺AI控制权。尽管有人对AI持怀疑态度，Ronacher对其带来的变革感到兴奋，认为这是不可逆转且充满潜力的开端。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI工具（如Claude）对编程效率的影响

不同观点：
• csomar认为，虽然使用了AI工具（如Claude），但编程速度并没有显著提升。他指出，尽管AI工具帮他节省了不少时间，但他感觉整体的“交付”速度变化不大。他的论据是，编写代码本身并不特别耗时，耗时的是测试、部署、解决奇怪的bug、写文档、注册服务等其他任务。

• 隐含观点：另一可能的立场是，AI工具在某些编程任务（如代码生成）上确实有效，但并没有显著改善整个开发流程的效率。这是因为开发过程还包括许多其他耗时的环节，而这些环节AI工具目前无法显著优化。

补充讨论：
• csomar提到，只有在进行加密或数学相关编程时，代码编写本身可能更耗时。这暗示了AI工具在处理复杂逻辑或算法时可能更有价值。
• 争议焦点在于AI工具对整体开发效率的实际影响。虽然AI工具能够提升某些具体任务的效率，但整体开发流程的效率提升可能并不明显，因为其他非编码任务仍然耗时。

44178147.article_content:
Armin Ronacher
's Thoughts and Writings
blog
archive
tags
projects
talks
about
AI Changes Everything
written on Wednesday, June 4, 2025
At the moment I'm
working on a new project
.
Even over the last two months, the way I do this has changed profoundly.
Where I used to spend most of my time in Cursor, I now mostly use
Claude
Code
, almost entirely
hands-off.
Do I program any faster?  Not really.  But it feels like I've gained 30%
more time in my day because the machine is doing the work.  I alternate
between giving it instructions, reading a book, and reviewing the changes.
If you would have told me even just six months ago that I'd prefer being
an engineering lead to a virtual programmer intern over hitting the keys
myself, I would not have believed it.  I can go can make a coffee, and
progress still happens.  I can be at the playground with my youngest while
work continues in the background.  Even as I'm writing this blog post,
Claude is doing some refactorings.
While all this is happening, I've found myself reflecting a lot on what AI
means to the world and I am becoming increasingly optimistic about our
future.  It's obvious now that we're undergoing a tremendous shift.  AI is
out of the bottle, and there's no putting it back.  Even if we halted all
progress today, froze the weights, halted the training, the systems
already out there would still reshape how we live, work, learn, and
communicate to one another.
What however took longer to accept is just how
profound
that change
really is.  As an engineer coming from a world of deterministic things,
who deeply values the craft of engineering, to accept the messiness of
what agents are doing took a while to digest.  It took me a while to even
warm up to tool usage by AI in the first place â just two years ago I was
convinced
AI might kill my wife
.  In
those two years however we can incredibly far.  We have reached the point
where even if we stopped here (and there is no indication we will) AI is
already a new substrate for a lot of new innovation, ideas and creations
and I'm here for it.  It has moved beyond being a curious tool.
Never before have I seen a technology surface in every day life so
quickly, so widely.  Smartphones adoption felt slow in comparison.  Today
I can't finish a commute or coffee without spotting someone chatting with
ChatGPT.  I've had conversations with baristas, hairdressers, parents at
the playground â people who aren't what I would consider âtech-savvyâ â
telling me how AI changed the way they write letters, search for recipes,
help their kids with homework, or translate documents.  The ripple effect
is already massive. And still, the majority of the world hasn't touched
these tools yet.  Entire communities, professions, and economies are yet
to begin exploring their transformation.
That's what makes this moment feel so strange â half revolutionary, half
prelude.  And yet, oddly, there are so many technologists who are
holdouts.  How could techies reject this change?  Thomas Ptacek's piece
â
My AI Skeptic Friends Are All Nuts
â really resonated with me.  It
takes a humorous stab at the push against AI that is taking place from my
very circles.  Why is it that so many people I've respected in tech for
years â engineers, open source contributors â are the ones most resistant
to what's happening?  We've built something beyond what we imagined, and
instead of being curious, many are dismissive and denying its
capabilities.  What is that?
Of course the implications are vast and real and the rapid development
forces big questions.  What does this mean for the education of our
children?  If AI can teach, explain, and personalize lessons better than a
classroom of thirty ever could, what becomes of schools as we know them?
And if kids grow up expecting to interact with intelligence â not just
absorb content â how do we teach them to reason, create, and collaborate
in ways that leverage this power without becoming dependent on it?
On the global stage, there are also ramifications that seem more
fundamental than in previous cycles.  It does not feel like the rise of
search engines or social media, where the rest of the world was satisfied
with being a consumer of US infrastructure.  This feels more like the
invention of the steam engine.  Once it existed, there was no future
without it.  No country could afford to stay on the sidelines.  But steam
machines also became quickly commoditized and there was plenty of
competition of manufacturers.  It was just too obvious of a technological
leap.  With AI, every nation, every corporation will want its own models,
its own control, its own stake in the future.
And so, as I alternate between delegating tasks to Claude and reading
something thoughtful in between, I can't help but feel excited about being
there when we're at the beginning of something irreversible and expansive.
I understand why it's tempting to be cynical or fearful.  For sure the job
of programmers and art

data.title: Why I Use a Dumbphone in 2025 (and Why You Should Too)
data.author: rd_wei
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在2025年使用无应用程序、无社交媒体的“笨手机”带来的好处，主要分为技术和心理两方面。心理上，这种手机有助于减少分心，提升注意力质量，降低认知过载，增加与现实世界的互动。短视频等内容让许多人上瘾，导致注意力持续时间缩短，而笨手机帮助打破这种成瘾性，提高工作效率。技术上，笨手机电池续航长达三天，保护隐私，设计简洁实用。虽然切换到笨手机不意味着完全放弃智能功能，但能有效减少不必要的使用，让生活更专注和自由。文章鼓励尝试使用旧式手机，以体验其诸多益处。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人们对是否应放弃智能手机或限制其使用存在不同看法，主要涉及智能手机的必要性、实用性、对注意力的影响以及社会沟通方式的变化。

不同观点：
• [puttycat] 认为智能手机上的某些应用（如银行、WhatsApp等）是必需的，一旦需要使用这些应用，就难以摆脱对智能手机的依赖。例如，银行业务需要通过手机应用验证在线购买，因此完全摆脱智能手机是不现实的。

• [nehal3m] 对摆脱智能手机的诱惑表示理解，并认同其有助于提升注意力、功能分区以及减少第三方追踪。然而，现代智能手机非常实用，完全放弃会失去很多便利。虽然可以通过一些策略（如灰度模式、关闭通知等）限制其使用，但保持这种状态需要持续的警惕和努力。

• [yyx] 认为不一定要安装那些消耗注意力的应用（如TikTok、Instagram Shorts、YouTube Reels），可以选择安装那些不需要持续关注的有用应用，以此保持智能手机的实用性而不被其绑架。

• [freehorse] 指出，现代沟通方式主要依赖聊天应用（如WhatsApp、Signal等），如果不使用这些应用，就几乎没有与他人沟通的方式。这意味着完全放弃智能手机或将其留在家里并不现实。

• [crypt1d] 支持摆脱智能手机的想法，但指出如果工作主要依赖电脑，这个想法很快就会遇到问题。

• [ivape] 提出，摆脱智能手机可以让人们更专注于与面前的人交流。然而，现代社会中许多人缺乏真正的社交联系，社会已经偏离了正常轨道。需要某种形式的社会崩溃，让人们重新学会彼此的名字和面对面的交流。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于智能手机的必要性和实用性之间的平衡。一方面，某些应用和服务使得完全摆脱智能手机变得困难；另一方面，人们也认识到智能手机对注意力和个人生活的负面影响，试图通过各种策略限制其使用。

• 社会沟通方式的变化（从传统的短信和电话转向聊天应用）也被认为是难以摆脱智能手机的重要原因。

• 有人提出，现代社会的整体问题不仅仅是智能手机本身，而是更广泛的社会联系和沟通方式的变化。

44178418.article_content:
Imagine living in 2025 without notifications, without constant updates. While everyone carries a phone in their pocket with a thousand reasons to get distracted, I use a phone without apps, without social media, without distractions. Many would say I’m limited, but I say I’m free.
Why?
When talking about reasons why someone should switch to a dumbphone, I believe we need to separate two types of benefits: technical and mental. The technical benefits relate to the device’s productivity and efficiency, while the human benefits are connected to us as humans-beings who can easily get distracted and lose hours watching content we don’t even care about.
Mental Benefits
Mental benefits improve the quality of our attention, reduce cognitive overload, and allow us to be more present throughout the day. Here are some of the most important mental benefits of using a dumbphone:
Addiction is real
With the rise of short-form content (TikTok, Instagram Shorts, YouTube Reels), it has become incredibly easy to damage our attention span. Addiction to this type of content is real, it’s not just some outdated “boomer” opinion. It’s here, affecting many of us, and data proves it! A Microsoft study showed that the average attention span dropped from 12 seconds in the 2000s to 8 seconds in 2013. Today, in 2025, the estimated average attention span is 7 seconds, even
less than that of a goldfish
, which is estimated at 9 seconds.
As the chart shows, attention spans are plummeting. Today’s social media is like a drug, with the only difference being that it’s free.
Productivity
One of the most surprising effects of switching to a dumbphone has been its direct impact on my productivity. Without notifications, constant messages, or the temptation to “just check something real quick,” I rediscovered how much real time there is in a day.
Work sessions became deeper and less fragmented, and (linking back to the first point) my ability to concentrate improved dramatically. Plus, my mind feels less tired because it’s not constantly interrupted. With a smartphone, just one notification can cost you 15 minutes lost on Reddit.
Studies like
this one
have shown that merely having your smartphone in sight reduces your cognitive capacity.
Real (and Healthy) Relationships
Do I really need to explain this? When you don’t have a smartphone within reach, you actually start listening to the person in front of you. You’re truly present. You don’t check messages while talking, don’t scroll while walking or taking a break ,you begin to appreciate the world as it is, noticing small details you previously overlooked.
Technical Benefits
Technical benefits refer to the practical and functional features of the dumbphone. Paradoxically, going back actually offers more advantages than moving forward.
Battery Lasts 3 Days (Not 3 Hours)
Although it may sound trivial, it’s worth emphasizing: the battery life of a dumbphone is LEGENDARY. You literally only need to charge it once every three days at most, and charging takes very little time. Plus, removable batteries are super convenient if you want to be sure you never run out of power.
Privacy
For me, this could fit under mental benefits, but it’s more appropriate here. It’s no secret that most apps these days (all for some people) collect data to exploit or sell it. Personally, I’m very pragmatic about privacy ,there’s no freedom without privacy, and there’s no real freedom with a smartphone.
Nowadays, it’s incredibly hard to have a smartphone that truly keeps your activities private, especially with Google’s digital signature system making rooted devices unusable. In this context, a dumbphone is perfect ,it has no GPS, no Wi-Fi, nothing that tracks you.
Minimal and Functional Design
All dumbphones have small screens and simple buttons. From a software perspective, there’s not much to say. This is actually a delicate topic, as the definition of dumbphone is still debated. Some say a phone with WhatsApp but all other dumbphone features counts, others disagree. Personally, I believe even a simple messaging app like WhatsApp ruins the true experience a dumbphone offers. When using a dumbphone, everything is simpler, more straightforward. If you need to reach someone, you call them directly instead of writing a message and waiting for a reply ,and they do the same with you.
It’s Not All or Nothing
Switching from a smartphone to a dumbphone
doesn’t mean
abandoning WhatsApp, Reddit, or YouTube altogether. It means using them less frequently. You can still access these platforms on your PC, which naturally reduces how often you check them and limits usage to only what’s necessary, exactly what we’re trying to achieve!
Conclusion
There are many other benefits I didn’t go into, like improved sleep quality (blue light is harmful), durability and sturdiness, ease of repair, and so on. I hope this list of reasons to buy an old used phone and ditch your smartphone inspires you to try it. I want to stress that switching to a d

About the role
Depot is the fastest place to build software. Our platform integrates with services and tools like GitHub Actions, Docker, Bazel, Gradle, Turborepo, and more to make builds exponentially faster, saving our customers collective decades of build time every month.
To support our rapidly growing customer base, we are looking for our first
Enterprise Support Engineer
, based within a few hours of GMT (UTC+0) to join our team.
About the job
You will become a customer-facing subject-matter expert on CI/CD optimization, Docker, and build tools across a variety of languages and technologies
You will advise customers on best practices and handle technical support requests
You will identify product and resource gaps in customer contexts and work with the founders to prioritize and escalate them
You will assist customers migrating from legacy build infrastructure to take full advantage of Depot’s platform
About you
You are able to debug and troubleshoot issues, combining experience and intuition to find root causes for bugs and issues
You are comfortable in front of customers, able to assist but also empower them to become successful on their own
You are comfortable stepping outside your comfort zone. We assist customers with their GitHub Actions workflows, give recommendations for Dockerfile optimizations, debug performance regressions, and generally see a wide range of build and CI configurations
You can operate independently, but know when to flag for help
You know how to work under pressure in times of urgency. Blocked build pipelines can mean not deploying critical fixes to production, not hitting deadlines, etc, so we and our customers take issues seriously
You are a skilled communicator who can explain, articulate, and present things clearly & concisely in both asynchronous and synchronous settings
What you will need
DevOps consulting or similar customer-facing technical experience
Working knowledge of CI/CD platforms, e.g. GitHub Actions
Working knowledge of Docker, Dockerfiles, and container build optimizations
Working knowledge of major cloud platforms, Kubernetes, or other services that DevOps engineers are likely to interface with
Strong ability to communicate directly with customers, via email, Slack, or on a video call
What would be helpful
Experience with GitHub Actions optimization
Experience with BuildKit and/or advanced Dockerfile features (buildx, multi-stage builds)
API integration experience, to help our customers integrate our programmatic build API into their platforms
Previous consulting experience in DevOps, CI migration, or containerization
About
Depot
Depot is a build acceleration and developer productivity platform that saves companies like PostHog, Wistia, Semgrep, and Secoda thousands of hours in build time every week.
We are developers. We started Depot because we were frustrated with the constant pain of slow build performance. We were fed up waiting for builds and annoyed by the lack of tooling and providers that actually made builds performant. So, we went and built the solution we had always wanted.
Slow builds are the dam standing in the way between mediocrity and innovation. They’re wasteful, expensive, and a drain on developer happiness & productivity. They slow down innovation.
Taking a 40-minute build down to a minute, changes everything. We help folks save literal years in build time every single week.
And we’re just getting started. For us, it’s all about iteration speed and keeping developers in their flow state.
Our mission is to be relentless in accelerating software development.

44144299.article_content:
Dan Puttick
Writing a postmortem: an interview exercise I really like
2017-10-31
First, some exciting news that’s relevant as context: starting in November, I’ll be joining
Mapbox
in their Washington,
DC
office. One thing that made me excited about joining Mapbox was how much I enjoyed their
interview process
. No part of it felt like it required extra “preparation” and it was clear that some significant thought had been put into its design. In my opinion, this is a pretty useful signal about an engineering organization. If we accept that finding great engineers (by whatever definition of “great” you subscribe to) is one of the largest contributors to the success of any company, it’s possible that a company with an interview process that appears disorganized or nonsensical is otherwise well-functioning, but it’s probably at least somewhat less likely.
One aspect of the Mapbox interview process that I particularly liked was their request that I write a blameless postmortem as a take-home exercise. If the term is unfamiliar, postmortems are a tool designed to help facilitate a culture of building institutional knowledge and learning from the past. Whenever something goes wrong – an outage, bug in production, failure to meet an
SLA
, etc – anybody involved in the situation can call for a postmortem. The postmortem takes the form of a shared document where everybody can contribute their account of the incident to help identify its ultimate causes and propose changes to prevent it from happening again. The “blameless” aspect is crucial: a good postmortem avoids conclusions like “Dan wrote a bug and it brought down our service” and instead says “Dan wrote a bug and it brought down the service: we need to improve our testing and deployment processes to make sure that they catch this category of bugs in the future.” For many mistakes that initially look like they ought to be blamed on an individual, it’s possible to identify a deficiency in a process as the root cause. You can read more about blameless postmortems in the
Google
SRE
book
.
I thought this exercise was a great interview question because it lets the reader learn more about several different attributes that one might associate with good programmers:
It’s a sample of the type of written communication you’ll be doing frequently in a work environment. Between documentation, taking notes while working, design documents, commit messages, chat, and email, programmers can produce significantly more prose than  code. Being able to express technical concepts clearly, unambiguously, and succinctly is essential. I may be wrong, but I sometimes get the feeling that this is widely acknowledged, but without the accompanying recognition that writing is a skill that can be improved relatively easily. Producing excellent writing might take a lot of work, but learning to write
decently
isn’t that different from improving as a programmer: it takes building up experience, practicing deliberately, taking the time to revise repeatedly, and getting constructive feedback.
It’s a great way for the writer to demonstrate their ability to assume the perspective of others. So much of being a good engineer is having empathy for your users and the other programmers who will read, modify, or interact with your code. Writing a useful postmortem necessarily requires empathy, because you have to put yourself in the shoes of everybody involved in the incident and understand what they were thinking and why they took the actions they did.
It helps assess the writer’s ability to think critically and logically about a complex chain of events. Imagining all possible contributing factors to an incident and identifying the various links of causality is the same type of thinking as is required when trying to think of edge cases or identify the tradeoffs and compromises in a system’s design. Finding ultimate rather than proximate causes, dismissing alternate explanations, and considering counterfactuals are all closely related to the type of critical thinking involved in debugging software or troubleshooting systems.
When I sat down to write my postmortem, I wasn’t sure whether to analyze a programming-related incident or choose something else. The instructions said the postmortem could be about anything I liked, and I decided it might be fun to write about a certain eventful and unusual accident that happened to me a few years ago. What I wrote is definitely not perfect, it’s just one example, and there’s no one “right” way to format or organize a postmortem. Anyway, I’m excited about the new job, and feel free to reach out if you’re curious about the Mapbox hiring process or what it’s like to work there (you should probably give me some time after I’ve started for the latter). Here’s what I sent the hiring team, unedited, in full:

data.title: X's new "encrypted" XChat feature doesn't seem to be any more secure
data.article_summary: Elon Musk's X platform has introduced "XChat," a new direct messaging feature claimed to have "Bitcoin-style encryption" and a "whole new architecture." However, experts are skeptical, as the Bitcoin blockchain does not use encryption. The feature is marketed as secure, but lacks details on end-to-end encryption (E2EE), raising concerns about privacy. The help page warns that X can still access and compromise messages under legal processes, similar to previous versions. Critics, including Matthew Hodgson of Element, argue that XChat lacks transparency, control, and true encryption, suggesting it may not be as secure as claimed. The platform's privacy practices and past data collection also fuel doubts about XChat's safety.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Twitter（或X平台）的端到端加密直接消息（EDM）实现及其安全性

不同观点：
• **[mjg59]**：认为当前的EDM实现使用了libsodium密封盒和juicebox.xyz协议来存储密钥材料。虽然技术本身没问题，但身份未验证导致易受中间人攻击（MITM）。同时，juicebox协议要求远程存储加密密钥材料，如果Twitter自己控制这些存储领域，用户需信任Twitter不会滥用这些数据。尽管需要PIN来解密，但由于PIN只有4位数，通过GPU暴力破解仅需约一秒。此外，该方案不具备前向安全性，一旦密钥泄露，所有历史消息都可被解密。总体认为这不是一个真正有效的端到端加密方案。

44178008.article_content:
Security
36
X's new 'encrypted' XChat feature seems no more secure than the failure that came before it
36
Musk's 'Bitcoin-style encryption' claim has experts scratching their heads
Brandon Vigliarolo
Tue 3 Jun 2025
//
18:02 UTC
Elon Musk's X social media platform is rolling out a new version of its direct messaging feature that the platform owner said had a "whole new architecture," but as with many a Muskian proclamation, there's reason to doubt what's been said.
Dubbed "XChat" (not to be confused with the venerable Linux/Windows IRC app of the same name), Musk informally
announced
the feature on Sunday, a few days after the company formerly known as Twitter
paused
encryption on messaging to make "some improvements.".
Musk's declaration, however, didn't reveal much about the nature of the changes, and has been enough to cause some encryption experts to doubt what was stated by the world's richest man.
"All new XChat is rolling out with encryption, vanishing messages and the ability to send any kind of file," Musk said in a tweet. "Also, audio/video calling.
"This is built on Rust with (Bitcoin style) encryption, whole new architecture," Musk added. And here's where the skeptics and cryptocurrency fans in the digital town square pounced: There ain't no encryption on the Bitcoin blockchain.
As reported by crypto news site
Coindesk
, experts have been quick to point out that, while there's plenty of cryptography and digital signing involved in Bitcoin, the blockchain itself isn't encrypted, and there really isn't such a thing as "Bitcoin style encryption."
In other words, it's worth questioning whether XChat is going to be encrypted in a way that most people think of encrypted chat: End-to-end encryption (E2EE) that renders messages completely unreadable by anyone who might happen to snoop in them, be it an illicit intermediary or the platform that hosts the messages itself. That's how Signal and Meta-owned WhatsApp work.
As was the case
in 2023
, when then-Twitter first announced encrypted messages under owner Elon Musk, it doesn't appear that XChat will offer true E2EE. The
help page
, which was updated with the launch of the service, still warns "currently, we do not offer protections against man-in-the-middle attacks" and says that Twitter itself, "as a result of a compulsory legal process," could compromise so-called encrypted DMs on the platform without the sender or receiver being aware.
The help page does say that messages are stored on X infrastructure in an encrypted format, and are only decrypted once received "so that they can be read by the user." That sounds a lot like E2EE, but it's crucial to note that the old version of the encrypted DM help page said the same thing, followed by that "we-can-still-read-your-messages" warning, so take that with a grain of salt. Perhaps the details will become clearer once X releases a whitepaper and open-sources its implementation of Xchat, as it promised to do "later this year."
X marks the drop for European users
Musk's DOGE muzzled on X over tape storage baloney
Elon's latest X-periment: Blocked users can still stalk your public tweets
Musk's xAI swallows Musk's X in ego-friendly, all-stock deal
Safety not guaranteed
Skeptics about the new Xchat's privacy include Matthew Hodgson, the co-founder and CEO of encrypted messaging platform Element, used by the US military, NATO, the United Nations, and other highly secure organizations.
"XChat looks to be just another centralized platform where users have zero control over their data," Hodgson said in a statement emailed to
The Register
. "Elon Musk says it's 'encrypted' but offers no technical transparency, no audits, no open source, just vague references to Bitcoin-style architecture."
Hodgson referred to allegations that Musk's
position at DOGE
potentially gave him access to sensitive government data and the personal information of US citizens, as well as
reports
claiming the social media platform formerly known as Twitter had collected more data than necessary. He claims both are reasons to question whether XChat is anywhere as safe to use as Musk claims.
"Such actions highlight a pattern of data handling that prioritizes X rather than its users," Hodgson said. Anything less than "open protocols, transparency and decentralization," said the Element chief, "is just marketing."
We've reached out to X to get more details on the nature of XChat, but didn't immediately hear back. ®

data.title: Decentralization Hidden in the Dark Ages
data.author: palmfacehn
data.article_summary: 本文简要探讨了中世纪的分权社会，特别是后罗马时期欧洲的治理模式，挑战了“黑暗时代”的刻板印象。作者指出，中世纪的法律基于地方传统和文化，国王也需遵守法律，无权单方面更改。每个自由人对自己土地拥有主权，税收是自愿的。国王的合法性来自民众的同意，而非世袭或神权。此时的社会以法律为最高准则，国王与贵族都有责任维护法律。与现代政府不同，当时贵族有义务抵制超越权限的国王。作者引用Hans-Hermann Hoppe和Fritz Kern的观点，强调中世纪的法律至上原则，与后来的专制主义形成对比。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对宪法形式、中世纪社会与现代社会的对比以及权力结构的讨论

不同观点：
• **pcaharrier** 认为宪法形式虽然在名义上保护了君主不受人民影响，但对限制君主的行动几乎没有作用，甚至相比中世纪的社会自由有所倒退。他质疑现代宪法是否真的能保护人民自由。

• **GuB-42** 解释“黑暗时代”中的“黑暗”应理解为历史记录的缺乏，而非当时生活特别糟糕。他认为“黑暗 ages”这个术语现在更多指的是难以获取信息，而不是邪恶或悲惨。

• **rimbo789** 持极端看法，认为中世纪的统治者如果有手段，会像斯大林一样集中权力。这一观点暗示了人类统治者普遍的集权倾向，无论时代如何。

• **jongjong** 批评现代法律体系过于关注字面解释而非伦理和意图，导致法律漏洞。他还抨击了有限责任和公司人格等概念，认为这些是现代社会腐败的根源，并将其与历史上的奴隶制度进行类比，指出不公正的社会秩序依赖于虚假叙事。

• **lou1306** 反对“中世纪社会缺乏记录所以更分散”的观点，指出蛮族王国在476年后不久就开始恢复记录，并且中世纪的分权结构并不隐蔽，甚至有相关电子游戏（如《十字军之王II》）反映这一主题。

• **dunkeltaenzer** 从历史和神话的角度探讨了中央集权与分散权力的斗争，认为罗马和埃及的文化创伤通过宗教和神话代代相传，最终演变为现代社会的结构性问题。他强调了过去智慧和现代社会问题的联系，并提出通过重新连接传统文化来修复这些问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是中世纪社会是否真的比现代社会更加自由分散。**pcaharrier** 和 **jongjong** 都对现代宪法和法律体系持批判态度，而 **lou1306** 则为中世纪的记录和法律体系辩护。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是对“黑暗 ages”的不同理解。**GuB-42** 强调历史记录的缺乏，而 **dunkeltaenzer** 则从更深层次的文化和神话角度分析该时期。

• **jongjong** 和 **dunkeltaenzer** 都对现代社会的权力结构提出了深刻批评，尽管他们使用的论据和历史背景不同。前者侧重于法律漏洞和经济理论的批判，而后者从更广泛的文化和历史创伤角度进行分析。

• 总体来看，评论者们对于中世纪与现代社会的对比、宪法和法律体系的有效性以及权力结构的道德性存在明显分歧。

A man’s home truly was his castle.
Although the term has fallen out of use in the academic
community, for many this period is known as the Dark Ages – with all of the associated
stereotypes: barbarians, boorish behavior, and the uncivilized society that
came to Europe with the fall of the much more civilized Rome.
From
Wikipedia
:
The Dark Ages is a historical
period used for the first part of the Middle Ages. The term emphasizes the
cultural and economic deterioration that supposedly occurred in Europe
following the decline of the Roman Empire.
The label employs traditional
light-versus-darkness imagery to contrast the "darkness" of the
period with earlier and later periods of "light".
The (Not So) Dark Ages
How
did people live absent a strong central power (Rome)?
In what manners was governance achieved?
How did such a society evolve over the centuries
into the nation-states of Europe?
From
whose perspective were these ages “dark”?
Hans-Hermann
Hoppe, in
his essay entitled
“On the Impossibility of
Limited Government and the Prospects for a Second American Revolution,” makes
reference to certain aspects of this time period in history:
Feudal lords and kings did not typically fulfill the
requirements of a state; they could only "tax" with the consent of
the taxed, and on his own land every free man was as much a sovereign (ultimate
decision maker) as the feudal king was on his.
Tax payments
were voluntary.
On his land, each free
man was as sovereign as the king.
This
doesn’t seem so “dark.”
Hoppe
quotes Robert Nisbet:
The subordination of king to law was one of the most
important of principles under feudalism.
The
king was below the law.
This might be
one factor as to why the time period is kept “dark.”
Hoppe
references a book by Fritz Kern, “
Kingship and Law in the Middle
Ages
.”
The book was originally written in German in
1914, and is a thorough and eye-opening examination of the relationship of king
and lord during this time period, as well as the relationship of both king and lord
to the law.
I will rely upon, and will
quote extensively, from this book throughout this essay.
Except as noted, all quoted items will be
from this book.
During
the early Middle Ages, there was no concept of a Divine Right of Kings, nor did
the earlier period hold to the idea of kingship by birthright.
These ideas developed over the centuries and
only took shape in the late Middle Ages.
Contrary to these, in the early Middle Ages…
…an act of popular will was an essential element in the
foundation of government….
To
become king required consent of those doing the choosing.
Additionally, the king did not hold absolute
power:
…even the rudiments of an absolutist doctrine had scarcely
appeared.
Both
the king and the people were subservient to the law – and not an arbitrary law,
but a law based on custom, “the laws of one’s fathers.”
All well-founded private rights were protected from
arbitrary change….
Germanic and ecclesiastical opinion were firmly agreed on
the principle, which met with no opposition until the age of Machiavelli, that
the State exists for the realization of the Law; the power of the State is the
means, the Law is the end-in-itself; the monarch is dependent on the Law, which
is superior to him, and upon which his own existence is based.
The
king and the people were not bound to each other, but each was bound to the
Law, giving all parties responsibility to see that the integrity of the Law is
maintained.
A breech by one imposed an
obligation on the other to correct the breech.
The relationship of each party (king and lord) was to the Law, not to
the other party, and each had duty to protect it.
Contrast
this to the situation today: whereas today it is an illegal act for the people
to resist the government authority, during this period after the fall of Rome
the lords had a duty to resist the king who overstepped his authority.
This is not to say that such challenges went
unopposed by the king –physical enforcement by the lords wa
44177797.article_summary: 本文简要探讨了中世纪的分权社会，特别是后罗马时期欧洲的治理模式，挑战了“黑暗时代”的刻板印象。作者指出，中世纪的法律基于地方传统和文化，国王也需遵守法律，无权单方面更改。每个自由人对自己土地拥有主权，税收是自愿的。国王的合法性来自民众的同意，而非世袭或神权。此时的社会以法律为最高准则，国王与贵族都有责任维护法律。与现代政府不同，当时贵族有义务抵制超越权限的国王。作者引用Hans-Hermann Hoppe和Fritz Kern的观点，强调中世纪的法律至上原则，与后来的专制主义形成对比。
44177797.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对宪法形式、中世纪社会与现代社会的对比以及权力结构的讨论

不同观点：
• **pcaharrier** 认为宪法形式虽然在名义上保护了君主不受人民影响，但对限制君主的行动几乎没有作用，甚至相比中世纪的社会自由有所倒退。他质疑现代宪法是否真的能保护人民自由。

• **GuB-42** 解释“黑暗时代”中的“黑暗”应理解为历史记录的缺乏，而非当时生活特别糟糕。他认为“黑暗 ages”这个术语现在更多指的是难以获取信息，而不是邪恶或悲惨。

• **rimbo789** 持极端看法，认为中世纪的统治者如果有手段，会像斯大林一样集中权力。这一观点暗示了人类统治者普遍的集权倾向，无论时代如何。

• **jongjong** 批评现代法律体系过于关注字面解释而非伦理和意图，导致法律漏洞。他还抨击了有限责任和公司人格等概念，认为这些是现代社会腐败的根源，并将其与历史上的奴隶制度进行类比，指出不公正的社会秩序依赖于虚假叙事。

• **lou1306** 反对“中世纪社会缺乏记录所以更分散”的观点，指出蛮族王国在476年后不久就开始恢复记录，并且中世纪的分权结构并不隐蔽，甚至有相关电子游戏（如《十字军之王II》）反映这一主题。

• **dunkeltaenzer** 从历史和神话的角度探讨了中央集权与分散权力的斗争，认为罗马和埃及的文化创伤通过宗教和神话代代相传，最终演变为现代社会的结构性问题。他强调了过去智慧和现代社会问题的联系，并提出通过重新连接传统文化来修复这些问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是中世纪社会是否真的比现代社会更加自由分散。**pcaharrier** 和 **jongjong** 都对现代宪法和法律体系持批判态度，而 **lou1306** 则为中世纪的记录和法律体系辩护。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是对“黑暗 ages”的不同理解。**GuB-42** 强调历史记录的缺乏，而 **dunkeltaenzer** 则从更深层次的文化和神话角度分析该时期。

• **jongjong** 和 **dunkeltaenzer** 都对现代社会的权力结构提出了深刻批评，尽管他们使用的论据和历史背景不同。前者侧重于法律漏洞和经济理论的批判，而后者从更广泛的文化和历史创伤角度进行分析。

• 总体来看，评论者们对于中世纪与现代社会的对比、宪法和法律体系的有效性以及权力结构的道德性存在明显分歧。

data.title: Machine Code Isn't Scary
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了机器码并消除其神秘感。作者从学习高层次编程语言开始，逐渐克服对低层次编程的恐惧，特别是机器码。文章解释了机器码的基本概念，包括指令、寄存器和内存，并以ARM 64位架构为例，展示了如何理解和编写简单的机器码指令。机器码指令是32位数字，包含操作类型和参数。通过具体例子，如“添加立即数”指令，文章展示了如何操作这些二进制数。寄存器用于存储值，不同的处理器架构有不同的寄存器数量和命名规则。虽然手写二进制机器码繁琐，但理解其结构有助于消除对机器码的恐惧。文章最后提到，掌握JSON模式验证的人同样能理解和编写机器码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：机器代码编程及相关工具、教学和学习难度

不同观点：
• **flohofwoe** 认为，在Z80等处理器上进行机器代码编程时，理解操作码结构对模拟器开发很有帮助，但在实际编写机器代码时并不实用。他指出，在没有汇编器的情况下，通常使用查表法来查找指令和对应的机器码，并强调了手动管理地址和代码补丁的复杂性。

• **Lerc** 主张将汇编语言作为编程入门教学语言。他认为汇编指令本身简单易懂，但随着程序规模的扩大，管理这些指令变得繁琐且难以处理。他强调，学习汇编可以帮助理解高级编程语言的必要性，并解决编程中的基础问题。

• **shakna** 分享了自己在Aarch64和RISC-V上直接执行内存字节的编程经验，认为这种非优化的JIT方法比预期的要简单，打破了之前看到的复杂性传闻。

• **dedicate** 认为机器代码的“可怕”之处在于需要面对大量的十六进制或助记符，感觉需要特别的解码技巧才能理解。

• **amelius** 提到，过去机器代码的“可怕”在于系统出错时需要重启，但现在这种情况已经不再常见。

• **PlunderBunny** 讲述了自己在80年代学习BASIC并试图理解机器代码的经历，指出直到发现操作系统命令后，才开始理解如何将简单的操作组合成复杂的功能。

• **davemp** 推荐了capstone工具，认为其对处理条件字段等机器代码相关任务非常有用，提供了学习和理解机器代码的另一种途径。

• **jmclnx** 怀念DOS时代可以直接接近机器的体验，虽然未完全掌握机器语言，但觉得尝试的过程很有趣，并提到debug.com可以用来创建机器语言程序。

• **oleganza** 感谢文章的分享，并通过自身23年的计算机科学经验，强调了知识传递和理解的重要性，指出通过适当的讲解和交流可以帮助更多人获得启示和进步。

补充讨论：
• 机器代码编程的历史背景和工具演变，如DOS时代的debug.com和现代的capstone工具。
• 学习汇编语言的教学方法和其在编程教育中的潜在价值。
• 不同用户在面对机器代码时的个人体验和心理感受，如“可怕”的十六进制墙和系统重启问题。
• 强调知识分享和文档撰写在编程社区中的重要性，帮助更多人理解复杂的技术概念。

44177446.article_content:
Jimmy Miller
Machine Code Isn't Scary
The first programming language I ever learned was ActionScript. Writing code for Macromedia's Flash might be the furthest away from "bare metal" as you can possibly get. As I continued learning new languages, this starting heritage stuck with me. I was mostly interested in high-level, "web languages". Low-level languages felt impenetrable. Over time, I learned a bit more about them here and there, but for some reason, this notion stuck with me. Low-level things are scary, and machine code epitomized that most directly. When I Googled things asking about writing in "straight machine code", I was met with discouraging messages rather than learning.
Eventually, I decided I needed to overcome this barrier if I was going to achieve my goals. In doing so, I learned something I didn't expect.
Machine code isn't scary. If you can make sure your JSON conforms to a JSON schema, you can write machine code.
Which Machine Code?
One problem with machine code is that there isn't simply one standard. There are many different "instruction sets" depending on the processor. Most modern PCs use x86-64 machine code, but newer Macs, Raspberry Pis, and most mobile devices use ARM. There are other architectures out there, especially as you go back in time. The goal of this article won't be to give you a deep understanding of any particular instruction set, but instead, to give you enough information about how machine code typically works so you cannot be afraid of machine code. So we will start by having our examples be in ARM 64-bit (also written as aarch64). Once we have a decent understanding of that, we will talk a bit about x86-64.
Machine Code Basics
To understand the basics of machine code, you need three concepts:
Instructions
Registers
Memory
Instructions are exactly what they sound like; they are the code that will run. Machine code instructions are just numbers. In fact, in AArch64, every instruction is a 32-bit number. Instructions encode what operation the machine should run (add, move, subtract, jump, etc.) and accept some arguments for what data to operate on. These arguments might be constants (meaning like the number 2; these constants are often called "immediates"), but they can also be registers or a memory address. For now, just think of a register as a variable and memory as a list.
Arm Instructions
Here is an example of the instruction

Now this might look a bit confusing, but once you've seen these tables long enough, they start to be fairly straightforward. Each column in this table represents a single bit in a 32-bit number. If the value is a 0 or 1, that just means it is already filled in. If it has a label, it is a variable that needs to be filled in.
sf
tells us whether the registers we are going to use are 64-bit or 32-bit registers.
sh
stands for shift.
sh
goes in conjunction with imm12, which stands for a 12-bit immediate (constant). So if we want to add
42
to something, we would put

in for
imm12
and set sh to 0 (meaning we aren't shifting the number). But what if we want to represent a number larger than 12 bits? Well, the add instruction doesn't let us represent all such numbers; but setting sh to 1 lets us shift our number by 12 bits. So for example we can represent

by leaving our 42 alone and setting sh to 1. This is a clever technique for encoding larger numbers in a small space. Variables that start with R are registers, in this case, Rn is our argument to add, and Rd is our destination.
So the above instruction can be thought of like this:

Our add instruction is really just a data structure where we put the right parts in the right places.
Registers
Registers are small places to store values. Every instruction set will have a different number of these registers, different sizes of registers, different kinds of registers, and different naming conventions for registers. For AArch64, there are 31 general-purpose registers numbered X0 through X30 for 64-bit registers. Let's say we want to add 42 to register X0 and store the result in X1; we use this binary number.

Writing out all these binary numbers all the time (or even converting them to hex) can often be tedious. So instead, we usually talk about instructions in a simple text format

data.title: Nncp: Ad-hoc friend-to-friend delay-tolerant sneakernet-compatible darknet
data.author: gasull
data.article_summary: NNCP（Node to Node Copy）是一组简化安全存储转发文件、邮件和命令交换的工具，旨在帮助构建小型（几十个节点）的朋友对朋友（F2F）、静态路由、延迟容忍的暗网网络。它支持完整性检查、端到端加密、公钥认证和洋葱加密，每个节点同时作为客户端和服务器运行，支持推送和轮询模式，并支持多播区域。NNCP还支持离线传输、不同存储介质及空气隔离计算机，但也提供在线TCP守护进程。其优势在于简化、加密安全、兼容Sneakernet并易于与现有SMTP服务器集成，是基于GNU GPLv3的自由软件，适用于所有POSIX系统。

不同观点：
• [digdugdirk] 认为去中心化网络项目的设计决策很有趣，并询问是否有关于类似项目（如去中心化网格网络）的详细列表。他还关注内容中心网络的最新研究，认为这可能是此类项目的一个良好选择，显示出对技术方向的关注。

• [photonthug] 对项目的呈现形式提出质疑，最初不确定该项目的严肃性或时效性。尽管最终找到了一些更清晰的说明和发布日期，但认为这些内容更像博客而非正式参考资料，暗示项目的专业性或可信度可能存在问题。他还提到Hacker News（HN）社区可能对此类项目持批判态度，尤其是与自托管电子邮件相关的项目。

• [lexicality] 从个人情感和审美角度出发，表达了对“偷偷传递SD卡来传输文件”这种类似 sneakernet 项目的喜爱，但同时希望未来不会真的需要在日常生活中依赖这样的技术，反映出对技术浪漫化想象与实际应用困境之间的矛盾心理。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是去中心化网络项目的严肃性和专业性。部分用户（如photonthug）对其呈现和文档的质量表示怀疑，而其他用户（如digdugdirk）则更关注技术本身的可行性和研究进展。

44143767.article_summary: NNCP（Node to Node Copy）是一组简化安全存储转发文件、邮件和命令交换的工具，旨在帮助构建小型（几十个节点）的朋友对朋友（F2F）、静态路由、延迟容忍的暗网网络。它支持完整性检查、端到端加密、公钥认证和洋葱加密，每个节点同时作为客户端和服务器运行，支持推送和轮询模式，并支持多播区域。NNCP还支持离线传输、不同存储介质及空气隔离计算机，但也提供在线TCP守护进程。其优势在于简化、加密安全、兼容Sneakernet并易于与现有SMTP服务器集成，是基于GNU GPLv3的自由软件，适用于所有POSIX系统。

44177674.article_content:
Meta
announced
Tuesday morning that it was paying billions of dollars to keep an Illinois nuclear power plant running through 2047. The social media company will buy all the “clean energy attributes” of Constellation Energy’s Clinton Clean Energy Center, a 1.1 gigawatt nuclear power plant in central Illinois, starting in June 2027.
Electricity will still flow to the local grid, so Meta’s purchase won’t directly power one of its data centers, though the company does have one about two hours north of Clinton in DeKalb. Rather, the deal is a bit of carbon accounting to lower the company’s overall climate impact. It doesn’t reduce emissions on the grid, but prevents them from potentially increasing.
Neither company disclosed exact financial terms, but the multibillion-dollar deal will help Constellation relicense the plant and guarantee a customer for the duration of that license extension.
Big Tech companies — Meta included — have recently become vocal backers of the fission industry. Before the recent boom in data center construction, nuclear reactors had faced a grim future as cheap wind, solar, and natural gas undercut their power-generating costs. But the surge in AI and cloud computing has sent tech companies searching for power, which in turn has led to a
string of investments
in nuclear startups.
Meta and Constellation have alluded to the deal as a way to save the nuclear power plant from shutdown, though neither said it was at imminent risk of closure.
The power provider initially planned to shut down the Clinton reactor in
June 2017
as it faced stiff competition from cheap natural gas, but Illinois legislators stepped in
with subsidies
that encouraged Constellation to keep the lights on. Those subsidies are set to expire in 2027, and Constellation says the Meta deal will help prevent the closure.
But since 2017, Constellation has not threatened to shut down the Clinton power plant. Instead, in 2022, the company
said
it would apply to extend the reactor’s operating license through 2047.

TechCrunch has asked Constellation about its plans for the Clinton power plant before the Meta deal materialized, and we’ll update this article if we receive a reply. It’s likely that the company would have turned to ratepayers, something Constellation hints at in today’s
press release
: The deal with Meta “essentially replaces the ZEC [zero-emission credit] program and ensures long-term operations of the plant without ratepayer support.”
Meta and its Big Tech peers have fallen head over heels for nuclear power lately. Meta announced earlier this year that it was
soliciting proposals for new nuclear power plants
that would generate between 1 and 4 gigawatts of power. Today, the company said it has received over 50 qualified submissions for sites in more than 20 states.
With the Meta deal, Constellation has landed another Big Tech patron for its nuclear fleet. In September, the power provider said that it would
restart a reactor
at Three Mile Island after Microsoft agreed to buy all the resulting power.

Widespread dissatisfaction over the NIH’s “continuous free fall” has people speaking out.
Walker Bragman

Jay Bhattacharya’s stint as director of the National Institutes of Health is off to a rocky start. At his first town hall last month, the former Stanford University health economist, who became known during the early days of the COVID-19 pandemic for evangelizing mass infection as the path to herd immunity, was greeted by a largely stone-faced audience.
Things did not get much better from there. A joke in his opening remarks about the difficulty of the job turning his hair grayer did not land. Later, dozens
walked out
after he expressed support for the speculative lab leak explanation of COVID’s origins, which is disfavored by experts. During the Q&A session, he was heckled about cuts to research impacting minority communities.
”It’s good to have free speech,” Bhattacharya remarked during the walkout. “Welcome, you guys.”
But inside NIH, many are feeling unwelcome—and ready to be heard.
Important Context
spoke with a dozen people working at the agency in various roles and institutes, on both the intramural (internally funded) and extramural (grants) side. All painted a grim picture of an institution plagued by chaos, an unclear leadership structure, mismanagement, and widespread fear and demoralization due to capricious rule changes, restrictions, and research cuts.
One man they blamed? Jay Bhattacharya.
Like journalism that holds the oligarchy accountable?

to the
Accountability Journalism Institute
.

Due to clear personal and professional risks associated with whistleblowing and speaking out, we have kept the identities of these individuals anonymous, allowing each to decide how they are identified in this article. One staffer wished to be identified as a program officer and is quoted multiple times throughout this article. They are initially referred to as “a program officer” and subsequently as “the program officer.” A staffer who asked to be identified as extramural is also quoted in multiple places—first as “an extramural staffer,” then as “the extramural staffer.”
“It’s a total shit show,” one agency staffer told
Important Context
, explaining that Bhattacharya seemed unaware of how NIH operated when he arrived. They said he had been promising reforms that were already part of the agency’s work.
“His attitude coming in has just been so condescending, and so like, ‘Oh, we're going to make NIH great’…and ‘we're going to make…science transparent, and we're going to introduce all of these programs’ that, mind you, already exist,” the staffer said. “Like, these are things we actively do…You fired people that do those things that you say you want to do.”
Others we spoke to questioned Bhattacharya’s intentions, suggesting he had a dubious personal agenda. An extramural staffer described the current NIH leadership as “people settling grudges.” A scientist inside the agency said, “It’s very clear he has a vendetta against the NIH.”
Another NIH scientist told
Important Context
that Bhattacharya was “basically just trying to create an environment where lies can be treated the same as scientific truth and he and his cronies can like, jam through bullshit studies and then he can try to scream academic freedom.” They said that the way things were going, it looked like the NIH was “going to collapse on itself at some point,” adding that the current administration was “trying to kill most of what we do.”
“It is catastrophic,” they said. “The public should understand that [President Donald] Trump wants to kill U.S. science. And is succeeding.”
“It’s very clear he has a vendetta against the NIH.”
Prior to becoming NIH director, Bhattacharya had never worked in government or managed a large team. A professor and right-wing public health policy advocate, his nomination was seen by some of his allies as a sort of payback against his (and the president’s) perceived enemies. “Is this what winning looks like?” asked Bhattacharya’s longtime collaborator,
Jeffrey Tucker
, founder of the
anti-vaccine dark money group
the Brownstone Institute
, in a
blog post
.
